definition_zh: 罪犯；违法者；违规者；冒犯他人的人；惹人反感的人；（事故或问题的）罪魁祸首
definition_en: a person who commits a crime or breaks a rule, or who gives offence to others; also the thing chiefly responsible for a problem
core_image: 一个人抬脚跨过地上那道白线，鞋底已经落在禁止的一侧，身上还别着写有名字的牌子
scene: 小区业主会上，大家讨论那位总把垃圾倒进邻家院子的住户，一致认为他是破坏规矩的人。At the residents' meeting the neighbours agreed that the man who kept dumping rubbish over the fence was an offender.
sceneCN: 这里指「违反规矩、触犯他人的人」，对应第 1 个义项：实施了违法或违规行为的人；句意为业主会上邻居们认定那个反复往邻家院子倒垃圾的人就是破坏规矩者。画面要点：越过白线的脚、写有名字的牌子、倒在界外的垃圾。

pos.zh: 罪犯；违法者；违规者（可数，法律与日常通用）
冒犯者；惹人反感的人（由动词「触怒」加施事后缀而来）
罪魁祸首；主要祸源（可指事物，常用于环境、事故话题）

derivatives.zh: 去掉施事后缀后的动词原形，承拉丁 offendere「撞上、触犯」→ 由「撞到某物」转为「得罪人、违犯法度」
加名词后缀（源自拉丁语，表行为或状态）→ 由「触犯」这一动作转为「所犯之事、违法行为」
美式拼写，同样来自名词后缀（拉丁语中表状态的词尾） → 由动作转为「罪错、犯规」，并引申出「进攻」义
加形容词后缀（源自拉丁语，表倾向或性质）→ 由「触犯」转为「带有冒犯性的、令人不快的」
加否定前缀于 offensive → 由「会冒犯人」转为「不惹人反感的、无害的」

senses.title: A person who commits a crime
senses.definition: a person who has committed a crime, especially one identified in legal or police records
senses.definitionCN: 实施了犯罪行为的人，尤指被法律或警方记录在案者
senses.example: At the residents' meeting the neighbours agreed that the man who kept dumping rubbish over the fence was an offender.
senses.exampleCN: 业主会上，邻居们认定那个反复往邻家院子倒垃圾的人就是违法者。
senses.why: The Latin verb offendere meant 'to strike against' something, and -er names the one who does it; a criminal is literally the person who has struck against the line the law drew.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词 offendere 意为「撞上某物」，这个后缀指做出该动作的人；罪犯字面上就是撞到法律所画那道线的人。

senses.title: A person who breaks a rule, not a law
senses.titleCN: 违反规章而非法律的人
senses.definition: a person who contravenes the rules of an institution, sport or workplace without necessarily committing a crime
senses.definitionCN: 违反机构、运动或工作场所规章的人，未必构成犯罪
senses.example: A student who copies another's essay is an offender under the school's honesty code.
senses.exampleCN: 抄袭他人文章的学生，按学校诚信守则属于违规者。
senses.why: The line crossed need not be a statute; any drawn boundary, from a school code to a game's rules, produces an offender when someone steps over it.
senses.whyCN: 被越过的那条线不必是成文法；从校规到比赛规则，只要有人踩过任何画出的界线，就产生一个违规者。

senses.title: A person who gives offence by words
senses.definition: a person whose remarks or behaviour wound or insult someone
senses.definitionCN: 因言语或举止刺伤、侮辱他人而冒犯对方的人
senses.example: His jokes made him an offender in the eyes of the older guests.
senses.exampleCN: 他的玩笑使他在年长宾客眼中成了冒犯者。
senses.why: To offend was also to strike someone's feelings; the same -er suffix turns that blow into a person, so offence is no longer a line on the ground but a wound in another mind.
senses.whyCN: offend 也有「击伤他人感受」之义；同一个施事后缀把这一击落回到人身上，冒犯便从地上的线变成他人心里的伤。

senses.title: A person who disgusts or annoys
senses.definition: a person who is widely regarded as unpleasant or troublesome
senses.definitionCN: 被众人视为讨厌、惹麻烦的人
senses.example: In the office he was the offender whom nobody wanted to sit beside.
senses.exampleCN: 在办公室里，他是那个谁都不愿挨着坐的讨厌鬼。
senses.why: The physical core survives as social discomfort: the one who keeps bumping into other people's comfort is felt as an offender even when no rule is written.
senses.whyCN: 物理上的核心意象转为社交不适：总撞到别人舒适区的人，即使没有明文规定，也会被感觉成冒犯者。

senses.title: The chief source of a problem
senses.definition: the thing most responsible for a fault, a pollution or an accident
senses.definitionCN: 对某一缺陷、污染或事故负主要责任的事物
senses.example: Plastic packaging is the biggest offender in household waste.
senses.exampleCN: 塑料包装是生活垃圾中最大的祸源。
senses.why: Once the label applies to causes rather than persons, the guilty party can be a material; what 'strikes against' cleanliness takes the role of the offender.
senses.whyCN: 当这一标签从人转向原因，肇事者可以是某种材料；撞向洁净之物的东西便顶上了祸源的角色。

senses.title: A player who commits a foul
senses.definition: an athlete who commits an illegal move and is penalised by the referee
senses.definitionCN: 做出违规动作并被裁判处罚的运动员
senses.example: The referee sent the offender to the bench for two minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 裁判把犯规者罚到替补席上坐两分钟。
senses.why: A playing field is the clearest case of a line drawn on the ground, so the sports sense keeps the original picture almost unchanged.
senses.whyCN: 球场是最典型的「在地上画线」的场合，因此体育义几乎原封不动地保留了最初的画面。

senses.title: The person named in a charge
senses.titleCN: 指控文书中被点名的一方
senses.definition: the person identified in a legal charge before any finding of guilt
senses.definitionCN: 在尚未判定有罪之前，被法律指控文书点名的人
senses.example: The report names the alleged offender but protects the victim.
senses.exampleCN: 报道点出了被指控者，却保护了受害者的身份。
senses.why: Legal drafting needs a neutral noun for the party on the wrong side of the line; offender supplies it without yet asserting guilt.
senses.whyCN: 法律文书需要一个中性名词来称呼站在界线错侧的一方，offender 正好提供这一称呼，同时并不预先断定有罪。

senses.title: One who breaks a moral or sacred law
senses.titleCN: 违背道德或神圣律法的人
senses.definition: a person who transgresses a moral, religious or conscience-bound standard
senses.definitionCN: 违背道德、宗教或良心准则的人
senses.example: In the old sermon he was called an offender against heaven itself.
senses.exampleCN: 在那篇古老的布道中，他被称为连上天都敢触犯的人。
senses.why: The line can be drawn by God rather than by a state; the oldest use of offendere in religious writing already meant to stumble against a sacred order.
senses.whyCN: 这条线也可以由神明而非国家来画；offendere 在宗教文献里最早的用法本就指撞向神圣秩序而失足。

intro.en: Offender is English offend plus the agent suffix -er. Offend came through Old French from Latin offendere 'to strike against, stumble', a compound of ob- 'against' and a verb of striking. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: offender 是英语动词 offend 加施事后缀构成。offend 经古法语来自拉丁 offendere「撞上、失足」，由表「对着」的前缀与一个表「撞击」的动词复合而成。年代均为约数。

items.en: The prefix ob- meant 'toward, against, in the way of', and it marks the direction of a collision rather than its cause.
items.cn: 这个前缀意为「朝向、对着、挡在路上」，它标出撞击的方向，而非撞击的成因。

items.en: Offendere meant 'to strike against, hit, stumble', and by extension 'to commit a fault'; it was built from ob- plus a verb of striking.
items.cn: offendere 意为「撞上、击中、失足」，引申为「犯过错」；由一个表「对着」的前缀加一个表撞击的动词构成。

items.en: The participle offensa 'a striking against' supplied the noun for a fault, the ancestor of English offence and offense.
items.cn: 分词形式 offensa 意为「撞上」，提供表示过错的名词，是英语 offence 与 offense 的前身。

items.en: Old French took the verb as offendre and passed it to English in the fourteenth century with the sense 'to commit a sin or fault'.
items.cn: 古法语把该动词作 offendre 吸收，并于十四世纪传给英语，当时意为「犯下罪过或过失」。

items.en: Adding -er to the verb produced offender, first for a sinner before a court of law, then for any person who breaks a rule.
items.cn: 在动词后加施事后缀构成 offender，最初指在法庭上被审的罪人，后泛指任何破坏规则的人。

items.en: Nineteenth- and twentieth-century statutes fixed phrases such as repeat offender and young offender, while environmental writing extended the word to things.
items.cn: 十九、二十世纪的法条固定了「惯犯」「未成年犯」等说法，环境类写作又把该词扩展到事物身上。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin verb of striking and shows how far its family spread; the second group offers near alternatives for a person who does wrong.
note.cn: 第一组共享那个表「撞击」的拉丁动词，可见其词族分布之广；第二组是「做错事的人」的近义替代。

entries.definition: To break a law or to hurt someone's feelings; it is the verb from which the person-noun is built.
entries.definitionCN: 违反法律或伤害他人感情；它是派生人称名词所依托的动词。

entries.definition: The act of breaking a law or the feeling of being insulted; it names the deed, not the doer.
entries.definitionCN: 违法或冒犯的行为，也指被冒犯的感受；它指行为，不指行为人。

entries.definition: Causing resentment, or a military attack; the root idea of striking survives in both uses.
entries.definitionCN: 令人反感的，或指军事进攻；「撞击」的词根义在两种用法中都还在。

entries.definition: The party accused in a court case; it is built on defendere 'to ward off', the mirror image of striking against.
entries.definitionCN: 法庭上被指控的一方；由 defendere「挡开」构成，正是「撞上去」的镜像动作。

entries.definition: A person convicted of a crime; it states a legal category, while offender can merely name someone who broke a rule.
entries.definitionCN: 被判定有罪的人；它给出法律类别，而 offender 也可以只指破坏规则者。

entries.definition: The person responsible for a fault or mishap; it stresses blame rather than legal breach.
entries.definitionCN: 对过失或事故负有责任的人；它强调该受责怪，而非法律上的违犯。

entries.definition: A person who does something morally wrong; the judgement is ethical, not statutory.
entries.definitionCN: 做了道德上错事的人；其判断是伦理性的，而非法条性的。

entries.definition: A person who steps beyond a set limit or command; it keeps the image of crossing a line but sounds formal.
entries.definitionCN: 越过既定界限或命令的人；它保留「越过界线」的意象，但语体正式。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin verb, the real agent suffix and the real fixed phrases of law and sport.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁动词、真实的施事后缀，以及法律与体育中的真实固定搭配。

normal.en: Offendere is 'to strike against'; add -er and you have the one who strikes against the line.
normal.cn: offendere 意为「撞上去」；加上施事后缀就是那个撞向界线的人。

normal.en: The ob- in offend means 'against', the same direction seen in oppose and object.
normal.cn: offend 中那个表「对着」的前缀意为「对着」，与 oppose、object 中的方向感相同。

normal.en: Fixed phrases sort people by repetition: first-time offender, repeat offender, habitual offender.
normal.cn: 固定搭配按次数给人分类：初犯、屡犯、习惯性违法者。

normal.en: Offence is the deed, offender is the doer, offensive is the quality: one root, three jobs.
normal.cn: offence 是事，offender 是人，offensive 是性质：一个词根，三种职务。

normal.en: In sport the offender is simply the player who crossed the line the referee watches.
normal.cn: 在体育中，犯规者就是那个越过裁判所盯那条线的球员。

abstract.en: Picture a chalk line on a pavement and a shoe sole landing just past it, the dust still rising.
abstract.cn: 想象人行道上一条粉笔线，一只鞋底刚落到线外，尘土还未落下。

abstract.en: Picture a name tag pinned on a coat before the wearer has even entered the room.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚名牌在本人还没进屋之前就已别在了外套上。

abstract.en: Picture a broken fence with a single footprint on the forbidden side of the grass.
abstract.cn: 想象一段破损的栅栏，草地禁入的一侧只有一个脚印。

examples.en: The police recorded the offender's fingerprints and released him pending trial.
examples.cn: 警方录下该罪犯的指纹，随后在候审期间将其释放。

examples.en: Any offender caught smuggling will lose the licence for good.
examples.cn: 任何被查获走私的违法者都将永久失去执照。

examples.en: The report calls the city's ageing sewers the main offender in the flooding.
examples.cn: 报告称城中老化的下水道是此次内涝的主要祸源。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「哦，犯的」——哦，这事原来是他犯下的：跨过界线、犯下过错的那个人 → 罪犯、违规者

root: 拉丁语表「对着」的前缀 + 表撞击的词干 → offendere「撞上、失足、犯过」→ 古法语 offendre → 英语 offend；加表施事者的后缀 → offender，即「撞到界线上的那个人」；同族有 offence、offense、offensive、defendant。

sensesIntro.en: All eight senses start from one picture: a person stepping over a drawn line. The line may be a statute, a school code, someone's feelings, a game's rules, a charge sheet or a sacred order; whenever it is crossed, the one who crossed it is the offender.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都始于同一幅画面：一个人跨过画好的线。这条线可以是成文法、校规、他人的感受、比赛规则、指控文书或神圣秩序；只要有线被越过，越线者就是 offender。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person whose shoe has just landed on the forbidden side of a chalk line.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人的鞋底刚落在粉笔线外的那一侧。

branches.en: STATUTE: the line is a law, and the one who crosses it is a criminal in the eyes of the court.
branches.cn: 成文法：线是法律，越线者在法庭眼中即罪犯。

branches.en: RULES OF PLAY: school codes and referees' whistles draw thinner lines, yet crossing them still makes an offender.
branches.cn: 游戏规则：校规与裁判的哨声画出更细的线，越过它们同样成为违规者。

branches.en: SOCIAL WOUND: the line becomes another person's comfort, and the one who keeps bumping it is felt as offensive.
branches.cn: 社交伤害：线变成他人的舒适边界，反复撞上去的人便被视为冒犯者。

branches.en: BLAME SHIFTED: when the guilty party is a material or a practice, the word lends its blame to things.
branches.cn: 归责转移：当肇事者是材料或做法时，这个词把自己的责难借给了事物。

branches.en: FORMAL AND SACRED LABELS: legal drafting and religious language keep the noun for the party on the wrong side, before or beyond any trial.
branches.cn: 正式与神圣标签：法律文书与宗教语言把这个名词留给站在错侧的一方，无论审前还是超越审判。

intro.en: Offender is a transparent English build: a Latin verb of striking plus the agent suffix -er, with older relatives showing the same prefix at work.
intro.cn: offender 的构造清楚可拆：一个表「撞击」的拉丁动词，加上施事后缀；更早的同族词展示了同一前缀的作用。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family around offendere includes offensa, offensio and the verb itself; the prefix ob- also appears in object and oppose.
latinIntro.cn: offendere 周围的拉丁词族包括 offensa、offensio 与动词本身；这个前缀也见于 object 与 oppose。

items.example: The prefix turns a neutral motion into a collision.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把中性的移动变成了撞击。

items.meaning: to strike against; to commit a fault
items.example: Loud remarks may offend a listener.
items.exampleCN: 大声的评论可能冒犯听者。

items.meaning: a person or thing that performs the action
items.example: The suffix is added straight to the verb stem.
items.exampleCN: 该后缀直接加在动词词干之后。

items.meaning: a person who breaks a law or rule
items.example: The offender was charged the next morning.
items.exampleCN: 该违法者第二天早上被起诉。

items.meaning: several people who break the same line
items.example: Young offenders receive separate treatment.
items.exampleCN: 未成年犯会受到另行处理。

items.meaning: the act of breaking a law; a feeling of hurt
items.meaningCN: 违法行为；被冒犯的感受
items.example: Driving without a licence is an offence.
items.exampleCN: 无照驾驶是一项违法行为。

items.meaningCN: 引人反感的；用于进攻的
items.example: The poster used offensive language.
items.exampleCN: 那张海报用了冒犯性语言。

items.example: He kept the talk inoffensive.
items.exampleCN: 他让谈话保持在无害的范围。

items.example: The defendant denied the charge.
items.exampleCN: 被告否认了指控。

items.example: The team took a defensive stance.
items.exampleCN: 该队采取了防守姿态。

latinEntries.meaning: to strike against; to stumble; to commit a fault

definition_zh: 违反（法律、规则）；违背（协议、誓言）；侵犯（权利、隐私）；亵渎（圣地）；强暴；（体育）犯规；侵入（领地、领空）
definition_en: the act of breaking or acting against a law, a rule, an agreement, a right or something held sacred
core_image: 一道刷在地上的红线被人一脚踏过，线外立着写有禁止字样的木牌，脚印清晰地留在另一侧
scene: 环保督察在保护区里发现一片被砍倒的树木，当场按森林保护条例开出违法通知单。After finding the felled trees inside the reserve, the inspector issued a citation for violation of the forest code.
sceneCN: 这里指「对法规的违反」，对应第 1 个义项：以作为或不作为破坏法律规定的行为；句意为督察在保护区内发现被砍的树木后，依森林保护条例开出违法通知单。画面要点：红线、禁止木牌、留在另一侧的脚印。

pos.zh: 违反；违背；侵犯；亵渎（可数，常与 of 连用指出被破坏的对象）
（一次具体的）违法行为；违规事例（可数，警察与法庭文书常用）
（体育中的）犯规（可数，裁判用语）

derivatives.zh: 去掉名词后缀后的动词原形，回到拉丁 violare「以强力对待」→ 由「施加强力」转为「破坏、触犯」
violate 加施事后缀（源自拉丁语，表做某事的人）→ 由「违反」这一动作转为「违反者、侵害者」
violate 加形容词后缀（源自拉丁语，表倾向）→ 由「违反」转为「构成违反的、侵害性的」
加否定前缀与表「能够被……」的形容词后缀→ 由「可被侵犯」转为「不可侵犯的、神圣不可破的」
加否定前缀于拉丁分词 violatus → 由「已被破坏」转为「完好未损的、未被亵渎的」

senses.title: The breaking of a law
senses.definition: an act that breaks a statute or an ordinance, or the fact of breaking it
senses.definitionCN: 破坏成文法或法令的行为，或这种破坏本身
senses.example: After finding the felled trees inside the reserve, the inspector issued a notice for violation of the forest code.
senses.exampleCN: 在保护区内发现被砍的树木后，督察依森林保护条例开出违法通知。
senses.why: Latin violare meant to treat something with force, and a statute is treated with force when someone acts straight through it; the noun violation names that act of forcing past a legal line.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 violare 意为「以强力对待」，当有人径直穿过法条行事，就是对该法条施加强力；名词 violation 指这种强行越过法律界线的行为。

senses.title: The breach of a rule or regulation
senses.definition: the failure to obey a rule, code or administrative regulation that is not itself a criminal statute
senses.definitionCN: 未遵守某项规则、守则或行政条例，而该规则本身并非刑事法律
senses.example: Parking on the grass is a violation of the club's rules.
senses.exampleCN: 把车停在草地上违反了俱乐部的规定。
senses.why: The force need not be aimed at a state; a club, a school or an agency draws its own line, and forcing past it produces the same noun on a smaller scale.
senses.whyCN: 这股强力不必冲着国家而去；俱乐部、学校或机构也会自画界线，强行越过就在更小的尺度上产生同一个名词。

senses.title: The breaking of an agreement
senses.definition: the failure to honour a contract, treaty or promise that binds two parties
senses.definitionCN: 未履行约束双方的合同、条约或承诺
senses.example: The company was sued for violation of the supply contract.
senses.exampleCN: 该公司因违反供货合同而被起诉。
senses.why: A contract is a line two parties drew together; forcing through it is the same physical gesture, except the injured party is the partner rather than the state.
senses.whyCN: 合同是双方共同画下的一条线；强行穿过去是同一个动作，只是受损方由国家变成了合作方。

senses.title: The infringement of a right
senses.definition: an interference with someone's legal right, privacy or personal freedom
senses.definitionCN: 对他人法定权利、隐私或个人自由的干涉
senses.example: Reading her letters without permission was a violation of her privacy.
senses.exampleCN: 未经允许拆看她的信件侵犯了她的隐私。
senses.why: A right is a boundary drawn around a person; the force now presses into someone's own space, so the act is felt as invasion rather than mere non-compliance.
senses.whyCN: 权利是画在一个人周围的界线；此时强力压进的是某人自己的空间，于是这一行为被感受为侵入，而不只是不合规。

senses.title: The desecration of something sacred
senses.definition: the treatment of a sacred place, object or rite with irreverence or destructive force
senses.definitionCN: 以不敬或破坏性的强力对待圣地、圣物或仪式
senses.example: Digging up the burial ground was condemned as a violation of the dead.
senses.exampleCN: 挖掘那片墓地受到谴责，被视为对逝者的亵渎。
senses.why: The oldest lines were drawn by religion, and violare in Roman usage already covered the dishonouring of temples; the noun keeps that sacred sense alongside its legal one.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的界线由宗教画出，violare 在罗马用法中本就涵盖对神庙的污损；这个名词因此与法律义并行地保留了神圣义。

senses.title: Sexual assault, in formal and legal use
senses.titleCN: 正式与法律语境中的强暴
senses.definition: the crime of forcing sexual contact on a person against their will, phrased in formal or legal registers
senses.definitionCN: 违背他人意愿强行施加性接触的罪行，用于正式或法律语体
senses.example: The statute treats such a violation as a felony.
senses.exampleCN: 该法将此类强暴行为定为重罪。
senses.why: Here the force is literal and the boundary is the body itself; the word's core of pressing through a limit reaches its most concrete and most serious point.
senses.whyCN: 此处强力是字面意义上的，界线就是身体本身；这个词「压过界限」的核心义在此到达最具体也最严重的程度。

senses.title: A foul in sport
senses.definition: an illegal move in a game that breaks its written rules and is punished by an official
senses.definitionCN: 比赛中破坏成文规则、由裁判加以处罚的违规动作
senses.example: The referee whistled a violation before the shot was taken.
senses.exampleCN: 投篮之前裁判就吹了一次犯规。
senses.why: A court is a rectangle of painted lines, so the original picture returns almost literally: a body moves across a line that the game forbids it to cross.
senses.whyCN: 球场就是由画线围出的矩形，最初的画面几乎原样复现：一具身体越过了比赛禁止它越过的线。

senses.title: An unlawful entry into territory
senses.titleCN: 对领地或领空的非法进入
senses.definition: the entering of airspace, waters or land without permission, treated as a breach of sovereignty
senses.definitionCN: 未经许可进入领空、领水或陆地，被视为对主权的破坏
senses.example: The drone's flight over the base was a violation of national airspace.
senses.exampleCN: 无人机飞越基地上空侵犯了国家领空。
senses.why: When the line is a border on a map, pressing through it becomes trespass; the same noun covers the aircraft that crosses without leave.
senses.whyCN: 当那条线是地图上的国界，强行穿过去就成了侵入；同一个名词也覆盖未经许可越界的飞行器。

intro.en: Violation is the noun of action from Latin violare 'to treat with force, violate'. The further origin of violare is disputed: it is often linked with vis 'force', but that link is not settled, so it is reported here as uncertain. English took the word through French and directly from Latin. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: violation 是拉丁动词 violare「以强力对待、破坏」的动作名词。violare 更早的来源有争议：常被认为与 vis「力量」相关，但这一联系并未定论，故此处如实标注为存疑。英语经法语并直接从拉丁语吸收该词。年代均为约数。

items.en: Vis meant 'force, strength, violence'. Some accounts derive violare from it, but the derivation is contested and no single hypothesis is adopted here.
items.cn: vis 意为「力量、强度、暴力」。有说法认为 violare 由它派生，但此说存在争议，此处不选定论。

items.en: Violare is attested as 'to treat with force, to violate, to dishonour', used of laws, of women and of temples alike.
items.cn: violare 见于文献，意为「以强力对待、破坏、使蒙羞」，法律、人身与神庙都可作其对象。

items.en: Violatio, the noun of action, named the deed itself rather than the doer, and passed into the Romance languages.
items.cn: 动作名词 violatio 指行为本身而非行为人，并传入罗曼诸语。

items.en: The agent noun violator named the person who applies the force, an early sign that the family could name both deed and doer.
items.cn: 施事名词 violator 指施加强力的人，说明这一词族很早就能同时命名行为与行为人。

items.en: Old French carried the noun as violation in legal and religious texts, and its form, not the bare Latin stem, shaped the English spelling.
items.cn: 古法语在法律与宗教文本中沿用 violation 这一名词，英语的拼写形态来自它，而非裸露的拉丁词干。

items.en: English adopted violation for the breaking of a law, a oath or a sacred thing, and later extended it to rights, borders and games.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪吸收 violation，指对法律、誓言或神圣之物的破坏，后来又扩展到权利、边界与比赛。

note.en: The first group pairs two true relatives with two words that merely resemble the spelling; the second group offers near alternatives for the act of breaking a limit.
note.cn: 第一组把两个真正的同族词与两个只是拼写相似的词并列；第二组是「破坏界限」这一行为的近义替代。

entries.definition: To break a law, a right or something sacred; it is the verb that stands behind the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 破坏法律、权利或神圣之物；它是该名词背后的动词。

entries.definition: The person who breaks the law or the boundary; it names the agent where violation names the act.
entries.definitionCN: 破坏法律或界线的人；violation 指行为，它指行为人。

entries.definition: A small purple flower; it comes from Latin viola, the plant, and is only similar in spelling, not related in origin to violation.
entries.definitionCN: 一种紫色小花；出自拉丁语 viola（该植物），只是形近，与 violation 并非同源。

entries.definition: A stringed instrument; it comes through Italian from a medieval instrument name, and is only similar in sound, not related in origin.
entries.definitionCN: 一种弦乐器；经意大利语来自中古乐器名，只是读音形似，并非同源。

entries.definition: A breaking of a contract, duty or defence; it stresses the gap left behind, while violation stresses the force used.
entries.definitionCN: 对合同、义务或防线的破坏；它强调留下的缺口，而 violation 强调所用的强力。

entries.definition: An encroachment on a right, copyright or territory; it is the usual term in intellectual property, narrower than violation.
entries.definitionCN: 对权利、版权或领地的侵占；是知识产权领域的常用词，范围比 violation 窄。

entries.definition: A minor breach of a rule or law; it usually implies a small, punishable slip rather than a grave offence.
entries.definitionCN: 对规则或法律的轻微破坏；通常指可受处罚的小过失，而非严重罪行。

entries.definition: The act of treating a sacred place or object with contempt; it covers only the sacred branch of violation.
entries.definitionCN: 以轻蔑态度对待圣地或圣物的行为；只覆盖 violation 的神圣义分支。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin verb, the real action suffix and the real legal phrases that carry the word.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁动词、真实的动作名词后缀，以及承载该词的真实法律用语。

normal.en: Violare is 'to treat with force', so a violation is force applied where a limit should hold.
normal.cn: violare 意为「以强力对待」，所以 violation 就是在该有限制之处施加了强力。

normal.en: The suffix -tion turns the act of breaking into the thing broken: violate becomes violation.
normal.cn: 名词后缀把「破坏」的动作转为「所破坏之事」：violate 变成 violation。

normal.en: Legal phrases fix the object: traffic violation, violation of contract, violation of privacy.
normal.cn: 法律短语把对象固定下来：交通违规、违反合同、侵犯隐私。

normal.en: The agent is violator, the act is violation, the adjective is violative: three shapes of one stem.
normal.cn: 行为人是 violator，行为是 violation，形容词是 violative：同一词干的三种形态。

normal.en: A violation needs a line already drawn: no rule, no violation.
normal.cn: violation 需要一条早已画好的线：没有规则，就没有违反。

abstract.en: Picture a red line painted across a doorway and a heel landing beyond it in one stride.
abstract.cn: 想象门槛上刷着一道红线，一步之间鞋跟就落到了线外。

abstract.en: Picture a seal on a letter torn open from the wrong side, the wax split in two.
abstract.cn: 想象信封上的火漆印被人从内侧撕开，蜡一分为二。

abstract.en: Picture a rope around a temple door that someone has simply walked through, the rope still swinging.
abstract.cn: 想象神庙门前的绳子被人径直穿过，绳子还在晃。

examples.en: The factory was fined for repeated violations of the clean-air standards.
examples.cn: 这家工厂因多次违反清洁空气标准而被罚款。

examples.en: Sending her medical records to a third party was a clear violation of privacy.
examples.cn: 把她的病历发给第三方，明显侵犯了隐私。

examples.en: The umpire called a foot violation and awarded the point to the other side.
examples.cn: 裁判吹了脚部犯规，把这一分判给了对方。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「歪了，雷神」——把规矩歪着来，雷神都要劈下来：越线的举动 → 违反、违规

root: 拉丁 vis「力量」（与 violare 的联系存疑）→ violare「以强力对待、破坏」→ 动作名词 violatio → 古法语 violation → 英语 violation；名词后缀把「破坏」这一动作转为「所破坏之事」，同族有 violate、violator、inviolable。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses share one gesture: force applied across a limit. The limit may be a statute, a regulation, a contract, a right, a sacred place, a body, a touchline or a border; violation names the forcing through, and the register shifts with the object.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项共享同一个动作：把强力压过一道界限。这界限可以是成文法、条例、合同、权利、圣地、身体、边线或国界；violation 指强行穿过，语体则随对象而变化。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a foot crossing a painted red line, a forbidden sign standing on the other side.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只脚越过刷好的红线，另一侧立着禁止牌。

branches.en: LAW: the strongest line belongs to the state, and forcing past it produces the plain legal sense.
branches.cn: 法律：最强的线属于国家，强行越过它便产生最朴素的法律义。

branches.en: ADMINISTRATION: smaller authorities draw thinner lines, from parking rules to building codes.
branches.cn: 行政规管：较小的权威画出更细的线，从停车规定到建筑规范。

branches.en: CONTRACT: two parties draw the line together, so the breach injures a partner rather than the public.
branches.cn: 合同：线由双方共同画出，因此违反伤及的是合作方而非公众。

branches.en: THE PERSON AS BOUNDARY: privacy and the body are the innermost lines, and the force here becomes invasion.
branches.cn: 以人为界：隐私与身体是最内层的线，此处的强力便成了侵入。

branches.en: SACRED, PLAYFUL AND NATIONAL LINES: temples, touchlines and borders all repeat the same crossing under different guardians.
branches.cn: 神圣、竞技与国界之线：神庙、边线与国界，都在不同的守护者之下重复同一次越线。

intro.en: Violation is a Latin verb stem plus a Latin action suffix, and its family includes both agent nouns and negated adjectives.
intro.cn: violation 由一个拉丁动词词干加一个拉丁动作名词后缀构成，其词族既有施事名词，也有加否定成分的形容词。

latinIntro.en: Latin violare gave violatio and violator; adding the negative prefix in- yields the two adjectives inviolable and inviolate.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 violare 衍生出 violatio 与 violator；加否定前缀则得到 inviolable 与 inviolate 两个形容词。

items.meaning: force; the act of breaking through
items.example: The stem carries the idea of force from the start.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干从一开始就带着「强力」的意思。

items.structure: violare (Latin verb, to treat with force)
items.example: The Latin verb covered laws, persons and temples.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁动词的对象包括法律、人与神庙。

items.meaning: to break a law or a boundary
items.example: Drivers who violate the speed limit are fined.
items.exampleCN: 超速驾驶者会被罚款。

items.meaning: the act or instance of breaking a limit
items.meaningCN: 破坏界限的行为或事例
items.example: The violation was recorded on camera.
items.exampleCN: 这次违规被摄像头记录了下来。

items.example: Three violations were listed on the notice.
items.exampleCN: 通知上列出了三起违规。

items.example: The suffix turns a verb of action into a name for the deed.
items.exampleCN: 该后缀把动作动词变成对行为的称呼。

items.meaning: a person who breaks the limit
items.example: The violator refused to pay the fine.
items.exampleCN: 违规者拒绝缴纳罚款。

items.example: The clause was held violative of the treaty.
items.exampleCN: 该条款被裁定违反了条约。

items.meaning: able to be broken or profaned
items.example: Even a strong oath is violable.
items.exampleCN: 再强的誓言也可能被违背。

items.example: The border was declared inviolable.
items.exampleCN: 该边界被宣布为不可侵犯。

items.example: The shrine remained inviolate for centuries.
items.exampleCN: 那座神殿数百年间未遭亵渎。

latinEntries.meaning: to treat with force; to violate; to dishonour
latinEntries.meaningCN: 以强力对待；破坏；使蒙羞
已被破坏的；遭强力对待的

definition_zh: 违反（法律、规则）；违背（誓言、协议）；侵犯（权利、隐私）；亵渎（圣地）；强暴；扰乱（安宁）；擅自闯入（边境、领空）
definition_en: to break or act against a law, a promise, a right, a sacred place or a boundary, especially by force
core_image: 一个人抡拳砸在刻满誓约文字的石碑上，裂纹顺着字迹一路劈开，碎屑落进界线之内
scene: 半夜的居民区里，一支赶工的施工队无视禁鸣时段的公告，整夜开着搅拌机。The crew ignored the night-time noise ban and kept the mixers running all night, choosing to violate the order.
sceneCN: 这里指「违反明文规定」，对应第 1 个义项：以行动破坏法令或规章的约束；句意为施工队无视夜间禁鸣公告，整夜开动搅拌机，公然违反该规定。画面要点：砸裂的石碑、沿着字迹裂开的缝隙、越界的碎屑。

pos.zh: 违反；违背；侵犯；亵渎（及物动词，宾语为法律、协议、权利、圣地等）
强暴；侵害（人身）（法律与正式语体用语）
扰乱；打破（安宁、寂静等抽象状态）

derivatives.zh: 加名词后缀（源自拉丁语，表动作或结果）→ 由「违反」这一动作转为「所犯的违反之事、违规事例」
加施事后缀（源自拉丁语，表做某事的人）→ 由「违反」转为「违反者、侵害者」
加形容词后缀（源自拉丁语，表倾向或性质）→ 由「违反」转为「构成违反的、侵害性的」
加否定前缀与表「能够被……」的形容词后缀→ 由「可被侵犯」转为「不可侵犯的、不容破坏的」
加否定前缀于拉丁分词 violatus → 由「已被破坏」转为「完好无损的、未被亵渎的」

senses.title: To break a law or a rule
senses.definition: to act in a way that a statute, regulation or written rule forbids
senses.definitionCN: 以成文法、条例或书面规则所禁止的方式行事
senses.example: The crew ignored the night-time noise ban and kept the mixers running all night, choosing to violate the order.
senses.exampleCN: 施工队无视夜间禁鸣公告，整夜开动搅拌机，公然违反该规定。
senses.why: Latin violare meant to treat something with force; a written law is broken in the same physical way, by pushing straight through the limit it sets.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 violare 意为「以强力对待某物」；成文法律被破坏的方式同样具象，就是径直推过它设定的限度。

senses.title: To break a promise or an agreement
senses.definition: to fail to keep a vow, a contract or an undertaking that one has bound oneself to
senses.definitionCN: 未遵守自己受其约束的誓言、合同或承诺
senses.example: He violated his oath by telling the press what had been said in secret.
senses.exampleCN: 他把密室中的话告诉媒体，违背了自己的誓言。
senses.why: A promise is a line drawn by the speaker's own hand; breaking it is forcing through one's own boundary, which is why the word sounds harsher than plain failure.
senses.whyCN: 誓言是说话者亲手画下的线；违背它就是强行穿过自己设的界，因此这个词比「没做到」听起来严厉得多。

senses.title: To infringe a right or privacy
senses.definition: to interfere with someone's legal right, personal space or private information
senses.definitionCN: 干涉他人的法定权利、个人空间或私人信息
senses.example: Opening her letters without permission violates her privacy.
senses.exampleCN: 未经允许拆看她的信件侵犯了她的隐私。
senses.why: A right is a circle drawn around a person; the same force now presses inward, so violation is felt as invasion rather than disobedience.
senses.whyCN: 权利是画在一个人周围的圆圈；同一个强力此时向内挤压，因此 violation 被感受为侵入而非不服从。

senses.title: To desecrate something sacred
senses.definition: to treat a sacred place, object or rite with destructive irreverence
senses.definitionCN: 以破坏性的不敬态度对待圣地、圣物或仪式
senses.example: To build a car park there would violate the old burial ground.
senses.exampleCN: 在那里建停车场会亵渎那片古老墓地。
senses.why: The earliest limits were religious, and Roman violare already covered the dishonouring of temples; the sacred sense is the oldest branch of the word.
senses.whyCN: 最早的界限出自宗教，罗马语的 violare 本就涵盖污损神庙；神圣义是这个词语义树上最老的一枝。

senses.title: To rape or sexually assault
senses.definition: to force sexual contact on a person against their will, used in legal and formal registers
senses.definitionCN: 违背他人意愿强行施加性接触，用于法律与正式语体
senses.example: The court found that he had violated her.
senses.exampleCN: 法庭认定他对她实施了强暴。
senses.why: Here the limit is the body and the force is literal; the core image of pressing through a boundary reaches its most concrete and gravest use.
senses.whyCN: 此处界限就是身体，强力是字面意义上的；「压过界线」的核心意象在此到达最具体、最严重的用法。

senses.title: To disturb peace or silence
senses.definition: to break a state of quiet, order or calm that others rely on
senses.definitionCN: 打破他人所依赖的安静、秩序或平静状态
senses.example: A single shout violated the silence of the reading room.
senses.exampleCN: 一声喊叫打破了阅览室的寂静。
senses.why: The boundary can be intangible: silence is a fragile enclosure, and any loud act that tears it is treated as a violation of it.
senses.whyCN: 界限可以是非实体的：寂静是一层脆弱的围合，任何撕破它的喧响都被当作对这一状态的侵犯。

senses.title: To enter without permission
senses.definition: to enter a place, airspace or territory that one has no right to enter
senses.definitionCN: 进入自己无权进入的场所、领空或领土
senses.example: The plane violated the airspace of the neighbouring state.
senses.exampleCN: 那架飞机侵犯了邻国领空。
senses.why: When the line is drawn on a map, forcing through it becomes trespass; the aircraft or the walker is the moving body in the original picture.
senses.whyCN: 当线画在地图上，强行穿过去便成了侵入；飞机或行人就是最初画面里那个移动的身体。

senses.title: To act against a principle or a natural order
senses.definition: to go against a rule of reason, of nature or of good conduct that is not written down
senses.definitionCN: 违背未写成文字的道理、自然规律或行为准则
senses.example: Cutting a river's course that way violates every principle of hydrology.
senses.exampleCN: 那样截断河道违背了水利学的每一条原理。
senses.why: Even unwritten laws can be pictured as lines; once the mind has drawn one, an act that crosses it is called a violation by analogy with statute.
senses.whyCN: 即使不成文的法则也能被想象成线；一旦心里画出这条线，越过它的行为就依成文法的类比被称为违背。

intro.en: Violate came into English from the Latin past participle violatus, the participle of violare 'to treat with force, dishonour'. The deeper origin of violare is disputed: a link with vis 'force' is often suggested but not settled. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: violate 由拉丁过去分词 violatus 进入英语，该分词出自 violare「以强力对待、使蒙羞」。violare 更深一层的来源有争议：常有人提出它与 vis「力量」相关，但并无定论。年代均为约数。

items.en: Vis meant 'force, strength'. Some etymologists connect violare with it, but the derivation is disputed, so it is recorded here as uncertain.
items.cn: vis 意为「力量、强度」。有词源学者把 violare 与它联系起来，但该派生关系存在争议，此处如实记为存疑。

items.en: Violare is attested in laws and in poetry for 'to treat with force', 'to violate a law', 'to dishonour a temple or a person'.
items.cn: violare 见于法律与诗歌文本，意为「以强力对待」「破坏法律」「污损神庙或人身」。

items.en: The past participle violatus supplied the form English borrowed; the participle is the usual route by which Latin verbs enter English as -ate verbs.
items.cn: 过去分词 violatus 提供了英语借用的形态；拉丁动词常以分词形态进入英语，成为带该动词词尾的动词。

items.en: The action noun violatio named the deed, and it later gave English violation, the abstract partner of the verb.
items.cn: 动作名词 violatio 命名行为本身，后来为英语提供 violation，成为与该动词配套的抽象名词。

items.en: Middle English took the verb as violaten, meaning to break a law, a vow or a sacred thing.
items.cn: 中古英语以 violaten 的形式吸收该动词，意为破坏法律、誓言或神圣之物。

items.en: Later statutes and technical writing extended the verb to rights, privacy, airspace and even principles, fixing the wide range it now covers.
items.cn: 后来的法条与技术写作把该动词扩展到权利、隐私、领空乃至原理，确定了它今日覆盖的宽广范围。

note.en: The first group sets two true relatives beside two words that only look or sound alike; the second group gives near alternatives for the act of breaking a limit.
note.cn: 第一组把两个真正的同族词与两个只是形音相近的词并列；第二组是「破坏界限」这一动作的近义替代。

entries.definition: The act or instance of breaking a limit; it names the deed, while violate names the doing.
entries.definitionCN: 破坏界限的行为或事例；violate 指做这件事，它指做出来的事。

entries.definition: The person who breaks the law or the boundary; it shifts the focus from action to agent.
entries.definitionCN: 破坏法律或界线的人；它把焦点从动作转到行为人。

entries.definition: A purple flower; it comes from Latin viola, the plant, and is only similar in spelling, not related in origin to violate.
entries.definitionCN: 一种紫色花；出自拉丁语 viola（该植物），只是拼写相似，与 violate 并非同源。

entries.definition: Using great physical force; it is generally linked with the same force-word vis, though the exact tie to violate is not settled.
entries.definitionCN: 使用巨大身体力量的；一般被认为与同一个表力量的词 vis 有关，但与 violate 的确切联系尚未定论。

entries.definition: To break through or fail to observe a contract or duty; it pictures the gap left in a wall, not the blow struck.
entries.definitionCN: 突破或未遵守合同、义务；它想象的是墙上留下的缺口，而不是击出的那一拳。

entries.definition: To encroach on a right, a copyright or a limit; it is the standard verb in intellectual property and is narrower than violate.
entries.definitionCN: 侵占权利、版权或限度；是知识产权领域的标准动词，范围比 violate 窄。

entries.definition: To go beyond a limit or command; its Latin parts mean 'to step across', which makes the line-crossing image explicit.
entries.definitionCN: 越过限度或命令；其拉丁成分意为「跨过去」，把越线意象说得最明白。

entries.definition: To treat a sacred place or object with contempt; it covers only the sacred branch of violate.
entries.definitionCN: 以轻蔑态度对待圣地或圣物；只覆盖 violate 的神圣义分支。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin participle, the real derived family and the real objects this verb takes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁分词、真实的派生词族，以及这个动词真正搭配的对象。

normal.en: Violare is 'to treat with force', so to violate is to use force where a limit should stand.
normal.cn: violare 意为「以强力对待」，所以 violate 就是在该有限制之处使用了强力。

normal.en: The Latin participle violatus is why the English verb ends in -ate, like other borrowed verbs.
normal.cn: 拉丁分词 violatus 正是这个英语动词以该动词词尾收束的原因，与其他借入动词一样。

normal.en: The family splits by ending: -tion for the deed, -or for the doer, -ive for the quality.
normal.cn: 这个词族按词尾分工：名词后缀指事，施事后缀指人，形容词后缀指性质。

normal.en: Real objects make the meaning concrete: violate a law, a contract, privacy, a treaty.
normal.cn: 真实宾语让词义落地：违反法律、合同、隐私、条约。

normal.en: Silence, airspace and principles can all be violated: anything with an edge can be pushed through.
normal.cn: 寂静、领空与原理都可以被违背：凡有边界之物，都能被推穿。

abstract.en: Picture a fist hitting a stone tablet of vows until the carved letters split down the middle.
abstract.cn: 想象一拳砸在刻着誓言的石碑上，刻字从中间裂开。

abstract.en: Picture a foot pushing through a paper screen, the torn edge curling back on both sides.
abstract.cn: 想象一只脚捅穿纸屏，撕开的边缘向两侧卷起。

abstract.en: Picture someone stepping over a rope at a shrine, the rope still swinging behind the heel.
abstract.cn: 想象有人跨过神殿前的绳子，绳子在脚跟后面还在摆动。

examples.en: Any firm that violates the safety code loses its operating licence.
examples.cn: 任何违反安全规程的公司都会失去运营执照。

examples.en: The magazine was accused of violating the children's privacy.
examples.cn: 该杂志被指侵犯了这些孩子的隐私。

examples.en: Do not violate the silence of the chapel with a phone call.
examples.cn: 不要用一通电话打破小教堂的寂静。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「歪，累特」——把规矩歪着来，迟早累到自己：越过限度的动作 → 违反、侵犯

root: 拉丁 vis「力量」（与 violare 的联系存疑）→ violare「以强力对待、破坏」→ 过去分词 violatus → 英语 violate；同一词干加名词后缀得 violatio／violation，加施事后缀得 violator，加否定前缀得 inviolable、inviolate。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all perform one act: force applied across a limit. The limit ranges from a statute to a vow, a right, a temple, a body, a silence, a border and finally an unwritten principle; the verb stays the same while the object changes.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在做同一个动作：把强力压过一道界限。这界限从成文法到誓言、权利、神庙、身体、寂静、国界，最后到不成文的原理；宾语在变，动词不变。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a fist smashing a stone tablet of vows, the crack running along the carved words.
core.cn: 核心意象：一拳砸裂刻着誓约的石碑，裂缝沿刻字延伸。

branches.en: WRITTEN LAW: the state's line is the plainest object, and breaking it is the everyday sense of the verb.
branches.cn: 成文法：国家的线是最直白的对象，破坏它就是该动词最日常的义。

branches.en: SELF-BOUND PROMISE: the line is drawn by the speaker's own word, so the breach wounds trust as well as order.
branches.cn: 自我约束的承诺：线由说话者自己的话画出，违背既伤秩序也伤信任。

branches.en: INNER AND INTANGIBLE BOUNDARIES: privacy, rights and silence are enclosures around a person, pressed into rather than crossed.
branches.cn: 内在与非实体边界：隐私、权利与寂静是围住一个人的圈，是被压进去而非被跨过。

branches.en: SACRED AND BODILY LIMITS: temple and body carry the oldest and gravest force of the word.
branches.cn: 神圣与身体界限：神庙与身体承载着这个词最古老也最沉重的强力。

branches.en: MAPPED AND UNWRITTEN LINES: borders on a map and principles in the mind are crossed in the same manner.
branches.cn: 地图之线与心中之线：国界与原理都以同一种方式被越过。

intro.en: Violate is a Latin participle turned English verb; around it cluster an action noun, an agent noun and two negated adjectives.
intro.cn: violate 是拉丁分词转成的英语动词；它周围聚着一个动作名词、一个施事名词和两个加否定的形容词。

latinIntro.en: Latin violare yields the participle violatus and the nouns violatio and violator; in- negates the derived adjectives.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 violare 衍生出分词 violatus 与名词 violatio、violator；否定前缀则对派生形容词加以否定。

items.example: The stem is shared by the whole family of words.
items.exampleCN: 整个词族都共享这个词干。

items.meaning: to perform the action named by the stem
items.example: Many Latin borrowings enter English with this ending.
items.exampleCN: 许多拉丁借词以这个结尾进入英语。

items.meaning: to break a limit by force
items.example: They violate the rule at every checkpoint.
items.exampleCN: 他们在每个检查点都违反规定。

items.meaning: he, she or it breaks the limit
items.example: The new plant violates the emission cap.
items.exampleCN: 新厂违反了排放上限。

items.meaning: broke the limit; having been broken
items.meaningCN: 破坏了界限；已被破坏的
items.example: The treaty was violated twice.
items.exampleCN: 该条约被违反了两次。

items.meaning: breaking the limit while doing something
items.meaningCN: 在做某事的同时破坏界限
items.example: They were fined for violating the ban.
items.exampleCN: 他们因违反禁令被罚款。

items.meaning: the act or instance of breaking a limit
items.meaningCN: 破坏界限的行为或事例
items.example: The violation cost them the contract.
items.exampleCN: 这次违规让他们失去了合同。

items.example: The violator was named in the report.
items.exampleCN: 报告点名了违规者。

items.example: The practice was ruled violative of the code.
items.exampleCN: 该做法被裁定违反了守则。

items.meaning: not to be broken or profaned
items.example: They called the right inviolable.
items.exampleCN: 他们称这项权利不可侵犯。

items.example: The old walls stood inviolate.
items.exampleCN: 古老的城墙完好未损地立着。

latinEntries.meaning: to treat with force; to violate; to dishonour
latinEntries.meaningCN: 以强力对待；破坏；使蒙羞
已被破坏的；遭强力对待的

definition_zh: 处罚；罚款；刑罚；（体育）点球、罚球；罚杆；不利后果；代价
definition_en: a punishment or disadvantage imposed for breaking a rule, failing a standard, or gaining an unfair advantage
core_image: 裁判在记分牌上划掉犯规一方的一分，再让对方站到更有利的位置上
scene: 足球场上，后卫在禁区里从背后绊倒对方前锋，裁判指向点球点，并向犯规者出示黄牌。The referee awarded a penalty after the defender tripped the striker inside the box.
sceneCN: 这里指「体育比赛中因犯规而判给对方的一次罚球」，对应第 4 个义项：犯规之后由对方在固定位置主罚的一脚；句意为后卫在禁区内绊倒前锋后，裁判判给了点球。画面要点：禁区线、点球点、裁判手中的黄牌。

pos.zh: 处罚；罚款；刑罚（可数，常与 impose、pay、face 连用）
（体育）点球、罚球；罚杆（可数，足球、橄榄球、高尔夫常用）

derivatives.zh: 与 penalty 同出拉丁 poena，经形容词 poenalis 进入英语 → 由「那笔罚」转为形容「与刑罚有关的性质」
由 penal 加动词后缀（经法语与拉丁语，表「使……化」）→ 语义由「属于刑罚的」转为「施加处罚这一动作」
由 penalize 加名词后缀（源自拉丁语，表动作或结果）→ 由「施加处罚」转为「被处罚的过程或状态」
penalty 加复数后缀 → 由一次处罚转为多起、多类处罚
与 penalty 同出拉丁 poena，经动词 punire 加形容词后缀（源自拉丁语，表倾向）→ 由「罚金」转为「以惩罚为目的、带有惩罚性质的」

senses.title: A punishment for a breach
senses.titleCN: 因违反规则而受的处罚
senses.definition: a punishment imposed on a person or group that has broken a rule or failed a duty
senses.definitionCN: 对违反规则或未尽义务的个人与团体所施加的惩罚
senses.example: The league imposed a heavy penalty on the club for breaching the salary cap.
senses.exampleCN: 联盟因该俱乐部违反工资上限而对其处以重罚。
senses.why: Latin poena named the price exacted after a wrong, so the word begins as the consequence that follows a fault, not as the fault itself.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 poena 指犯错之后被索取的代价，所以这个词从一开始就是过错之后随之而来的后果，而不是过错本身。

senses.title: Money exacted for an offence
senses.titleCN: 为违法行为缴纳的钱款
senses.definition: a sum of money that an offender is required to pay to the authority that recorded the offence
senses.definitionCN: 违法者必须向记录该行为的机关缴纳的一笔钱
senses.example: Drivers face a penalty of two hundred pounds for using a phone at the wheel.
senses.exampleCN: 司机开车时使用手机，将面临两百英镑的罚款。
senses.why: Since poena also meant the compensation handed over to settle a wrong, the abstract consequence could be counted out in coins.
senses.whyCN: 因为 poena 也指为平息过错而交出的补偿，这种抽象的后果便可以用钱币数出来。

senses.title: A punishment fixed in statute
senses.definition: the punishment that a law prescribes for a particular offence, usually stated as a maximum
senses.definitionCN: 法律为某一具体罪行规定的惩罚，通常以最高刑期或最高数额表述
senses.example: The statute carries a maximum penalty of ten years in prison.
senses.exampleCN: 该法条规定的最高刑罚是十年监禁。
senses.why: When a community writes the price of a wrong into a code, the word shifts from the verdict spoken in court to the number printed in the law book.
senses.whyCN: 当共同体把过错的代价写进法典，这个词就从法庭上宣读的判决，转为法律文本里印着的那个数目。

senses.title: A free shot awarded for a foul
senses.titleCN: 因犯规而判给对方的罚球
senses.definition: an advantage given to the opposing side in a sport because the other side broke a rule
senses.definitionCN: 体育比赛中因一方犯规而判给另一方的有利机会
senses.example: The referee awarded a penalty after the defender tripped the striker inside the box.
senses.exampleCN: 后卫在禁区内绊倒前锋后，裁判判给了点球。
senses.why: Sport borrowed the legal word because a foul must be paid for; here the payment takes the form of an unopposed shot from a marked spot.
senses.whyCN: 体育借用了法律用词，因为犯规必须付出代价；在这里，代价的形式是在固定点上无人防守的一脚射门。

senses.title: A stroke added in golf
senses.titleCN: 高尔夫中被加罚的一杆
senses.definition: an extra stroke added to a player's score as a punishment for a mistake on the course
senses.definitionCN: 球场上因失误而被加进球员成绩里的一杆
senses.example: His ball found the water, so he took a penalty and dropped again.
senses.exampleCN: 他的球落进水里，于是他接受罚杆后重新抛球。
senses.why: Golf counts strokes instead of money, so paying for a mistake means adding a stroke to your own card.
senses.whyCN: 高尔夫数的是杆数而不是钱，所以为失误付出代价，就是在自己的记分卡上多加一杆。

senses.title: A charge for breaking a contract
senses.titleCN: 违反合同条款应付的违约金
senses.definition: an amount that a contract requires one party to pay if it acts in a way the agreement forbids
senses.definitionCN: 合同要求一方在做出协议禁止的行为时支付的款项
senses.example: Early repayment of the loan triggers a penalty of one month's interest.
senses.exampleCN: 提前偿还贷款会触发相当于一个月利息的违约金。
senses.why: A contract fixes in advance what a breach will cost, turning the older idea of compensation into a clause with a stated figure.
senses.whyCN: 合同事先定明违约要花多少钱，把较早的「补偿」观念变成一条写着具体数目的条款。

senses.title: The price of an advantage
senses.definition: a disadvantage that comes with a privilege or a success rather than with a rule broken
senses.definitionCN: 伴随特权或成功而来的不利之处，而不是因违规招致的
senses.example: Fame brought her the penalty of constant scrutiny.
senses.exampleCN: 名气给她带来了被人时刻审视的代价。
senses.why: If every gain carries a price, then even a privilege can carry a penalty, although no rule has been broken.
senses.whyCN: 如果每一种获得都带着价码，那么连特权也能带上「罚」，尽管并没有谁违规。

senses.title: A handicap laid on a contestant
senses.titleCN: 加在参赛者身上的不利条件
senses.definition: a disadvantage imposed on a competitor in order to equalize unequal starting points
senses.definitionCN: 为使不相等的起跑条件趋于平衡而加在某位参赛者身上的不利条件
senses.example: The older runners started with a time penalty.
senses.exampleCN: 年长的跑者带着时间上的不利条件起跑。
senses.why: Any contest that tries to balance unequal starting points can turn punishment into a handicap placed on the stronger side.
senses.whyCN: 凡是试图平衡起跑差距的比赛，都能把「罚」变成加在占优一方身上的不利条件。

intro.en: Penalty comes from Latin poena 'penalty, punishment, compensation', itself a loan from Greek poine 'price paid for a wrong'. Through Old French penalite it entered English law. Dates below are approximate.
intro.cn: penalty 出自拉丁语 poena「处罚、惩罚、补偿」，而 poena 又借自希腊语 poine「为过错付出的代价」；它经古法语 penalite 进入英语法律用语。以下年代均为约数。

items.en: Poine named the price that settled a wrong, whether blood-money paid to a family or a fine owed to a community.
items.cn: poine 指为平息过错而付出的价，既可以是赔给家族的偿命钱，也可以是交给共同体的罚金。

items.en: Poena kept both halves of that idea: the punishment itself and the sum handed over in compensation.
items.cn: poena 保留了这个观念的两半：处罚本身，以及作为补偿交出的那笔钱。

items.en: The adjective poenalis 'of punishment' produced English penal and later supplied the stem for penalize.
items.cn: 形容词 poenalis 意为「与处罚有关的」，它生成英语的 penal，后来又提供了 penalize 的词干。

items.en: Legal French used penalite for the punishment attached to an offence, and Middle English took the word in the fifteenth century.
items.cn: 法律法语用 penalite 指附在某一罪行上的处罚，中古英语在十五世纪吸收了这个词。

items.en: Penalty first named a punishment in law, then any sum exacted, then any disadvantage fixed by an agreement.
items.cn: penalty 最初指法律上的处罚，随后指任何被索取的钱款，再后来指协议定下的任何不利后果。

items.en: Nineteenth-century football rules turned the word into the name of the kick itself, and golf gave it the sense of an added stroke.
items.cn: 十九世纪的足球规则把这个词变成那脚罚球本身的名称，高尔夫又赋予它「加罚一杆」的意思。

note.en: The first group gathers words built on the same Latin stem plus one mere look-alike; the second group offers near alternatives for a punishment or a burden.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁词干的词，外加一个只是长得像的词；第二组是「处罚或负担」这一意思的近义替代。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning 'of punishment'; it describes the legal character of a measure, not the measure itself.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「刑罚的」的形容词；它描述一项措施的惩罚性质，而不指这项措施本身。

entries.definition: The verb built on penal; it names the act of imposing what a penalty names as a thing.
entries.definitionCN: 由 penal 构成的动词；penalty 指那件被施加的罚，这个动词则指施加的动作。

entries.definition: Formed from Latin punire rather than directly from poena; it stresses the intention to punish.
entries.definitionCN: 由拉丁动词 punire 而非直接由 poena 构成；它强调「意在惩罚」这一层。

entries.definition: A small room where food is kept; it merely looks like penalty in spelling and is not related to it in origin.
entries.definitionCN: 存放食物的小房间；只是拼写与 penalty 相似，并非同源。

entries.definition: A sum paid as punishment for an offence; it covers the money sense but not the sporting or contractual ones.
entries.definitionCN: 因违法而缴纳的一笔钱；它只覆盖金钱义，不覆盖体育与合同义。

entries.definition: A penalty applied by an authority to enforce a rule; broader in politics and diplomacy, narrower in sport.
entries.definitionCN: 权威为执行规则而施加的处罚；在政治与外交中范围更广，在体育中范围更窄。

entries.definition: Something lost by rule because of a fault; it stresses what is taken away rather than what is imposed.
entries.definitionCN: 因过错而按规则失去的东西；它强调被拿走的东西，而不是被施加的东西。

entries.definition: A disadvantage placed on a stronger competitor; it matches the sporting sense but carries no blame.
entries.definitionCN: 加在较强竞争者身上的不利条件；与体育义相合，但不含责备。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin stem, the real derived words and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁词干、真实的派生词与真实的固定搭配。

normal.en: Poena is the Latin word for the price of a wrong; a penalty is that price written down.
normal.cn: poena 是拉丁语中「过错的代价」，penalty 就是把这笔代价写下来。

normal.en: The same family runs through penal, penalize and punitive, all keeping the idea of a price to be paid.
normal.cn: 同一词族贯穿 penal、penalize 与 punitive，都保留「要付代价」这一层。

normal.en: Fixed phrases lock the senses: death penalty, penalty kick, penalty clause.
normal.cn: 固定搭配锁定义项：死刑、点球、违约金条款。

normal.en: A penalty is always owed to someone: a referee, a court or a contract.
normal.cn: 罚总是欠着某一方的：裁判、法庭或合同。

normal.en: If no rule was broken and nothing is owed, there is no penalty.
normal.cn: 若无人违规、无所亏欠，就谈不上罚。

abstract.en: Picture a coin box beside a rulebook, and every broken rule drops a coin in.
abstract.cn: 想象规则手册旁放着一只钱箱，每破一条规则就投进一枚硬币。

abstract.en: Picture a runner made to stand two steps behind the line because he started too early.
abstract.cn: 想象一名跑者因为抢跑，被要求站到起跑线后两步。

abstract.en: Picture a hill of trophies with a small toll gate at the foot, charging every winner.
abstract.cn: 想象一座由奖杯堆成的山，山脚设着一道小收费站，向每位赢家收费。

examples.en: The court added a penalty for the delay in reporting the accident.
examples.cn: 法院因事故报告延误而加判了一笔处罚。

examples.en: A penalty shoot-out decided the final.
examples.cn: 点球决胜决定了决赛的归属。

examples.en: There is a penalty for paying the loan back early.
examples.cn: 提前还贷是要付违约金的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「派人提」——你一犯规，就派人来提走一笔钱 → 罚款、处罚

root: 希腊 poine「为过错付出的价」→ 拉丁 poena「处罚、补偿」→ 拉丁形容词 poenalis → 古法语 penalite → 英语 penalty；同族词有 penal、penalize、punitive、punish。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses rest on one move: a wrong creates a debt, and the debt is collected. The collection may be a punishment, a sum of money, a statutory sentence, a shot at goal, a golf stroke, a contractual charge, the price of privilege, or a handicap in a race.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都立于同一个动作：过错生出一笔债，这笔债要被收回。收回的形式可以是一次处罚、一笔钱、一条法定刑、一脚罚球、一杆罚杆、一项合同收费、特权的代价，或比赛中的不利条件。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a referee striking one point off the offender's side and moving the other side forward.
core.cn: 核心意象：裁判从犯规一方的记分上划掉一分，再把另一方往前挪。

branches.en: LEGAL CONSEQUENCE: a fault creates a debt that a verdict or a statute collects in the form of punishment.
branches.cn: 法律后果：过错生出一笔债，由判决或法典以处罚的形式把它收回。

branches.en: MONEY FORM: the debt is counted in coins, from a fine owed to a public authority to a charge written into a contract.
branches.cn: 金钱形式：这笔债用钱币计算，从欠公共机关的一笔罚金到写进合同的一项收费。

branches.en: SPORTING FORM: the payment becomes an uncontested shot at goal or an extra stroke on the card.
branches.cn: 体育形式：这笔代价变成一脚无人防守的射门，或记分卡上多加的一杆。

branches.en: VOLUNTARY PRICE: a privilege or a success brings its own burden, although no rule was broken.
branches.cn: 自愿的代价：特权或成功自带负担，尽管并没有人违规。

branches.en: EQUALIZING BURDEN: a contest lays a disadvantage on the stronger side to level the start.
branches.cn: 平衡的负担：比赛把不利条件加在占优一方，使起跑趋于齐平。

intro.en: Penalty is a noun from the poena family; its Latin adjective and its related verb branch into several English words about punishment.
intro.cn: penalty 是 poena 词族中的名词；它的拉丁形容词与相关动词分出了若干与惩罚有关的英语词。

latinIntro.en: Latin poena and poenalis give penal, penalty and penalize, while Latin punire, built on poena, gives punish, punishment and punitive.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 poena 与 poenalis 生出 penal、penalty 与 penalize；由 poena 构成的拉丁 punire 则生出 punish、punishment 与 punitive。

items.example: The stem carries the idea of a debt owed after a fault.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干带着「犯错之后欠下一笔债」的意思。

items.example: The referee awarded a penalty.
items.exampleCN: 裁判判了一个点球。

items.example: The new law raised the penalties for dumping waste.
items.exampleCN: 新法提高了倾倒废弃物的处罚。

items.example: The country still keeps a penal code.
items.exampleCN: 该国仍然保留着一部刑法典。

items.example: The rules penalize late filing.
items.exampleCN: 规则对逾期提交予以处罚。

items.meaning: the act or state of being punished
items.example: He objected to the penalization of small firms.
items.exampleCN: 他反对对小企业施加处罚。

items.example: The measure was more punitive than preventive.
items.exampleCN: 这项措施更偏向惩罚，而非预防。

items.meaning: to make someone suffer for a wrong
items.example: The court punished the driver.
items.exampleCN: 法庭处罚了那名司机。

items.meaning: the suffering imposed for a wrong
items.meaningCN: 因过错而被施加的痛苦
items.example: The punishment was a month without pay.
items.exampleCN: 处罚是停薪一个月。

items.example: Such conduct is punishable by law.
items.exampleCN: 这种行为依法应受处罚。

latinEntries.meaning: to punish; to exact a penalty

definition_zh: 处罚；惩罚；处以罚款；扣分；判罚；使处于不利地位
definition_en: to impose a punishment or a disadvantage on someone because of a fault or an advantage they hold
core_image: 记分员在犯规者名字后面添上一笔扣减，把他刚挣来的领先一点点抹掉
scene: 赛季审查时，委员会发现一支车队在测试中用了超标的引擎，于是决定扣掉它上一站挣得的积分。The committee penalized the team by deducting the points it had won at the previous race.
sceneCN: 这里指「以扣分的方式处罚」，对应第 3 个义项：把已经获得的分数部分或全部扣除；句意为委员会因引擎违规而扣掉了该车队上一站赢得的积分。画面要点：审查报告、积分表、被划掉的那几行数字。

pos.zh: 处罚；使处于不利地位（及物动词，常与 for 连用说明原因）

collocations.zh: 使小企业处于不利地位
对提前还款收取违约金

derivatives.zh: 由 penalize 加名词后缀（源自拉丁语，表动作或结果）→ 由「施加处罚」转为「被处罚的过程或状态」
由 penalize 加过去分词后缀 → 由「施加处罚」转为形容「已经受罚的」
由 penalize 加现在分词后缀 → 由「施加处罚」转为形容「带有惩罚性质、正在造成不利的」
去掉动词后缀，回到形容词词干（拉丁 poenalis）→ 由「施加处罚的动作」回到「与刑罚有关的性质」
去掉动词后缀，换上名词后缀（经古法语与拉丁语，表性质）→ 由「施加处罚」转为「所施加的那份处罚」

senses.title: To punish under a rule
senses.titleCN: 依规则对违规者施加处罚
senses.definition: to impose a declared punishment on someone who has broken a rule
senses.definitionCN: 对违反规则的人施加事先声明的惩罚
senses.example: The referee penalized the forward for a deliberate handball.
senses.exampleCN: 裁判因前锋故意手球而判罚了他。
senses.why: The suffix -ize turns the noun of punishment into an action, so the word names the moment a rule is enforced against a person.
senses.whyCN: 动词后缀把「处罚」这个名词变成动作，于是这个词指的就是规则落到某人身上的那一刻。

senses.title: To impose a fine
senses.definition: to require an offender to pay a sum of money as the punishment
senses.definitionCN: 要求违规者缴纳一笔钱作为惩罚
senses.example: The city penalizes owners who fail to clear snow from the pavement.
senses.exampleCN: 市政府对未清除人行道积雪的业主处以罚款。
senses.why: Because the noun behind the verb could mean a sum of money, the action can be carried out with a receipt and a payment deadline.
senses.whyCN: 因为动词背后的名词本就可以指一笔钱，所以这个动作可以用一张收据和一个缴款期限来完成。

senses.title: To strip points or a result
senses.titleCN: 扣除已获得的分数或成绩
senses.definition: to deduct points, a win or a record that someone has already gained
senses.definitionCN: 把某人已经取得的分数、胜场或纪录扣除
senses.example: The committee penalized the team by deducting the points it had won at the previous race.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会扣掉了该车队上一站赢得的积分，以示处罚。
senses.why: When the punishment is counted in points rather than money, the same verb simply takes away what the scoreboard already holds.
senses.whyCN: 当惩罚以分数而不是钱来计算，同一个动词所做的就是拿走记分牌上已有的东西。

senses.title: To handicap a player in sport
senses.titleCN: 在比赛中判罚或加罚某位选手
senses.definition: to place a sporting disadvantage on a player or team for an infringement
senses.definitionCN: 因违规而把某项体育上的不利加给选手或球队
senses.example: Golfers are penalized two strokes when the ball goes out of bounds.
senses.exampleCN: 球出界时，高尔夫球手会被加罚两杆。
senses.why: The penalty in sport is not paid to anyone; it is carried by the offender, so the verb shifts from collecting a debt to loading a burden.
senses.whyCN: 体育中的罚并不是付给谁的，而是由犯规者自己背着；于是这个动词从「收取代价」转为「给身上加负担」。

senses.title: To make a group bear a cost
senses.titleCN: 让某一群体承担额外成本
senses.definition: to arrange rules or charges so that a particular group carries a heavier burden
senses.definitionCN: 使规则或收费安排让某一群体承担更重的负担
senses.example: The tax penalizes families with a single earner.
senses.exampleCN: 这项税使单收入家庭处于不利地位。
senses.why: Once the verb means 'load a burden on', no offence is needed: a policy itself can penalize by loading one group more heavily than another.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个动词意为「给身上加负担」，就不需要有人违规：一项政策只要让某一群体背得更重，就已经在「罚」它了。

senses.title: To forbid by attaching a sanction
senses.titleCN: 以处罚为后盾禁止某种行为
senses.definition: to attach a legal sanction to a practice so that those who repeat it are punished
senses.definitionCN: 为某种行为附加法律制裁，使继续做的人受到惩罚
senses.example: The new code penalizes the dumping of waste in rivers.
senses.exampleCN: 新法典对向河流倾倒废弃物的行为规定了处罚。
senses.why: A law that threatens punishment is written in the same verb: the action is not yet punished, but the sanction already stands behind the ban.
senses.whyCN: 一条以惩罚相威胁的法律也用同一个动词来写：行为尚未受罚，但制裁已经立在禁令背后。

senses.title: To punish a group for one member's act
senses.titleCN: 因一人之过而连带处罚整组人
senses.definition: to make several people suffer for the fault of a single member among them
senses.definitionCN: 因群体中某一个人的过错而让多个人一起承担后果
senses.example: The coach penalized the whole squad for one player's lateness.
senses.exampleCN: 教练因一名球员迟到而处罚了整支队伍。
senses.why: If punishment can be assigned by rule rather than by blame, it can also be spread across a group, whether or not each member took part.
senses.whyCN: 如果处罚可以按规则指派而不必按罪责指派，它也能摊到一整组人身上，无论每个人是否参与。

senses.title: To treat unfairly through a built-in bias
senses.titleCN: 因规则自带的偏见而使人吃亏
senses.definition: to place a particular kind of person at a disadvantage through rules that do not name them openly
senses.definitionCN: 通过并未明指某类人的规则，使这类人处于劣势
senses.example: The old rules penalized women who took career breaks.
senses.exampleCN: 旧规则使中断职业发展的女性吃亏。
senses.why: A burden can fall on a whole category of people without any fault at all, and at that point the verb shades into unfair treatment.
senses.whyCN: 负担可以毫无过错地落在整整一类人身上，到了这一步，这个动词就带上「不公平对待」的色彩。

intro.en: Penalize is an English construction rather than a Latin inheritance: the adjective penal, from Latin poenalis, plus the verb suffix -ize. It appeared in the nineteenth century, when English began to form verbs freely from adjectives. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: penalize 是英语自身的构造，而不是直接承自拉丁：它由拉丁 poenalis 而来的形容词 penal 加动词后缀构成，出现于十九世纪，正值英语开始大量由形容词造动词的时期。年代均为约数。

items.en: Poena named punishment and the compensation that settled a wrong, and it is the ultimate source of the whole family.
items.cn: poena 指处罚以及为平息过错而付的补偿，是整个词族的最初源头。

items.en: The adjective poenalis 'of punishment' passed through French as penal into English, keeping the descriptive sense.
items.cn: 形容词 poenalis 意为「与处罚有关的」，经法语作 penal 进入英语，保留了描述性质的意思。

items.en: English penal described laws, codes and systems of punishment, so the stem was ready to take an action suffix.
items.cn: 英语的 penal 用来描述法律、法典与惩罚体系，这个词干已经准备好接上一个表动作的后缀。

items.en: The suffix -ize, from French -iser and Latin -izare, turns an adjective into a verb meaning 'to make or to act in that way'.
items.cn: 动词后缀经法语与拉丁语而来，把形容词变成意为「使之成为或按此行事」的动词。

items.en: The verb is first recorded in the nineteenth century, when rules, taxes and games all needed a word for the act of laying a penalty on someone.
items.cn: 这个动词首见于十九世纪，当时规则、税制与比赛都需要一个词来指「把处罚加到某人身上」这一动作。

items.en: Twentieth-century usage widened it from legal punishment to any rule, fee or bias that leaves one side worse off.
items.cn: 二十世纪的用法把它从法律惩罚扩展到任何使某一方更吃亏的规则、收费或偏见。

note.en: The first group holds the same Latin stem and one mere look-alike; the second group offers near alternatives for the act of imposing a burden.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁词干的词，外加一个只是长得像的词；第二组是「施加负担」这一动作的近义替代。

entries.definition: The adjective from which the verb is built; it names the character of a measure rather than the act of applying it.
entries.definitionCN: 动词所由构成的形容词；它指一项措施的性质，而不是施加这一动作。

entries.definition: The noun naming what is imposed; the verb names the imposing, so the pair look alike but differ in grammatical role.
entries.definitionCN: 指被施加之物的名词；动词则指施加动作，两者形近而语法角色不同。

entries.definition: An adjective from Latin punire meaning 'intended to punish'; it describes purpose, not the act of applying a rule.
entries.definitionCN: 由拉丁 punire 而来的形容词，意为「意在惩罚的」；它描述目的，而不描述执行规则的动作。

entries.definition: A flat board or a group of experts; it merely looks like penalize in spelling and is not related to it in origin.
entries.definitionCN: 一块平板或一组专家；只是拼写与 penalize 相似，并非同源。

entries.definition: To make someone suffer for a wrong; it stresses the pain inflicted, while penalize stresses the rule or the disadvantage.
entries.definitionCN: 因过错而使人受苦；它强调施加的痛苦，而 penalize 强调规则或不利处境。

entries.definition: To correct behaviour by training or punishment; it carries the aim of reform, which penalize does not require.
entries.definitionCN: 以训练或惩罚纠正行为；它带着「改正」的目的，而 penalize 并不要求这一点。

entries.definition: To charge a sum of money as punishment; it covers one sense of penalize and nothing more.
entries.definitionCN: 以收取一笔钱作为处罚；它只覆盖 penalize 的一个义项，别无其他。

entries.definition: To put someone in a worse position; it captures the burden sense but leaves out the rule and the fault.
entries.definitionCN: 使某人处于更差的位置；它抓住「负担」这一层，却不含规则与过错。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin stem, the real adjective it comes from and the real related nouns.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁词干、构成它的真实形容词，以及真实的同族名词。

normal.en: Penalize is penal plus -ize, so it means 'to make penal', to turn a rule into an actual burden.
normal.cn: penalize 是 penal 加动词后缀，意思是「使带有惩罚」，把一条规则变成真实的负担。

normal.en: Everything in this family goes back to poena, the Latin price of a wrong.
normal.cn: 这一词族里的一切都可上溯到 poena，即拉丁语中「过错的代价」。

normal.en: Penalize usually names who suffers and why: penalize a team for cheating, penalize drivers for speeding.
normal.cn: penalize 通常点明谁受损与为何受损：因作弊处罚球队，因超速处罚司机。

normal.en: Pair it with its noun to feel the difference: the noun names what is imposed, the verb names who is made to carry it.
normal.cn: 把它与同族名词配对来体会差别：名词说的是被施加的那项处罚，动词说的是让谁去承担这项处罚。

normal.en: No fault is needed in the modern sense; a tax or a deadline can penalize you simply by costing you more.
normal.cn: 现代义里不必有人犯错；一项税或一个截止期限，只要让你多付，就已经在「罚」你。

abstract.en: Picture a hand pressing down on one side of a balance while the other side rises.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手把天平的一端往下按，另一端就翘了起来。

abstract.en: Picture a scoreboard where a small eraser rubs out two lines the moment a whistle blows.
abstract.cn: 想象哨声一响，一块小橡皮就在记分牌上擦掉两行数字。

abstract.en: Picture a runner carrying a sandbag that nobody else in the race was given.
abstract.cn: 想象一名跑者背着一只沙袋，而赛道上其他人都没有分到。

examples.en: The board penalized the firm for filing a false report.
examples.cn: 董事会因该公司的虚假报告而对其作出处罚。

examples.en: Rules that penalize part-time students keep many adults out of college.
examples.cn: 使非全日制学生吃亏的规则，把许多成年人挡在大学门外。

examples.en: He was penalized ten seconds for blocking another skier.
examples.cn: 他因阻挡另一名滑雪者而被加罚十秒。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「劈了来宰」——一刀劈下去再宰一刀，违规者被一层层扣罚 → 处罚、扣分

root: 拉丁 poena「处罚、补偿」→ 拉丁形容词 poenalis → 法语 penal → 英语形容词 penal → 加动词后缀 → penalize「把处罚加到某人身上」；同族词有 penalty、punish、punitive。

sensesIntro.en: All eight senses are one act seen from different angles: a burden is placed on someone. The burden may follow a broken rule, take the shape of money, remove points, handicap a player, fall on a group, stand behind a ban, cover a whole squad, or follow from a rule's hidden bias.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项是同一个动作的不同侧面：把一份负担加到某人身上。这份负担可以因违规而来、以钱的形式出现、扣走分数、加在选手身上、落到某个群体、立在禁令背后、摊到整支队伍，或来自规则里隐藏的偏见。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a scorer adding a deduction behind an offender's name and rubbing out the lead just earned.
core.cn: 核心意象：记分员在犯规者的名字后面添上一笔扣减，把刚挣来的领先擦掉。

branches.en: ENFORCEMENT: the rule is applied to a person, either as a declared punishment or as a sum of money.
branches.cn: 执行：规则落到具体的人身上，或表现为声明的处罚，或表现为一笔钱。

branches.en: SCORE AND SPORT: what was already gained is taken away, or a stroke is added on the field.
branches.cn: 分数与赛场：已经拿到的东西被拿走，或在场上多加一杆。

branches.en: STRUCTURAL COST: rules and charges can load one group more heavily without any offence.
branches.cn: 结构性成本：规则与收费可以不经任何过错，就把某一群体压得更重。

branches.en: SANCTION ATTACHED: a ban is written with its punishment already standing behind it.
branches.cn: 附加制裁：一条禁令在写下的同时，惩罚已经立在它背后。

branches.en: SPREAD AND BIAS: the burden reaches a whole squad, or quietly falls on a category of people.
branches.cn: 扩散与偏见：负担扩到整支队伍，或悄然落在某一类人身上。

intro.en: Penalize is a transparent English build: a Latin-derived adjective plus a verb suffix, with the Latin noun still visible underneath.
intro.cn: penalize 是构造透明的英语词：一个源自拉丁的形容词加一个动词后缀，底下的拉丁名词仍清晰可见。

latinIntro.en: The Latin noun poena and its adjective poenalis sit under penal, penalty and penalize, while the Latin verb punire underlies punish and punitive.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁名词 poena 及其形容词 poenalis 位于 penal、penalty 与 penalize 之下，而拉丁动词 punire 则位于 punish 与 punitive 之下。

items.example: The stem is hidden but still present in the word.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干虽被遮住，却仍在词里。

items.example: The penal system was under review.
items.exampleCN: 惩罚体系正在接受审查。

items.meaning: to make or to act in the stated way
items.meaningCN: 使成为或按所说的方式行事
items.example: The suffix turns adjectives into verbs.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把形容词变成动词。

items.example: The code penalizes late payment.
items.exampleCN: 法规对逾期付款予以处罚。

items.example: The penalized firms appealed.
items.exampleCN: 受罚的公司提出了申诉。

items.example: A penalizing tariff hurt consumers.
items.exampleCN: 一项惩罚性关税伤害了消费者。

items.example: The penalization of whistle-blowers drew criticism.
items.exampleCN: 对举报人的处罚引来批评。

items.example: The penalty was doubled on appeal.
items.exampleCN: 上诉后处罚被加倍。

items.structure: Latin punire through Old French punir
items.meaning: to make suffer for a wrong
items.example: They punish cheating severely.
items.exampleCN: 他们对作弊处罚很重。

items.example: Punitive damages were awarded.
items.exampleCN: 法院判给了惩罚性赔偿。

definition_zh: 惩罚；处罚；严厉对待；粗暴使用使损坏；重创（对手）；猛烈抨击；使身体极度疲惫
definition_en: to make someone suffer for a wrong, or to treat a person or thing so harshly that it is worn down
core_image: 木槌落下，犯错的人被带离座位，去承受自己招来的那阵疼痛
scene: 夜间巡查时，看守发现一名囚犯试图翻墙逃走，于是把他单独关进一间没有窗的小屋。The warden punished the prisoner by locking him alone in a windowless cell.
sceneCN: 这里指「因过错而使某人受苦」，对应第 1 个义项：让犯错者为自己的行为承担痛苦；句意为看守把企图逃跑的囚犯单独关进没有窗的小屋作为惩罚。画面要点：夜间走廊、翻墙的脚印、被关上的铁门。

pos.zh: 惩罚；处罚（及物动词，常与 for 连用说明过错）
严厉对待；粗暴使用使损坏（口语中可指物）

forms.label: 现在分词作形容词（折磨人的）

derivatives.zh: 由 punish 加名词后缀（源自拉丁语，表动作结果）→ 由「使人受苦这一动作」转为「所施加的那份痛苦或处罚」
由 punish 加形容词后缀（源自拉丁语，表能够被）→ 由「施加惩罚」转为「依法可以受罚的」
由 punish 加现在分词后缀 → 由「惩罚他人」转为形容「像惩罚一样消耗人的、折磨人的」
由 punish 加施事后缀（表施动者）→ 由「惩罚」这一动作转为「施加惩罚的那个人」
与 punish 同出拉丁 punire，加形容词后缀（源自拉丁语，表倾向）→ 由「施加惩罚」转为「以惩罚为目的的、惩罚性的」
与 punish 同出拉丁 poena，经古法语形成名词 → 由「惩罚这一动作」转为「作为惩罚所付的那笔代价」

senses.title: To make someone suffer for a wrong
senses.definition: to cause a person who has done wrong to undergo pain, loss or hardship
senses.definitionCN: 使做错事的人经历痛苦、损失或艰难
senses.example: The company punished the clerk for leaking the file.
senses.exampleCN: 公司因那名职员泄露文件而惩罚了他。
senses.why: Latin punire meant to make someone pay for a wrong, so the core idea is not pain for its own sake but a debt being settled through suffering.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 punire 意为让某人为过错付出代价，所以核心并不是疼痛本身，而是一笔债通过受苦被结清。

senses.title: To sentence in a court
senses.definition: to impose a legal sentence on a convicted person
senses.definitionCN: 对已被定罪的人施加法律判决
senses.example: The court punished the fraud with five years in prison.
senses.exampleCN: 法庭判处那名诈骗犯五年监禁。
senses.why: When the debt is collected by a court, the suffering is fixed by law, given a name and given a term.
senses.whyCN: 当这笔债由法庭来收取，痛苦就由法律确定，被赋予名称，也被赋予期限。

senses.title: To discipline a child or pupil
senses.definition: to correct a child or pupil by withdrawing something valued or by mild suffering
senses.definitionCN: 以收回孩子看重的某物或轻微的苦头来纠正其行为
senses.example: His parents punished him by cancelling the trip.
senses.exampleCN: 他父母取消旅行作为对他的惩罚。
senses.why: A household collects the same debt in miniature: a small wrong, a small withdrawal of what the child values.
senses.whyCN: 家庭以缩小的尺度收取同一笔债：小小的过错，配上小小地拿走孩子看重的东西。

senses.title: To treat someone with deliberate harshness
senses.titleCN: 刻意以严酷手段对待某人
senses.definition: to subject a person to prolonged harsh treatment, whether or not a rule was broken
senses.definitionCN: 使某人长时间承受严酷对待，不论是否真的违规
senses.example: The guards punished the prisoners by keeping them standing all night.
senses.exampleCN: 看守让囚犯整夜站立，以此折磨他们。
senses.why: Once pain is separated from the debt, any deliberate infliction of suffering can take the name, even where no rule exists to be broken.
senses.whyCN: 一旦疼痛与那笔债脱钩，任何刻意施加的痛苦都能叫这个名字，哪怕并不存在可供违反的规则。

senses.title: To damage something by rough use
senses.titleCN: 因粗暴使用而损坏某物
senses.definition: to wear out or damage an object by using it far harder than it was designed for
senses.definitionCN: 以远超设计承受的方式使用，使物品磨损或损坏
senses.example: Rough roads punish the tyres far more than smooth ones.
senses.exampleCN: 崎岖路面比平坦路面更伤轮胎。
senses.why: Objects cannot owe a debt, so the word transfers to rough treatment that makes a thing suffer wear, as if the thing were being made to pay.
senses.whyCN: 物品不可能欠债，于是这个词转到「粗暴对待使某物受损」上，仿佛那件东西也在被逼着付出代价。

senses.title: To defeat an opponent by a wide margin
senses.titleCN: 以压倒性优势重创对手
senses.definition: to beat an opponent so heavily that the defeat feels like a penalty
senses.definitionCN: 以极大差距击败对手，使这场失败如同一种惩罚
senses.example: The champions punished the visitors with four goals in twenty minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 冠军队在二十分钟内连进四球，重创了客队。
senses.why: A contest can turn a score into a debt, and a heavy defeat is that debt being collected all at once.
senses.whyCN: 比赛可以把比分变成一笔债，而一场惨败就是这笔债被一次性收走。

senses.title: To criticise sharply
senses.definition: to attack a person, work or idea with very severe public criticism
senses.definitionCN: 以极严厉的公开批评攻击某人、某作品或某观点
senses.example: The critics punished the film for its empty spectacle.
senses.exampleCN: 影评人猛烈抨击这部影片空洞的视觉堆砌。
senses.why: Words can inflict suffering too, so sharp criticism borrows the same verb and makes its target pay in reputation.
senses.whyCN: 言语也能造成痛苦，于是尖锐的批评借用了同一个动词，让对象以名声偿付。

senses.title: To exhaust the body through effort
senses.titleCN: 使身体因用力而极度疲惫
senses.definition: to strain the body so hard that the effort feels like a punishment
senses.definitionCN: 使身体承担极大负荷，让这种用力如同惩罚
senses.example: The steep climb punished legs that had not trained.
senses.exampleCN: 陡峭的山路让未经训练的腿吃尽苦头。
senses.why: The body itself can be made to pay for the effort demanded of it, so intense exertion completes the drift from moral debt to sheer physical cost.
senses.whyCN: 身体本身也能为被要求的努力付出代价，于是高强度消耗完成了从道德亏欠到纯粹身体代价的漂移。

intro.en: Punish came into English through Old French punir from Latin punire, an earlier form poenire built on poena 'penalty'. The same poena family also produced penal, penalty and punitive. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: punish 经古法语 punir 进入英语，上溯拉丁 punire，其较早形式 poenire 由 poena「罚」构成；同一个 poena 词族还生出 penal、penalty 与 punitive。年代均为约数。

items.en: The Greek noun poine named the price paid to settle a wrong, and it was borrowed into Latin as the starting point of this family.
items.cn: 希腊名词 poine 指为平息过错而付出的价，它被借入拉丁语，成为这一词族的起点。

items.en: Poena meant punishment and also the compensation that settled a wrong, and from it the verb poenire was formed.
items.cn: poena 既指处罚，也指平息过错的补偿，动词 poenire 由它构成。

items.en: Punire replaced the older poenire and meant to inflict a penalty, to avenge, to take vengeance for a wrong.
items.cn: punire 取代了较早的 poenire，意为施加处罚、报复、为过错索取代价。

items.en: Old French punir carried the Latin verb into the sense of correcting by pain, and English borrowed it around 1300.
items.cn: 古法语 punir 把这一拉丁动词带入「以痛苦纠正」的意思，英语大约在十四世纪初借入。

items.en: English punish first meant to inflict a legal penalty, then any painful correction, and finally rough handling of people or things.
items.cn: 英语 punish 最初指施加法律上的处罚，随后泛指任何带来痛苦的纠正，最后扩展到对人、对物的粗暴对待。

items.en: Punishment names the suffering as a result, punishable names what may be punished, and punitive names the intention behind a measure.
items.cn: punishment 把痛苦作为结果来命名，punishable 指可以受罚的，punitive 则指一项措施背后的惩罚意图。

note.en: The first group holds the same Latin family plus one mere look-alike; the second group offers near alternatives for the act of making someone suffer.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁词族的词，外加一个只是长得像的词；第二组是「使人受苦」这一动作的近义替代。

entries.definition: The noun naming the suffering imposed; the verb names the act of imposing it.
entries.definitionCN: 指被施加的痛苦的名词；动词则指施加这一动作。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning 'liable to be punished'; it describes a legal status, not an act.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「可受处罚的」形容词；它描述的是一种法律状态，而不是动作。

entries.definition: From Latin punire with an adjective suffix; it describes the purpose of a measure rather than the deed itself.
entries.definitionCN: 由拉丁 punire 加形容词后缀而来；它描述一项措施的目的，而不是行为本身。

entries.definition: Weak and small; it merely looks like punish at the start and is not related to it in origin.
entries.definitionCN: 瘦小虚弱的；只是开头与 punish 相似，并非同源。

entries.definition: To impose a penalty, usually under a written rule; it stresses the rule, while punish stresses the suffering.
entries.definitionCN: 通常依据成文规则施加处罚；它强调规则，而 punish 强调痛苦。

entries.definition: To correct behaviour through training or punishment; reform is the aim, which punish does not imply.
entries.definitionCN: 通过训练或惩罚纠正行为；改正是目的，punish 并不含此意。

entries.definition: To punish or scold severely; it often means words rather than physical suffering and sounds formal.
entries.definitionCN: 严厉惩罚或斥责；常指言语而非肉体痛苦，语体正式。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning 'relating to punishment'; it cannot take an object and never names the act.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「与刑罚有关的」形容词；它不能带宾语，也不指动作。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin verb, the real derived family and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁动词、真实的派生词族与真实的固定搭配。

normal.en: Punish goes back through French punir to Latin punire, and behind punire stands poena, the price of a wrong.
normal.cn: punish 经法语 punir 上溯拉丁 punire，而 punire 背后站着 poena，即过错的代价。

normal.en: The family keeps splitting the same idea: punishment is the suffering, punitive is the intention, punishable is the liability.
normal.cn: 这一词族不断拆分同一个观念：punishment 是那份痛苦，punitive 是那种意图，punishable 是那种责任。

normal.en: Punish almost always asks two questions: who suffers, and for what.
normal.cn: punish 几乎总要回答两个问题：谁受苦，以及为了什么。

normal.en: Fixed phrases show the legal core: punish offenders, punish wrongdoing, be punished by law.
normal.cn: 固定搭配显出法律内核：惩罚违法者、惩处不当行为、受法律制裁。

normal.en: The object can be a person, a body, a pair of shoes or an opponent, but the verb always means someone or something pays.
normal.cn: 宾语可以是人、身体、一双鞋或一个对手，但这个动词始终表示「有人或某物在偿付」。

abstract.en: Picture a scale where the wrong sits on one pan and the suffering is poured onto the other until the beam levels.
abstract.cn: 想象一架天平，一端放着过错，另一端被倒进痛苦，直到横梁齐平。

abstract.en: Picture a receipt handed to someone who never asked to buy anything.
abstract.cn: 想象一张收据被递给一个根本没打算买东西的人。

abstract.en: Picture a path of sharp stones laid across a field so that every step costs the walker something.
abstract.cn: 想象田野上铺着一条尖石小路，每走一步都要让行人付出点代价。

examples.en: The school punished the boys for vandalising the gym.
examples.cn: 学校因这些男孩破坏体育馆而惩罚了他们。

examples.en: Years of heavy loads had punished the truck's suspension.
examples.cn: 多年的重载已经把卡车的悬挂系统损耗得很厉害。

examples.en: The home side punished every mistake in the second half.
examples.cn: 主队在下半场抓住了每一次失误并加以重创。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「怕你失」——怕你失了规矩，就先让你吃一阵苦头 → 惩罚、处罚

root: 希腊 poine「为过错付出的价」→ 拉丁 poena「罚、补偿」→ 拉丁动词 poenire / punire「施罚、索偿」→ 古法语 punir → 英语 punish；同族词有 punishment、punishable、punitive、penal、penalty。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one line: a wrong creates a debt, and suffering collects it. The collection can be a general punishment, a court sentence, a parent's correction, deliberate harshness, wear on an object, a heavy defeat, sharp criticism, or plain physical exhaustion.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿着一条线展开：过错生出一笔债，而痛苦负责把它收回。收回的方式可以是泛指的惩罚、法庭的判决、父母的管教、刻意的严酷、对物品的损耗、一场惨败、尖锐的批评，或纯粹的身体消耗。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a mallet falls and the offender leaves his seat to bear the pain he brought about.
core.cn: 核心意象：木槌落下，犯错的人离开座位，去承受自己招来的那阵疼痛。

branches.en: BASE ACT: pain is deliberately dealt out because a wrong was done.
branches.cn: 基础动作：因为有人做错，痛苦被刻意施加出去。

branches.en: TWO COURTS: the debt is collected by a judge with a sentence, or by a parent with a withdrawn privilege.
branches.cn: 两种法庭：债由法官以判决收取，或由父母以收回特权收取。

branches.en: HARSHNESS WITHOUT A RULE: suffering continues even when no rule existed to be broken.
branches.cn: 无规之严：即便没有可供违反的规则，痛苦仍被继续施加。

branches.en: NON-HUMAN TARGETS: an object wears out under rough use, or an opponent is crushed by a score.
branches.cn: 非人对象：物品在粗暴使用下损耗，对手被比分碾碎。

branches.en: COST WITHOUT A VERDICT: words wound a reputation, and effort wrings out the body.
branches.cn: 无判决的代价：言语损伤名声，用力榨干身体。

intro.en: Punish sits at the head of an English family whose members split the ideas of act, result, liability and purpose.
intro.cn: punish 位于一个英语词族的首位，其成员分别承担动作、结果、责任与目的这几层意思。

latinIntro.en: Latin poena and the verb punire underlie punish, punishment, punishable and punitive, while the adjective poenalis leads to penal and penalty.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 poena 与动词 punire 位于 punish、punishment、punishable 与 punitive 之下，而形容词 poenalis 则通向 penal 与 penalty。

items.meaning: to exact a price for a wrong
items.example: The stem appears in several English words.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干出现在好几个英语词里。

items.meaning: to make someone suffer for a wrong
items.example: They punished him for the delay.
items.exampleCN: 他们因延误而惩罚了他。

items.example: The code punishes repeat offenders.
items.exampleCN: 该法典惩罚屡犯者。

items.example: He was punished for cheating.
items.exampleCN: 他因作弊受到惩罚。

items.example: It was a punishing schedule.
items.exampleCN: 那是一个折磨人的日程。

items.example: The punishment fitted the crime.
items.exampleCN: 这项惩罚与罪行相称。

items.example: The offence is punishable by fine.
items.exampleCN: 该违法行为可处以罚金。

items.example: The punisher rarely escapes blame.
items.exampleCN: 施罚者很少能免于责难。

items.example: They imposed punitive tariffs.
items.exampleCN: 他们加征了惩罚性关税。

items.example: The penal code was revised.
items.exampleCN: 刑法典被修订了。

items.example: The penalty was severe.
items.exampleCN: 处罚很严厉。

definition_zh: 批准；认可；法令；（官方）授权；制裁；处罚；约束力
definition_en: official approval that makes an act valid, or a penalty imposed to make a rule binding
core_image: 祭司把一件器物放到祭坛上，它因此变得不可侵犯：既被允许使用，也带着碰了要受罚的威力
scene: 董事会上，委员会把一份新合同推到桌子中央，主席签下名字表示允许，同时写明违约者要缴纳罚款。The board chairman gave his sanction to the new contract and warned that any breach would bring a fine.
sceneCN: 这里指有权者签字使某事生效，对应第 1 个义项：官方批准使行为合法；句意为董事会主席批准了这份新合同，并警告任何违约都将带来罚款。画面要点：桌上的合同、签下的名字、罚款条款。

pos.zh: 批准；认可（不可数，常与 give、grant、seek 连用）
制裁；处罚（可数，表示具体措施时多用复数）
批准；准许；认可（尤指官方）

derivatives.zh: 可批准的；可施加处罚的（加形容词后缀（源自拉丁语，表「能被……」））→ 由「批准或处罚」转为「可以被批准或可以被处罚的」
未获批准的（加否定前缀（表「不」））→ 由「已批准」转为「缺少批准的」
获准的；受制裁的（加过去分词词尾，作形容词，表被动状态）→ 由「批准这一动作」转为「已被批准或已被处罚的」
批准行为；制裁行为（加动名词后缀，表动作本身）→ 由「批准」转为「批准这件事的进行过程」
使神圣；使成为正当（同出拉丁 sanctus，加动词后缀（源自拉丁语，表「使成为」））→ 由「神圣」转为「使某物变得神圣而不可侵犯」

senses.title: Approval that makes an act lawful
senses.titleCN: 使行为合法的官方批准
senses.definition: the official approval by which an authority turns a proposed act into a permitted one
senses.definitionCN: 权威机构所给的正式同意，使原本待定的行为成为被允许的行为
senses.example: Parliament gave its sanction to the treaty after a long debate.
senses.exampleCN: 经过长时间辩论，议会批准了这项条约。
