senses.why: Latin sancire meant to fix a thing as sacred and binding; a decree that was settled this way removed all doubt about whether an act was allowed, so the first English sense is doubt removed by authority.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 sancire 意为「订立、使不可侵犯」，以这种方式定下的事不再有「能不能做」的疑问，所以最早的英语义项就是权威消除疑问。

senses.title: Power vested in an office
senses.titleCN: 授予职位或机构的权限
senses.definition: the authority conferred on a person or body, allowing them to act in a particular matter
senses.definitionCN: 授予某人或某机构的权限，使其可在特定事务上采取行动
senses.example: The inspector acted beyond his sanction when he seized the files.
senses.exampleCN: 那名检查员查扣文件时超越了自己的权限。
senses.why: The decree is not a yes to one act but an inviolable grant; once it is attached to an office instead of an act, the office itself carries the right to act.
senses.whyCN: 这道定案不是对某一次行为的点头，而是一份不可侵犯的授予；当它附着于职位而非某件事，职位本身就带上了行事的权利。

senses.title: A formal decree or standing law
senses.titleCN: 正式法令或长期有效的法规
senses.definition: a decree or enactment issued by a church or state authority and treated as binding
senses.definitionCN: 由教会或国家权威发布、并被当作有约束力的法令或法规
senses.example: By an ancient sanction, the abbey held the right to tax the village.
senses.exampleCN: 凭一道古老的法令，这座修道院拥有向村庄征税的权利。
senses.why: Before it named either approval or penalty, the word named the decree itself; a decree is exactly what grants rights and threatens those who break them, so this sense keeps the oldest layer visible.
senses.whyCN: 在指批准或处罚之前，这个词指的就是法令本身；法令正是授予权利、又威胁违者的东西，所以这一义项让最古老的一层保持可见。

senses.title: The penalty attached to a rule
senses.definition: a punishment laid down for breaking a law or rule, especially one written into the law itself
senses.definitionCN: 为违反法律或规则者规定的处罚，尤指写进法律条文的那种
senses.example: The statute carries a heavy criminal sanction for smuggling.
senses.exampleCN: 该法规对走私规定了严厉的刑事处罚。
senses.why: In Roman law the sanctio was the clause of a statute that fixed what happened to those who broke it; the same decree permits and threatens, so the word slid from binding rule to penalty.
senses.whyCN: 在罗马法中，sanctio 正是法条里规定违者后果的那一款；同一道定案既准许也威胁，词义便从「有约束力的规则」滑向「处罚」。

senses.title: Punitive measures between states
senses.titleCN: 国与国之间的惩罚性措施
senses.definition: restrictions adopted by one or more countries against another country to force a change of policy
senses.definitionCN: 一国或多国针对另一国采取的限制作法，以迫使其改变政策
senses.example: The council imposed sanctions on the regime after the border attack.
senses.exampleCN: 边境袭击发生后，理事会对该政权实施了制裁。
senses.why: When states rather than courts issue the decree, the penalty is no longer a fine but the closing of markets and ports; the plural names that collective punishment.
senses.whyCN: 当发布这道定案的是国家而不是法庭，处罚便不再是一笔罚款，而是市场与港口的关闭；复数形式指的就是这种集体惩罚。

senses.title: The separate items of a sanctions list
senses.titleCN: 制裁清单上的各项具体措施
senses.definition: each individual measure in a package of restrictions, such as an embargo, an asset freeze or a travel ban
senses.definitionCN: 一揽子限制措施中的每一项，如禁运、资产冻结或旅行禁令
senses.example: The sanctions include a freeze on bank accounts and a ban on arms sales.
senses.exampleCN: 这些制裁措施包括冻结银行账户和禁止军售。
senses.why: Each measure is a separate clause of the same decree, so the plural counts clauses rather than countries: one embargo, one freeze, one travel ban.
senses.whyCN: 每一项措施都是同一道定案里的独立条款，因此复数数的是条款而不是国家：一项禁运、一项冻结、一项旅行禁令。

senses.title: Social pressure that enforces a norm
senses.definition: the approval or disapproval of a community that keeps its members to an accepted standard
senses.definitionCN: 社群所表达的赞成或反对，使成员遵守公认标准
senses.example: In that village, gossip is the strongest sanction against bad behaviour.
senses.exampleCN: 在那个村子里，闲话是对不良行为最强的约束。
senses.why: A community without a court still makes its rules sacred by withdrawing approval; social sanction is the same mechanism with praise as the reward and exclusion as the penalty.
senses.whyCN: 没有法庭的社群仍靠收回赞许来把规矩变得神圣；社会约束是同一套机制，以称赞为奖赏、以排挤为惩罚。

senses.title: The binding force of custom or law
senses.titleCN: 惯例或法律的效力来源
senses.definition: the quality that makes a rule or practice binding and beyond challenge
senses.definitionCN: 使规则或惯例具有约束力、不容置疑的那种性质
senses.example: The custom has the sanction of centuries behind it.
senses.exampleCN: 这一习俗背后有数百年的效力支撑。
senses.why: The oldest layer asks what makes a rule binding at all; sancire answers that the rule is made sacred, and this sense names that quality rather than any single permission or fine.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的一层问的是：规则凭什么有约束力；sancire 的回答是「使它神圣」，这一义项命名的正是这种性质，而不是某一次准许或某一笔罚款。

intro.en: Sanction goes back to Latin sanctio, a noun of action from sancire 'to decree, to make inviolable', the family that also produced sanctus 'holy'. One act of decreeing both permitted and threatened, and that double face is still visible in English.
intro.cn: sanction 上溯拉丁语 sanctio，是动词 sancire「订立、使不可侵犯」的动作名词，同一词族还产生 sanctus「神圣的」。订立这一动作既准许又威胁，这张双面至今留在英语里。

items.en: Sancire was an attested verb meaning to decree, to ratify and to make a thing inviolable; the deeper root is reconstructed and not certain.
items.cn: sancire 是文献中确有的动词，意为「订立、批准、使某物不可侵犯」；更早的词根属重构，尚无定论。

items.en: Sanctio, the noun of action, named the act of decreeing and, in legal language, the clause of a statute that fixed a penalty.
items.cn: 动作名词 sanctio 指订立这一行为；在法律用语中，它指法条内规定处罚的那一款。

items.en: The same family gave sanctus 'holy, set apart', the past-participle form whose sense of being untouchable underlies both approval and penalty.
items.cn: 同族还给出 sanctus「神圣的、被分隔出来的」，其「不可触碰」之意正是批准与处罚两面的共同底色。

items.en: English took the word in the sixteenth century from Latin legal writing, first for the confirming part of a statute, then for the penalty clause that made it effective; the date is approximate.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪从拉丁法律文本引入该词，先指法条中予以确认的部分，后指使其生效的罚则；年代为约数。

items.en: By the seventeenth century sanction also meant plain approval given by any authority, including the approval of a practice by long usage.
items.cn: 到十七世纪，sanction 也指任何权威给出的单纯许可，包括长期沿用对某种做法的认可。

items.en: After the First World War the plural sanctions came to mean punitive measures taken by states against another state, and that is now the dominant everyday sense.
items.cn: 第一次世界大战之后，复数形式 sanctions 开始指国家对另一国采取的惩罚性措施，这已成为今天最常见的日常义。

note.en: The first group gathers words that look or sound close, some sharing the Latin root and one only resembling it; the second group offers near alternatives for approval and for punishment.
note.cn: 第一组收外形或读音相近的词，其中几个同出拉丁词根，有一个只是形近；第二组是「批准」与「处罚」两方面的近义替代。

entries.definition: The quality of being holy and untouchable; it shares the Latin root but names a sacred state, not a permission or a fine.
entries.definitionCN: 神圣不可侵犯的性质；同出拉丁词根，但指的是神圣状态，而非许可或罚款。

entries.definition: Regarded as too holy or too important to be changed; the root is shared, yet the word describes reverence rather than legal force.
entries.definitionCN: 被视为神圣或重要到不可更改的；词根相同，但描述的是敬畏，而不是法律效力。

entries.definition: Making a show of being morally superior; it keeps the holy root but turns it into a criticism of pretended piety.
entries.definitionCN: 装出道德高尚样子的；保留「神圣」词根，却转为对伪善的批评。

entries.definition: Systems for clean water and waste; it is merely similar in form and not cognate, since it comes from Latin sanus 'healthy', not from the decree root.
entries.definitionCN: 清洁水源与排污的系统；只是形近、并非同源，它出自拉丁 sanus「健康的」，与「订立」词根无关。

entries.definition: A favourable opinion or consent; it states agreement but not that the agreement makes the act legally binding.
entries.definitionCN: 赞同或同意；它只说认可，不说这种认可使行为具有法律约束力。

entries.definition: The formal act of confirming a treaty or contract; it covers the approval side of sanction but never the penalty side.
entries.definitionCN: 对条约或契约的正式确认；它覆盖 sanction 的批准一面，却从不含处罚一面。

entries.definition: A disadvantage imposed for breaking a rule; it names the punishment only and says nothing about prior authorization.
entries.definitionCN: 因违规而被施加的不利后果；它只指处罚本身，不涉及事先的授权。

entries.definition: An official ban on trade with a particular country; it is one kind of sanction, narrower and always commercial.
entries.definitionCN: 对某国贸易的官方禁令；它是制裁的一种，范围更窄且总与贸易有关。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin root, the real related words and the real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁词根、真实的同族词与真实的固定搭配。

normal.en: Sancire meant to decree and to make inviolable, so a sanction is a rule made untouchable.
normal.cn: sancire 意为「订立、使不可侵犯」，所以 sanction 是被定得不可触碰的规矩。

normal.en: The same family gives sanctus 'holy', which is why a sanctioned thing feels set apart and protected.
normal.cn: 同一词族给出 sanctus「神圣的」，所以被 sanction 的事物总显得被分隔出来、受到保护。

normal.en: In Roman law the sanctio was the penalty clause of a statute, which explains the punishing side.
normal.cn: 罗马法中的 sanctio 是法条的罚则，这解释了它处罚的那一面。

normal.en: Fixed phrases sort the two faces: give sanction to a plan, impose sanctions on a country.
normal.cn: 固定搭配把两张面孔分开：说「予以批准」时后面接一项计划，说「施加制裁」时后面接一个国家。

normal.en: One decree does both jobs: it says the act is allowed and says what happens if the rule is broken.
normal.cn: 同一道定案兼做两件事：宣布行为被允许，并规定破坏规矩的后果。

abstract.en: Picture a stone tablet placed on an altar: the writing on it is both a permission and a warning.
abstract.cn: 想象一块石碑被放上祭坛：碑上的字既是许可，也是警告。

abstract.en: Picture a door with two plates, one reading open and one reading fine, both fixed by the same hand.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门挂着两块牌子，一块写着「开」，一块写着「罚」，两块由同一只手挂上。

abstract.en: Picture a rope around a market stall: it lets the trader in and keeps everyone else out.
abstract.cn: 想象市集摊位周围拉着一根绳：它放摊主进去，把其余人都挡在外面。

examples.en: The committee refused to sanction the use of the site for housing.
examples.cn: 委员会拒绝批准把这处场地用于建房。

examples.en: Several governments tightened sanctions on the country's banks.
examples.cn: 若干政府收紧了对该国银行的制裁。

examples.en: He broke the club's rules and faced the sanction of expulsion.
examples.cn: 他违反了俱乐部规定，面临开除这一处罚。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「三克神」：祭坛上只准放三克圣物，神点头便是批准，谁多拿一克就要受罚 → 批准与制裁同出一门

root: 拉丁 sancire「订立、使神圣」→ 过去分词 sanctus「神圣的」→ 名词 sanctio「法令、罚则」；英语 sanction 由「以法令定下」同时带出准许与惩处两面，同族词有 sanctity、sanctify、sacrosanct。

sensesIntro.en: All eight senses come from one act: something is declared sacred and therefore fixed. Fixing produces approval, the authority to approve, and the standing decree that carries it; the same fixing also produces the penalty for breaking it, the measures states take, the social pressure that replaces a court, and finally the sheer binding force of a rule.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都出自同一个动作：某物被宣布为神圣，因而被定死。定死产生批准、批准所需的权限、以及承载批准的成文法令；同一个定死也产生违规后的处罚、国家所采的措施、取代法庭的社会压力，最后是规则本身的约束力。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an object placed on an altar and made untouchable, so that using it is permitted and abusing it is punished.
core.cn: 核心意象：一件器物被放上祭坛而变得不可侵犯，使用它被允许，侵犯它要受罚。

branches.en: APPROVAL: the decree removes doubt, and the act becomes permitted.
branches.cn: 批准：定案消除疑问，行为由此成为被允许的。

branches.en: AUTHORITY AND ITS INSTRUMENT: the grant can belong to an office, or stand as a written decree.
branches.cn: 权限与其载体：授予可附着于职位，也可立为成文法令。

branches.en: PENALTY: the same decree states the consequence of breaking it.
branches.cn: 处罚：同一道定案写明破坏它的后果。

branches.en: MEASURES BETWEEN STATES: the penalty grows from a fine into embargoes and freezes, counted item by item.
branches.cn: 国家间的措施：处罚由罚款扩大为禁运与冻结，并按条逐项计数。

branches.en: BINDING FORCE: without a court, approval and exclusion still enforce a norm, and the power behind any rule is named.
branches.cn: 约束力：没有法庭时，赞许与排挤仍能维系规范，而任何规则背后的效力也被命名。

intro.en: Sanction is a Latin noun of action, so its endings are the Latin markers of action and result; the same root supplies several English words about holiness and binding force.
intro.cn: sanction 是拉丁语的动作名词，其词尾正是拉丁语表示动作与结果的标记；同一词根还提供若干关于神圣与约束力的英语词。

latinIntro.en: Latin sancire 'to decree, to make inviolable' yields sanctio and sanctus; English draws sanction from the first and sanctity, sanctify and sacrosanct from the second.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 sancire「订立、使不可侵犯」产生 sanctio 与 sanctus；英语从前者取得 sanction，从后者取得 sanctity、sanctify 与 sacrosanct。

items.structure: Latin element sanc- (from sancire, to decree)
items.example: The element carries the act of fixing something by authority.
items.exampleCN: 这一成分承载的是以权威把某事定下来的动作。

items.meaning: the act or result of doing
items.example: The ending turns a verb of decreeing into the name of the decree.
items.exampleCN: 这一后缀把「订立」的动词转为「所订立之物」的名称。

items.meaning: official approval, or a penalty that makes a rule binding
items.meaningCN: 官方批准，或使规则生效的处罚
items.example: The plan needed the sanction of the ministry.
items.exampleCN: 该计划需要部里的批准。

items.meaning: several punitive measures, or several approvals
items.meaningCN: 多项惩罚性措施，或多份批准
items.example: The sanctions were extended for another year.
items.exampleCN: 这些制裁又延长了一年。

items.meaning: approved, or subjected to a penalty
items.meaningCN: 已获批准的，或已受处罚的
items.example: The march was sanctioned by the city.
items.exampleCN: 这场游行得到了市里的批准。

items.meaning: the act of approving or punishing
items.meaningCN: 予以批准或施加处罚的行为
items.example: Sanctioning the sale took three weeks.
items.exampleCN: 批准这笔交易花了三周。

items.meaning: able to be approved or punished
items.meaningCN: 可被批准或可被处罚的
items.example: The conduct is not sanctionable under the rules.
items.exampleCN: 按规则，这种行为无法被处罚。

items.example: The unsanctioned rally was stopped at the square.
items.exampleCN: 这场未经批准的集会在广场上被制止。

items.meaning: to make holy or to give sacred authority
items.meaningCN: 使神圣，或赋予神圣的权威
items.example: The old rite was meant to sanctify the agreement.
items.exampleCN: 这一古老仪式意在使该约定变得神圣。

items.meaning: the state of being holy and inviolable
items.meaningCN: 神圣而不可侵犯的状态
items.example: The shrine was defended for its sanctity.
items.exampleCN: 这座圣殿因其神圣性而受到守护。

latinEntries.meaning: to decree, to ratify, to make inviolable
a decree; the penalty clause of a statute

latinEntries.meaningCN: 神圣的；被分隔出来的；不可侵犯的

definition_zh: 监禁；关押；徒刑；被囚禁的状态
definition_en: the state or act of being shut up in a prison, usually as a punishment
core_image: 一扇铁门从外面落锁，把一个人从街道上取走，只留下墙内一小块属于他的地面
scene: 法庭宣判后，法警把被告带离座位，走廊尽头的铁门关上，他将在窄小的牢房里度过许多年。The judge imposed a long term of imprisonment on the man who had robbed the shop.
sceneCN: 这里指作为刑罚的关押，对应第 1 个义项：被判入狱服刑；句意为法官对抢劫商店的男子判处长期监禁。画面要点：法槌落下、被告被带走、铁门合拢。

pos.zh: 监禁；关押（不可数，指刑罚或状态）
刑期；服刑期间（可数，常与 years、life 等连用）

derivatives.zh: 监禁；关押（由表「进入」的前缀（拉丁语 in）加 prison 构成）→ 由「监狱」转为「使进入监狱」
被关押的；受禁锢的（加过去分词词尾，作形容词，表被动状态）→ 由「关押」转为「处在被关押之中的」
可判处监禁的（加形容词后缀（源自拉丁语，表「能被……」））→ 由「关押」转为「够得上被关押的」
使人如困牢笼的（加现在分词词尾，作形容词，表主动施加）→ 由「关进监狱」转为「把人在感觉上关住的」

senses.title: The penalty of being locked away
senses.definition: the punishment in which a person is confined in a prison for a period set by a court
senses.definitionCN: 由法庭确定期限、把人在监狱内关押起来的刑罚
senses.example: The judge imposed a long term of imprisonment on the man who had robbed the shop.
senses.exampleCN: 法官对抢劫商店的男子判处长期监禁。
senses.why: The noun adds -ment, 'act or state', to imprison, so it names the whole condition produced when the verb is carried out; the penalty sense is that condition viewed as a sentence.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词由 imprison 加名词后缀（表动作或状态）构成，指动词执行后造成的整个处境；把它看作一种判决，就是作为刑罚的关押。

senses.title: The condition of being confined
senses.definition: the lived state of a person who is kept inside walls and cannot leave
senses.definitionCN: 人被关在墙内、不能离开的那种生活状态
senses.example: Years of imprisonment had left him afraid of open spaces.
senses.exampleCN: 多年监禁使他对开阔的空间感到害怕。
senses.why: The same -ment can name a state rather than an event, so the word shifts from the sentence handed down to what the sentence feels like from inside.
senses.whyCN: 同一个名词后缀也能指状态而非事件，词义于是从「宣判的那一下」转到「从里面感受到的判决」。

senses.title: A term served, viewed as time
senses.titleCN: 被当作一段时间来数的刑期
senses.definition: the period during which a person is held, treated as a span of time in someone's life
senses.definitionCN: 人被关押的那段时间，被当作某人生命中的一段来计量
senses.example: He wrote most of the novel during his imprisonment.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说的大部分是他在监禁期间写成的。
senses.why: Once the state has a beginning and an end, it can be counted; counting turns the condition into a term, and a term can be spent, served or survived.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这种处境有了开头和结尾，它就能被计数；计数把处境变成刑期，而刑期可以被度过、服完或熬过。

senses.title: Custody before any trial
senses.definition: confinement of a suspect while legal proceedings are still pending
senses.definitionCN: 在司法程序尚未结束期间对嫌疑人实施的关押
senses.example: Suspects may face months of imprisonment before any trial begins.
senses.exampleCN: 嫌疑人可能在审判开始之前被关押数月。
senses.why: If the verb only means to shut someone in, it need not wait for a verdict; custody is imprisonment before the penalty has been decided.
senses.whyCN: 如果动词的本义只是「把人关起来」，那就不必等判决；羁押是处罚尚未定下之前就已发生的监禁。

senses.title: Unlawful holding by captors
senses.titleCN: 被掳者实施的非法关押
senses.definition: confinement imposed by captors or authorities who have no legal right to hold the person
senses.definitionCN: 由无合法关押权的掳掠者或当局施加的关押
senses.example: The journalists described their imprisonment by the militia.
senses.exampleCN: 记者们描述了民兵对他们的关押。
senses.why: The word describes the physical fact of confinement and does not certify that the confinement is lawful, so it serves equally for a kidnapper's cellar.
senses.whyCN: 这个词描述的是关押这一物理事实，并不担保关押合法，因此同样适用于绑架者的地窖。

senses.title: Confinement of the mind
senses.definition: a figurative state in which a person feels trapped by circumstances, work or habit
senses.definitionCN: 人因处境、工作或习惯而感到被牢牢困住的比喻状态
senses.example: She felt her imprisonment in a job that allowed no creativity.
senses.exampleCN: 她感到自己被一份毫无创造空间的工作禁锢住了。
senses.why: The core image needs only walls and a lock; when the walls become rules or routines, the same noun describes a life with no exit.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象只需要墙与锁；当墙变成规矩或惯例，同一个名词就用来描述没有出口的生活。

senses.title: Mass detention of a group
senses.definition: the holding of many people together in camps or closed areas, often in wartime
senses.definitionCN: 把许多人集中关押在营地或封闭区域内，常发生在战时
senses.example: The museum records the imprisonment of thousands in the camps.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆记录了成千上万人在营地的关押。
senses.why: Because the noun has no singular subject built in, it can be used of a crowd as easily as of one man; scale changes, the walls do not.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词本身不限定只能指一个人，因此既可指一人也可指一群人；规模变了，墙还是那道墙。

senses.title: The act of putting someone away
senses.definition: the act of confining a person, considered as something done by an authority or a captor
senses.definitionCN: 把人关押起来这一动作，被视为某当局或掳掠者所做之事
senses.example: The imprisonment of the union leaders provoked protests across the city.
senses.exampleCN: 对工会领导人的关押在整座城市引发了抗议。
senses.why: The -ment noun can name the deed as well as its result; naming the deed lets speakers argue about who did it and whether it should have been done.
senses.whyCN: 带名词后缀的名词既能指结果，也能指行为本身；点出行为，人们才能争论是谁做的、该不该做。

intro.en: Imprisonment is English through and through in its building: in- 'into' plus prison plus -ment. Prison itself goes back through Old French to Latin prehensio 'a seizing', from prehendere 'to grasp', so the word is about capture before it is about architecture.
intro.cn: imprisonment 的构造完全是英语自身的：表「进入」的前缀加 prison 再加名词后缀。prison 经古法语上溯拉丁 prehensio「抓取」，源头是动词 prehendere「抓住」，所以这个词先说的是捕获，其次才是建筑。

items.en: Prehendere was an attested verb meaning to seize, grasp or take hold of a person or thing.
items.cn: prehendere 是文献中确有的动词，意为抓住、握取或捕获人或物。

items.en: The noun of action prehensio 'a seizing, a capture' supplied the sense of a person taken and held; the later sense of a place for holding them grew from this.
items.cn: 动作名词 prehensio「抓取、捕获」提供了「人被捉住并扣留」这一层意思；后来「扣留人的场所」之义即由此生长出来。

items.en: Old French shortened the Latin noun into prison, which meant both the act of holding and the place of confinement; the date of this reduction is uncertain.
items.cn: 古法语把这一拉丁名词缩短为 prison，兼指扣留的行为与关押的场所；这一缩略发生的年代不确定。

items.en: English borrowed the word in the thirteenth century, at first for the place and the state of being held there.
items.cn: 英语在十三世纪借入该词，最初指场所以及被关在其中的状态。

items.en: The verb was formed inside English by adding in- 'into' to the noun, so that it means literally to put someone into a prison.
items.cn: 动词是在英语内部构成的，给名词加上表「进入」的前缀，字面即「把某人放进监狱」。

items.en: Adding -ment, the Latin-derived suffix for an act or its result, produced the noun; its first records are medieval and the exact date is uncertain.
items.cn: 再加上源自拉丁、表示动作或其结果的名词后缀，便得到这个名词；其最早记录属中世纪，确切年代不确定。

note.en: The first group gathers forms that echo the word, three from the same Latin capture root and one only resembling it; the second group offers near alternatives for being held in custody.
note.cn: 第一组收外形相近的形式，其中三个同出拉丁「抓取」词根，一个只是形近；第二组是「被关押」这一意思的近义替代。

entries.definition: The building or institution where people are held; it shares the whole history of the longer noun but names the place rather than the penalty.
entries.definitionCN: 关押人的建筑或机构；它与长名词共享整段历史，但指的是场所而非刑罚。

entries.definition: The act of grasping or seizing; it preserves the Latin sense of taking hold that lies behind prison.
entries.definitionCN: 抓取或擒获的动作；它保留了 prison 背后「拿住」的拉丁本义。

entries.definition: To arrest someone or to grasp an idea; built on the same verb of seizing, with a prefix meaning 'towards'.
entries.definitionCN: 逮捕某人或理解某个观念；同建于那个「抓住」的动词，前缀表示「朝向」。

entries.definition: A mark or feeling left by contact; it is merely similar in form and not cognate, being built on a verb meaning 'to press into', not on the verb of seizing.
entries.definitionCN: 接触留下的印记或感觉；只是形近、并非同源，它建于表示「压入」的动词，而不是「抓住」的动词。

entries.definition: Imprisonment in a jail or camp, from Latin carcer 'prison'; it covers the same fact through a completely different word family.
entries.definitionCN: 在监狱或营地中的关押，出自拉丁 carcer「监狱」；它用完全不同的词族说出同一事实。

entries.definition: The state of being kept in custody, often before trial or without a sentence; it stresses withholding rather than punishment.
entries.definitionCN: 被扣留的状态，常在审判前或未判刑时；它强调「留住不放」，而非惩罚。

entries.definition: Being kept within limits or walls; it can apply to a sickroom or a cage, so it is wider and less legal than imprisonment.
entries.definitionCN: 被限制在界限或墙内；它可用于病房或兽笼，因此比 imprisonment 更宽、更少法律色彩。

entries.definition: Responsibility for and control over a person, especially by police or a guardian; it names the keeping, not the sentence.
entries.definitionCN: 对某人的看管与控制，尤指警方或监护人的看管；它指「看住」，不指刑罚。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin capture root, the real related forms and the real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁「抓取」词根、真实的同族形式与真实的固定搭配。

normal.en: Break it as in- 'into' + prison + -ment 'state', which is exactly how English built the word.
normal.cn: 拆成「进入」加「监狱」加「状态」，这正是英语当初造词的方式。

normal.en: Prison goes back to Latin prehensio 'a seizing', so the word began with a hand closing on a person.
normal.cn: prison 上溯拉丁 prehensio「抓取」，所以这个词最初是一只手把人抓住。

normal.en: Prehendere 'to grasp' also gives apprehend and prehension, all about taking hold.
normal.cn: prehendere「抓住」还给出 apprehend 与 prehension，都与拿住有关。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the legal frame: life imprisonment, a term of imprisonment, imprisonment without trial.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出法律框架：终身监禁、一段刑期、未经审判的关押。

normal.en: The Latin word for a prison building was carcer, a different family, which is why incarceration looks nothing like this word.
normal.cn: 拉丁语中表示监狱建筑的词是 carcer，属另一词族，所以 incarceration 与这个词毫无形似。

abstract.en: Picture a corridor of cells seen from outside, each door locked with the same key.
abstract.cn: 想象从外面看一条牢房走廊，每扇门都用同一把钥匙锁着。

abstract.en: Picture a man's outline left on a street, then a wall drawn where he used to stand.
abstract.cn: 想象街上留下一个人的轮廓，随后在他原来站的地方画起一堵墙。

abstract.en: Picture a clock inside a cell, its hands moving while the room stays still.
abstract.cn: 想象牢房里有一只钟，指针在走，房间却一动不动。

examples.en: He was sentenced to ten years' imprisonment for fraud.
examples.cn: 他因诈骗被判处十年监禁。

examples.en: The charity campaigns against the imprisonment of children.
examples.cn: 该慈善机构致力于反对关押儿童。

examples.en: Her imprisonment in that small town ended when the railway opened.
examples.cn: 铁路开通后，她被困在那座小城的日子结束了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「硬迫人」：硬把一个人迫进铁门里，门从外面锁上，许多年不得出来 → 监禁、关押

root: 拉丁 prehendere「抓住」→ 动作名词 prehensio「抓取、捕获」→ 古法语 prison「扣留；监所」→ 英语 prison；加表「进入」的前缀得 imprison，再加名词后缀得 imprisonment。

sensesIntro.en: The base is a physical fact: a person is taken and placed behind a lock. From that one fact come the court's penalty, the felt condition, the countable term, pre-trial custody, unlawful holding, mass detention, and the deed of putting someone away; only the last two steps leave the walls behind and confine a mind or a life.
sensesIntro.cn: 底层是一个物理事实：人被拿住并放到锁后。由这一个事实生出法庭的刑罚、身处其中的感受、可数的刑期、审判前的羁押、非法的关押、群体性的关押，以及「把人关进去」这一行为；只有最后一步离开实墙，把心智或生活关住。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a door locked from the outside, with one person left standing on the inner side of it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一扇从外面锁上的门，门内只剩一个人站着。

branches.en: THE DEED AND ITS SENTENCE: someone is put away, and the putting away is what the court orders.
branches.cn: 行为与判决：有人被关进去，而「关进去」正是法庭所判之事。

branches.en: INSIDE THE WALL: the same fact felt as a condition, then measured as a span of years.
branches.cn: 墙内的感受：同一事实先被感受为处境，再被量成若干年的跨度。

branches.en: BEFORE JUDGMENT: the lock can close while the case is still open.
branches.cn: 判决之前：案子还没结，锁已经可以先落下。

branches.en: WITHOUT RIGHT, AND IN NUMBERS: captors and camps keep people behind the same kind of door.
branches.cn: 无权与成群：掳掠者与营地用同一类门把人留住，只是没有合法权利、且人数众多。

branches.en: WALLS BECOME CIRCUMSTANCE: the lock turns into a job, a habit or a small town.
branches.cn: 墙化为处境：锁变成一份工作、一种习惯或一座小城。

intro.en: This noun is built from an English prefix, an English noun and a Latin-derived suffix, which makes its structure easy to see.
intro.cn: 这个名词由一个英语前缀、一个英语名词与一个源自拉丁的后缀构成，结构因此很容易看清。

latinIntro.en: The Latin contribution is indirect: the suffix -ment comes from -mentum, and prison itself descends from prehensio, a noun of action from prehendere 'to grasp'.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的贡献是间接的：名词后缀出自拉丁语中表动作或结果的词尾，而 prison 本身源自 prehensio，即动词 prehendere「抓住」的动作名词。

items.example: The prefix adds the direction of movement to the noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀给名词加上了移动的方向。

items.structure: assimilated form of in- before p
items.meaning: into, the same prefix reshaped for ease of speech
items.meaningCN: 进入；同一前缀在 p 前为顺口而变形的写法
items.example: Before a p the prefix is written with an m.
items.exampleCN: 在 p 之前，这个前缀写作 m。

items.meaning: a place where people are held
items.example: The old prison is now a museum.
items.exampleCN: 那座旧监狱现在是博物馆。

items.structure: Latin suffix -mentum (means or result of an action)
items.meaning: an act, its result, or the state produced
items.meaningCN: 动作、动作的结果，或由此产生的状态
items.example: The ending turns the verb into the name of its outcome.
items.exampleCN: 这一后缀把动词转为结果之名。

items.meaning: to put a person into a prison
items.example: The law allows courts to imprison offenders.
items.exampleCN: 法律允许法庭监禁罪犯。

items.meaning: the state of being held in prison
items.meaningCN: 被关押在监狱中的状态
items.example: The sentence was five years of imprisonment.
items.exampleCN: 判决是五年监禁。

items.example: The imprisoned editor was released in spring.
items.exampleCN: 被关押的编辑在春天获释。

items.meaning: serious enough to be punished with prison
items.meaningCN: 严重到可被判处监禁的
items.example: Theft is an imprisonable offence.
items.exampleCN: 盗窃是可判处监禁的罪行。

items.meaning: shutting someone in, or making a place feel like a cell
items.meaningCN: 把人关起来，或使某处像牢房一样令人窒息
items.example: The narrow streets have an imprisoning feel.
items.exampleCN: 这些窄巷给人一种被囚住的感觉。

latinEntries.meaning: to seize, grasp, take hold of

definition_zh: 监禁；关押；把……投入监狱；使陷于牢笼般的境地
definition_en: to shut a person or animal inside a prison or any place that allows no way out
core_image: 一个人被推进铁栅门内，门闩在他身后落下，外面的路从此不再属于他
scene: 士兵把俘虏带进石墙围起的小院，铁门在身后落锁，街市的声音一下就远了。The soldiers imprisoned the captured officer in a stone cell behind the walls.
sceneCN: 这里指把人关进监狱，对应第 1 个义项：把某人投入监所；句意为士兵把被俘的军官关在石墙后的牢房里。画面要点：俘虏、石墙小院、从外面落下的门闩。

pos.zh: 监禁；关押（多用于被动，常与 in、for 连用）
禁锢；使如处牢笼（比喻用法）

collocations.phrase: imprison an animal in a cage

derivatives.zh: 监禁；关押（加名词后缀，源自拉丁语，表动作或状态）→ 由「关押」转为「被关押这件事及其状态」
被关押的；受禁锢的（加过去分词词尾，作形容词，表被动状态）→ 由「关押」转为「处在被关押之中的」
可判处监禁的（加形容词后缀（源自拉丁语，表「能被……」））→ 由「关押」转为「够得上被关押的」
使人如困牢笼的（加现在分词词尾，作形容词，表主动施加）→ 由「关进监狱」转为「在感觉上把人关住的」

senses.title: To put a person into a prison
senses.definition: to confine a person in a prison, especially as a punishment ordered by a court
senses.definitionCN: 把人关押在监狱中，尤指按法庭判决作为惩罚
senses.example: The soldiers imprisoned the captured officer in a stone cell behind the walls.
senses.exampleCN: 士兵把被俘的军官关在石墙后的牢房里。
senses.why: In- carries the meaning 'into' and prison names the place, so the verb says exactly 'to put into a prison'; the core image is a step across a threshold that closes behind.
senses.whyCN: 前缀表示「进入」，prison 指出场所，所以动词说的正是「放进监狱」；核心意象是跨过一道随即在身后关闭的门槛。

senses.title: To hold someone in any closed place
senses.titleCN: 把某人关在任何封闭之处
senses.definition: to keep a person where they cannot leave, even if the place is not a formal prison
senses.definitionCN: 把人留在无法离开的地方，即使那地方并非正式监狱
senses.example: The sailors were imprisoned below deck while the storm lasted.
senses.exampleCN: 风暴期间，水手们被关在甲板下面。
senses.why: Prison had already widened from a building to any act of holding, so the verb can put a person in a cellar or a cabin as long as the way out is shut.
senses.whyCN: prison 早已从建筑物扩大到任何扣留行为，所以只要出口被封住，动词就可以把人关进地窖或船舱。

senses.title: To shut an animal in an enclosure
senses.titleCN: 把动物关进围栏或笼子
senses.definition: to confine an animal in a cage, pen or other enclosure
senses.definitionCN: 把动物关在笼子、围栏或其他封闭处所内
senses.example: The farmer imprisoned the injured bird in a wooden cage until it healed.
senses.exampleCN: 农夫把受伤的鸟关在木笼里，直到它痊愈。
senses.why: The same verb serves any creature that can be shut in; the cage replaces the cell and the species of the prisoner is no part of the meaning.
senses.whyCN: 同一个动词适用于任何能被关住的生物；笼子替换了牢房，被关者的种类并不参与词义。

senses.title: To hold a suspect before trial
senses.definition: to keep an accused person in custody while the case is still being heard
senses.definitionCN: 在案件仍在审理时把被指控者关押起来
senses.example: Police may imprison a suspect only for a limited period before a hearing.
senses.exampleCN: 警方只能在听证之前有限期地关押嫌疑人。
senses.why: The verb says nothing about a verdict; it only says the door is locked, so it can describe custody imposed while no court has yet spoken.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词不涉及判决，只说明门已锁上，因此可以描述法庭尚未发话时就已实施的羁押。

senses.title: To hold someone without any right to
senses.definition: to confine a person unlawfully, as a kidnapper or an armed group does
senses.definitionCN: 非法地把人关起来，如绑架者或武装团体所为
senses.example: The gang imprisoned the travellers in a cellar for three days.
senses.exampleCN: 那伙人把旅客关在地窖里三天。
senses.why: Because the word describes the lock rather than its legality, a captor with no authority performs the very same action and the same verb applies.
senses.whyCN: 这个词描述的是锁，而不是锁是否合法，所以毫无权限的掳掠者做出同一动作时，仍用同一个动词。

senses.title: To confine a mind or a life
senses.definition: to make someone feel trapped by fear, habit or circumstance, without any physical walls
senses.definitionCN: 使人因恐惧、习惯或处境而感到被困住，并无实体的墙
senses.example: Fear of failure had imprisoned her imagination for years.
senses.exampleCN: 对失败的恐惧多年来禁锢着她的想象力。
senses.why: Only the wall needs to be real in the base sense; once fear or routine takes its place, the verb can confine something that cannot be seen at all.
senses.whyCN: 在本义里只有墙必须是真实的；当恐惧或惯例取代了墙，动词就能关住完全看不见的东西。

senses.title: To trap matter inside a solid
senses.titleCN: 把物质封存在固体之内
senses.definition: to hold water, gas or another substance so that it cannot escape from rock or crystal
senses.definitionCN: 使水、气体或其他物质被封在岩石或晶体中而无法逸出
senses.example: Water imprisoned in the rock rises to the surface as a spring.
senses.exampleCN: 封存在岩石中的水以泉水的形式升到地面。
senses.why: Matter can be held the way a person is held: rock that will not let water out is said to imprison it, so the lock is borrowed for the crystal.
senses.whyCN: 物质也能像人一样被留住：不让水逃出的岩石被说成把水关住，锁的意象就此借给了晶体。

senses.title: To hold a whole group at once
senses.definition: to confine many people together in a camp, ghetto or other closed area
senses.definitionCN: 把许多人集中关押在营地、隔离区或其他封闭区域
senses.example: The authorities imprisoned thousands of civilians in the camp.
senses.exampleCN: 当局把数千平民关押在营地里。
senses.why: The verb has no singular subject built into it, so the same act can fall on thousands at once and the camp simply becomes a cell on a larger scale.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词本身不限定单一对象，所以同一动作可一次落在数千人身上，营地只是放大后的牢房。

intro.en: Imprison is formed inside English from in- 'into' and the noun prison. Prison descends through Old French from Latin prehensio 'a seizing', a noun of action from prehendere 'to grasp', so the word began with a hand taking hold of a person. The Latin noun for a prison building, carcer, belongs to another family and plays no part here.
intro.cn: imprison 是在英语内部用表「进入」的前缀与名词 prison 构成的。prison 经古法语上溯拉丁 prehensio「抓取」，那是动词 prehendere「抓住」的动作名词，所以这个词最初是一只手把人拿住。拉丁语中表示监狱建筑的 carcer 属另一词族，与此无关。

items.en: Prehendere meant to seize, grasp or lay hold of; it is attested in classical texts and its principal parts are prehendi and prehensum.
items.cn: prehendere 意为抓住、握取或拿住；古典文献中确有此词，其主要形式为 prehendi 与 prehensum。

items.en: The action noun prehensio named a seizing or a capture, and in later usage it could also mean the keeping of a captive.
items.cn: 动作名词 prehensio 指抓取或捕获，在后来的用法中也可指对俘虏的扣留。

items.en: Old French reduced the Latin noun to prison, which covered both the act of holding and the room where a person was held.
items.cn: 古法语把这一拉丁名词缩略为 prison，兼指扣留行为与关人的处所。

items.en: English borrowed the word in the thirteenth century and used it mainly for the building and for the state of being inside it.
items.cn: 英语在十三世纪借入该词，主要用于指建筑物以及身在其中的状态。

items.en: Adding the prefix that means 'into' produced a verb that could take an object: to put that person into the place. Its early records are medieval and the exact date is uncertain.
items.cn: 加上表示「进入」的前缀，便造出可带宾语的动词：把那个人放进那个场所。其早期记录属中世纪，确切年代不确定。

items.en: Later the verb extended to animals in cages, to minds held by fear and to water sealed in rock; the dates of these transfers are uncertain.
items.cn: 后来动词扩展到笼中的动物、被恐惧困住的心智以及封在岩石里的水；这些语义转移发生的年代不确定。

note.en: The first group gathers forms that echo the verb, three from the same Latin capture family and one only resembling it; the second group offers near alternatives for putting a person away.
note.cn: 第一组收与这个动词形近的形式，其中三个同出拉丁「抓取」词族，一个只是形近；第二组是「把人关起来」的近义替代。

entries.definition: The place itself, which supplies the whole second half of the verb; here a building is named, not an action.
entries.definitionCN: 场所本身，构成了这个动词的后半截；此处命名的是建筑，不是动作。

entries.definition: The act of grasping; it keeps the Latin sense of taking hold that the verb inherited.
entries.definitionCN: 抓取的动作；它保留了这个动词所继承的「拿住」本义。

entries.definition: The state or act of being confined, built from this verb with a suffix of action; it names the result rather than the deed.
entries.definitionCN: 被关押的状态或行为，由这个动词加表动作的后缀构成；它命名结果而非动作。

entries.definition: A mark or feeling left by contact; it is merely similar in form and not cognate, being built on a verb meaning 'to press into'.
entries.definitionCN: 接触留下的印记或感觉；只是形近、并非同源，它建于表示「压入」的动词。

entries.definition: To put someone in a local lock-up; it is the everyday word for the same act and carries no hint of the Latin root.
entries.definitionCN: 把某人关进地方看守所；它是同一动作的日常说法，不带那层拉丁词根。

entries.definition: To keep within bounds; it works for a room, a bed or a subject, and so is broader and less punitive.
entries.definitionCN: 使留在界限之内；它可用于房间、病床或话题，因此更宽泛、惩罚色彩更淡。

entries.definition: To keep a person in official custody, often briefly; it stresses that release is being withheld.
entries.definitionCN: 把人置于官方扣留之下，往往时间较短；它强调不放人。

entries.definition: To put someone in a jail or camp; it means the same thing but comes from Latin carcer, a wholly different family.
entries.definitionCN: 把人关进监狱或营地；意思相同，却出自拉丁 carcer，属完全不同的词族。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin capture root, the real related forms and the real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁「抓取」词根、真实的同族形式与真实的固定搭配。

normal.en: Split the word as 'into' plus 'prison', which is how it was actually built.
normal.cn: 把词拆成「进入」加「监狱」，这正是它当初的造法。

normal.en: Prison descends from Latin prehensio 'a seizing', so the word began as a hand closing on someone.
normal.cn: prison 上溯拉丁 prehensio「抓取」，所以这个词最初是一只手把人抓住。

normal.en: Prehendere 'to grasp' also gives prehension and apprehend, both about taking hold.
normal.cn: prehendere「抓住」还给出 prehension 与 apprehend，都与拿住有关。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the legal frame: be imprisoned for, be imprisoned without trial, unlawfully imprison.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出法律框架：因……被监禁、未经审判被关押、非法拘禁。

normal.en: The result noun is imprisonment, so a verb that puts a person in becomes a noun for the state of being in.
normal.cn: 结果名词是 imprisonment，于是「把人关进去」的动词变成「处于其中」的名词。

abstract.en: Picture a hand pushing a man's shoulders through a doorway, then the door closing on the hand.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手把人的肩膀推进门里，随后门在那只手上合拢。

abstract.en: Picture a bird in a cage drawn with the same lines as a cell.
abstract.cn: 想象一只笼中的鸟，笼子的线条与牢房一模一样。

abstract.en: Picture a thought wearing a collar and chain, unable to leave the room.
abstract.cn: 想象一个念头戴着项圈与锁链，走不出房间。

examples.en: The regime imprisoned the editor for a single article.
examples.cn: 该政权因一篇文章就把这位编辑关押起来。

examples.en: Debt had imprisoned him in a job he could not leave.
examples.cn: 债务把他困在一份他离不开的工作里。

examples.en: They imprison the bees in hives during the cold months.
examples.cn: 寒冷月份里，他们把蜜蜂关在蜂箱中。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「阴森森」：铁门里阴森森的，人被硬推进去就再难出来 → 监禁、关押

root: 拉丁 prehendere「抓住」→ prehensio「抓取、捕获」→ 古法语 prison「扣留；监所」→ 英语 prison；英语在其前加表「进入」的前缀构成 imprison，与 carcer「监狱」无关。

sensesIntro.en: One movement stands behind all eight senses: a person or thing is pushed across a threshold and the way back is shut. That gives the prison, the closed room, the cage, the pre-trial cell, the kidnapper's cellar, the trapped mind, the water sealed in stone, and finally the many behind one camp gate.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项背后只有一个动作：人或其他东西被推过一道门槛，回路随即关上。由此依次得到监狱、封闭的房间、兽笼、审判前的牢房、绑架者的地窖、被困住的心智、封在石中的水，最后是同一道营门后的许多人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a body pushed through a gate that is then barred from the outside.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个身体被推过门，随后门从外面闩上。

branches.en: THE DEED AT TWO SCALES: one person put in a cell, or thousands put in a camp.
branches.cn: 两种规模的行为：一人被关进牢房，或数千人被关进营地。

branches.en: ANY ENCLOSURE: a cabin, a cellar or a cage can take the place of the prison.
branches.cn: 任何封闭处所：船舱、地窖或兽笼都能取代监狱。

branches.en: BEFORE THE VERDICT: the door is barred while the case is still open.
branches.cn: 判决之前：案子未结，门已闩上。

branches.en: WITHOUT A RIGHT: the same barred door, held by someone who may not hold it.
branches.cn: 没有权利：同一扇闩上的门，却由无权这样做的人把守。

branches.en: THE THRESHOLD LEAVES THE WORLD: fear walls in a mind, and stone walls in water.
branches.cn: 门槛离开现实世界：恐惧把心智围住，岩石把水围住。

intro.en: The verb is a prefix plus a noun, and both halves are still recognisable in English today.
intro.cn: 这个动词是一个前缀加一个名词，两半在今天仍可辨认。

latinIntro.en: The prefix comes from Latin in- 'into', while the noun descends from prehensio, the action noun of prehendere 'to grasp'.
latinIntro.cn: 前缀出自拉丁语中表「进入」的 in，名词则源自 prehensio，即 prehendere「抓住」的动作名词。

items.example: The prefix supplies the direction of the action.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀提供动作的方向。

items.meaning: the same prefix, reshaped before a lip sound
items.meaningCN: 同一前缀在双唇音前为顺口而变形的写法
items.example: Before a p the nasal is written as m.
items.exampleCN: 在 p 之前，这个鼻音写作 m。

items.example: The prison stands beside the river.
items.exampleCN: 那座监狱立在河边。

items.example: They imprisoned him for his beliefs.
items.exampleCN: 他们因他的信念把他关押起来。

items.example: The law imprisons no one without a hearing.
items.exampleCN: 法律不会在未经听证的情况下关押任何人。

items.example: The imprisoned poet wrote on scraps of paper.
items.exampleCN: 被关押的诗人在纸片上写作。

items.meaning: the act of confining, or a quality that confines
items.meaningCN: 关押的动作，或使人受困的性质
items.example: The imprisoning heat kept everyone indoors.
items.exampleCN: 令人无处可逃的酷热使所有人都待在室内。

items.example: The court ordered three years of imprisonment.
items.exampleCN: 法庭判处三年监禁。

items.meaning: serious enough for a prison sentence
items.example: The offence is imprisonable under the statute.
items.exampleCN: 按该法规，这项罪行可判处监禁。

definition_zh: 监禁；关押；囚禁；（作为状态的）被收押；刑期；禁锢状态
definition_en: the state of being confined in a prison or jail, or the act of putting a person there
core_image: 铁门在身后合上，长长走廊尽头是一排上锁的牢房，人只能在栅栏后数着日子
scene: 宣判结束后，法警把被告带下法庭台阶，直接押往县看守所那扇厚重的铁门。After the sentence was read, the marshals took the defendant downstairs for incarceration in the county jail.
sceneCN: 这里指「被收押在监所里、人身自由被剥夺」这一状态，对应第 1 个义项：人已身处牢房之内、不能自行离开；句意为宣判之后，法警把被告带下法庭，送往县看守所关押。画面要点：铁门、长走廊、一排上锁的牢房。

pos.zh: 监禁；关押（多作不可数名词指状态，也可作可数名词指一段关押经历）

derivatives.zh: 由 incarceration 去掉名词后缀（源自拉丁语，表动作或状态）→ 由「被关押的状态」回到「把人关进牢中」这一动作
incarcerate 加过去分词词尾（转作形容词）→ 由「已被关进去」转为「处于被关押状态的」
拉丁 carcer（牢笼）加形容词后缀→ 由「牢笼」转为「与监狱、监禁制度有关的」
incarceration 与 rate 复合 → 由「监禁」转为「衡量在押人口比例的统计指标」

senses.title: The prison state: held behind bars
senses.titleCN: 被关在铁栏之后的处境
senses.definition: the condition of a person who is confined in a prison or jail and cannot leave by their own will
senses.definitionCN: 被关押在监狱或看守所之内、不能凭自己意愿离开的处境
senses.example: The report described the conditions of incarceration in the old county jail.
senses.exampleCN: 报告描述了旧县监狱中的关押条件。
senses.why: Latin carcer named a walled pen, and with in- 'into' plus a noun ending for a state, the word settles on being inside that pen rather than on the building that holds it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 carcer 指围起来的圈栏，加上表示「进入」的前缀与表状态的名词后缀，这个词就落在「身处围栏之内」的处境上，而不是指关人的那栋建筑。

senses.title: The act of locking away: the door closing
senses.definition: the act by which an authority places a person in custody in a prison or jail
senses.definitionCN: 有权机关将某人收押进监狱或看守所的行为
senses.example: The law limits the incarceration of juveniles to exceptional cases.
senses.exampleCN: 法律把对未成年人的关押限制在例外情形。
senses.why: The same abstract ending can name either the deed or the condition it produces, so the noun also looks at the instant the key turns, not only at the years that follow.
senses.whyCN: 同一个抽象名词后缀既能指行为，也能指行为造成的结果，因此这个词也会看钥匙转动的那一刻，而不只是之后的漫长年月。

senses.title: Time served: the calendar inside
senses.definition: a length of time that a person spends confined under sentence
senses.definitionCN: 被判刑者在监所内度过的时长
senses.example: He completed a five-year incarceration before returning to his hometown.
senses.exampleCN: 他服完五年刑期后才回到家乡。
senses.why: Once the confined state is measured along a calendar it becomes a block of time, and people speak of serving it, finishing it or having it reduced.
senses.whyCN: 被关押的状态一旦沿着日历被丈量，就变成一段可以「服完」「结束」「缩短」的时间块。

senses.title: Mass incarceration: a social pattern
senses.titleCN: 作为社会现象的大规模监禁
senses.definition: the large-scale and sustained imprisonment of a group or population by a legal system
senses.definitionCN: 某一法律制度对某群体或大量人口长期、成规模地关押
senses.example: Scholars link mass incarceration to changes in sentencing law.
senses.exampleCN: 学者把大规模监禁与量刑法律的变动联系起来。
senses.why: One cell repeated across a whole society stops being a private fate: the same enclosure, multiplied by policy, is read as a pattern of the state.
senses.whyCN: 一间牢房被整个社会重复无数次，就不再是私人命运：同一个围合经政策放大，被读成国家层面的模式。

senses.title: Wrongful incarceration: the key held unjustly
senses.definition: confinement that lacks lawful justification or that later proves to have been unjust
senses.definitionCN: 缺少合法依据、或事后被证明不公正的关押
senses.example: The inquiry documented years of wrongful incarceration.
senses.exampleCN: 调查记录了多年的错误关押。
senses.why: The walls stay exactly the same, but the hand that holds the key is now judged: the noun adds the idea that the enclosure should never have closed.
senses.whyCN: 墙还是同样的墙，但握钥匙的那只手此时受到评判：这个词多出一层「这道门本不该关上」的意思。

senses.title: A cage without bars: figurative confinement
senses.definition: a condition of being shut in or trapped as though inside a cage, without any literal prison
senses.definitionCN: 并无真实监狱、却像被关在笼中一样被禁锢的处境
senses.example: Her illness became an incarceration of the mind as much as of the body.
senses.exampleCN: 她的病既困住了身体，也把心关了起来。
senses.why: The bars need not be iron: any circumstance that removes a person's room to move reproduces the shape of the cell, so the prison word serves as a metaphor.
senses.whyCN: 栏杆不必是铁做的：任何削减一个人活动余地的处境都复制了牢房的形状，于是这个监狱用语被借作比喻。

senses.title: Medical trapping: tissue held fast
senses.definition: in medicine, the trapping of a hernia or an organ in a narrow opening so that it cannot slip back
senses.definitionCN: 医学上疝或器官被卡在狭窄开口中、无法回纳的情形
senses.example: Imaging showed the incarceration of a loop of bowel.
senses.exampleCN: 影像显示一段肠管发生了嵌顿。
senses.why: Clinical language borrowed the prison image for a loop of tissue held where it does not belong, unable to return to its proper place.
senses.whyCN: 临床语言借用了监狱意象，指一段组织被卡在它不该待的位置、回不到原处。

senses.title: A line in the file: recorded legal fact
senses.titleCN: 档案里的一条法律事实
senses.definition: the recorded fact of having been held in custody, counted in law, employment checks and research
senses.definitionCN: 被收押的经历被记录在案，成为法律、雇佣审查与研究统计中的一项事实
senses.example: Applicants are not asked about their incarceration history.
senses.exampleCN: 申请表格不询问申请人的被监禁经历。
senses.why: Modern administration turns the state into a data field: once a jail stay is written down, the noun names a fact about a person's past rather than a place or a moment.
senses.whyCN: 现代行政把这种处境变成一个数据栏：一次关押被写下来之后，这个词指的就是一个人过去的一项事实，而不是某个地点或某个瞬间。

intro.en: Incarceration is built inside Latin: in- 'into' plus carcer 'prison or enclosure' plus -atio, a suffix for an action or its result. English took the finished noun rather than assembling it anew. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: incarceration 是在拉丁语内部构成的：表示「进入」的前缀、意为「牢笼、围栏」的词干，再加表动作或结果的名词后缀；英语是把成品整词接收过来，而不是自己重新拼装。年代均为约数。

items.en: Carcer was the Latin word for a prison, a walled pen and the starting stalls of a circus; the shared idea was an enclosure that holds something in.
items.cn: carcer 是拉丁语中「监狱、围起的圈栏、竞技场出发栅」的说法，共同点是把东西关在里面的围合结构。

items.en: The verb incarcerare added in- 'into' to carcer, so it meant to put a person inside the enclosure.
items.cn: 动词 incarcerare 在 carcer 之前加表示「进入」的成分，意思就是把人送进这个围合之中。

items.en: The abstract noun incarceratio named both the act and the resulting state, and English kept that double reach.
items.cn: 抽象名词 incarceratio 同时指动作与由此形成的状态，英语沿用的正是这种两可的覆盖范围。

items.en: English adopted the noun in the sixteenth century, at first for literal imprisonment under law.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪吸收了这个名词，最初指法律意义上的实际关押。

items.en: Later centuries extended it to mass imprisonment as policy and to the trapping of tissue in medicine.
items.cn: 后世又把它扩展到作为政策的大规模监禁，以及医学上组织被卡住的情形。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin prison stem or merely resembles the word in spelling; the second group offers plainer words for holding a person against their will.
note.cn: 第一组或与本词共享拉丁「牢笼」词干，或只是拼写相近；第二组是「违背意愿留住一个人」的更朴素说法。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to put a person in prison; it is the action behind the noun, not a different family.
entries.definitionCN: 表示把某人关进监狱的动词，是名词背后的动作，并非另一词族。

entries.definition: An adjective built on the Latin prison word, meaning of or relating to prisons and their system.
entries.definitionCN: 由拉丁「监狱」一词构成的形容词，指与监狱及其制度有关的。

entries.definition: The appearance of a god or an idea in bodily form; it looks close but comes from Latin caro 'flesh', so it is merely look-alike, not a relative.
entries.definitionCN: 神或观念以肉身显现；拼写相近，但出自拉丁 caro「肉」，只是形近，并非同源。

entries.definition: To burn something to ashes; it resembles the word in shape but comes from Latin cinis 'ash', so it is merely look-alike, not a relative.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物烧成灰；拼写相似，但出自拉丁 cinis「灰」，只是形近，并非同源。

entries.definition: The state of being in prison; it is plainer and more neutral than the formal noun.
entries.definitionCN: 在监狱中的状态；比这个正式名词更直白、更中性。

entries.definition: Being kept within limits, whether in a cell, a room or a bed; it need not involve a prison at all.
entries.definitionCN: 被限制在一定范围之内，可以是在牢房、房间或病床上；完全不必涉及监狱。

entries.definition: Being held in official custody, often before trial, with less weight of sentence than incarceration.
entries.definitionCN: 被官方羁押，常在审判之前，量刑意味比监禁弱。

entries.definition: Official keeping of a person by an authority; it names who holds the person rather than the place.
entries.definitionCN: 官方对某人的监管看护；它说的是谁扣着这个人，而不是关在哪里。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin prison word, the real prefix and suffix, and real derived words.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁「监狱」一词、真实的前缀与后缀，以及真实的派生词。

normal.en: Carcer is Latin for a prison or a walled pen, so incarceration is literally 'being put into a carcer'.
normal.cn: carcer 在拉丁语里是监狱或围栏，incarceration 字面就是「被放进一个 carcer」。

normal.en: The prefix in- means 'into': the person is placed inside the enclosure, not merely left near it.
normal.cn: 前缀表示「进入」：人被放进围合的内部，而不只是被留在旁边。

normal.en: The ending -ation names an action or a state, which is why the word covers both the locking up and the years after.
normal.cn: 后缀表示动作或状态，因此这个词既覆盖落锁关人，也覆盖之后的年月。

normal.en: The verb incarcerate and the adjective carceral share the stem, so learning one opens the others.
normal.cn: 动词 incarcerate 与形容词 carceral 共用同一词干，记住一个就能带出另一个。

normal.en: Fixed phrases keep the modern sense: mass incarceration, incarceration rate, a term of incarceration.
normal.cn: 固定搭配守住现代义：大规模监禁、监禁率、一段刑期。

abstract.en: Picture a heavy door closing behind you while the corridor lights go out one by one.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇沉重的门在你身后合上，走廊的灯一盏一盏熄灭。

abstract.en: Picture a bird in a cage with the key lying on a table outside the bars.
abstract.cn: 想象笼中有一只鸟，钥匙就放在栏杆外的桌上。

abstract.en: Picture a wall calendar with a cross scratched into it for every day inside.
abstract.cn: 想象墙上挂着一本日历，每过一天就刻下一道叉。

examples.en: The judge reduced the sentence, but incarceration still lasted eleven months.
examples.cn: 法官缩短了刑期，但监禁仍持续了十一个月。

examples.en: Researchers measure incarceration by counting people held on a given day.
examples.cn: 研究人员以某一天的在押人数来衡量监禁规模。

examples.en: Long after release, the years of incarceration still shaped his habits.
examples.cn: 获释很久之后，多年的监禁仍然塑造着他的习惯。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「硬卡塞进」——人被硬卡着塞进铁门里去，门一落锁只剩牢房 → 监禁、关押

root: 拉丁语表「进入」的前缀 + carcer「牢笼、围栏」→ incarcerare「关进牢中」→ incarceratio「关押（动作或状态）」；英语 incarceration 即「被关入牢笼的状态」，同族词有 incarcerate、carceral。

sensesIntro.en: All eight senses keep one picture: a body placed inside an enclosure it cannot leave. The noun then reads that enclosure as a state, as an act, as time served, as a social pattern, as an injustice, as a metaphor, as a medical trapping and finally as a recorded legal fact.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都守着同一幅画面：一个人被放进走不出去的围合之中。名词随后把这围合读成状态、读成动作、读成刑期、读成社会模式、读成冤屈、读成比喻、读成医学上的嵌顿，最后读成档案里的一条法律事实。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person standing behind a locked cell door, with the corridor outside stretching away.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人站在上锁的牢门之后，外面的走廊一直延伸出去。

branches.en: THE CONDITION: a person is inside the enclosure and cannot leave, which is the plainest reading of the noun.
branches.cn: 处境：人被围在里面、走不出来，这是名词最朴素的读法。

branches.en: THE ACT: the same noun looks at the moment the door is locked and names what the authority does.
branches.cn: 动作：同一个名词也看落锁的那一刻，指权威所做的事。

branches.en: TIME AND INJUSTICE: the state stretched over a calendar becomes a term, and when the key was wrongly held it becomes a grievance.
branches.cn: 时间与冤屈：状态沿日历拉长成刑期；若钥匙本不该被握着，就变成一桩冤屈。

branches.en: SCALE: one cell repeated across a society turns a private fate into a public pattern.
branches.cn: 规模：一间牢房在社会里被重复无数次，私人命运就成了公共模式。

branches.en: OUTSIDE THE PRISON: the cage can be illness, a trapped organ or a line in a file, as long as something is held fast.
branches.cn: 牢房之外：只要有什么被牢牢卡住，笼子就可以是疾病、被嵌顿的器官，或档案里的一行字。

intro.en: The word is assembled from a Latin prefix, a Latin noun stem and a Latin noun suffix; none of the three parts is native English.
intro.cn: 这个词由拉丁前缀、拉丁名词词干和拉丁名词后缀拼成，三者都不是英语本土成分。

latinIntro.en: Latin carcer 'prison' also yielded the verb incarcerare and the related adjective stem used in English carceral.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 carcer「监狱」还衍生出动词 incarcerare，以及英语 carceral 所用的相关形容词词干。

items.example: The prefix places the person inside the enclosure.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把人放进围合的内部。

items.example: The stem supplies the image of the cage.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干提供了笼子的意象。

items.meaning: the act of, or the state produced
items.meaningCN: 动作，或动作造成的状态
items.example: The suffix turns the verb into a name for what was done and what resulted.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把动词变成指「做了什么、落下什么结果」的名词。

items.meaning: the state or act of being imprisoned
items.example: The report measured incarceration in the county.
items.exampleCN: 报告统计了该县的监禁情况。

items.meaning: to put a person into prison
items.example: Courts incarcerate people under sentence.
items.exampleCN: 法院把被判刑的人关进监狱。

items.example: The incarcerated man wrote to his family.
items.exampleCN: 那名被关押的男子给家人写了信。

items.example: Scholars study the carceral system.
items.exampleCN: 学者研究这套监狱制度。

items.meaning: to make; to put into a state
items.example: The ending marks the word as a verb of action.
items.exampleCN: 这个结尾把该词标为表示动作的动词。

items.meaning: a measure of how many people are imprisoned
items.meaningCN: 衡量在押人口比例的指标
items.example: The incarceration rate rose sharply that decade.
items.exampleCN: 那十年间监禁率急剧上升。

latinEntries.meaning: the starting gates of a circus

definition_zh: 监禁；关押；把…关进监狱；（引申）把…禁锢在狭小处
definition_en: to put a person into a prison or jail, or to confine someone or something as if in a cage
core_image: 狱警扣住人的手腕，把人推过铁门，门闩在身后落下
scene: 临时法庭设在镇礼堂，判决一念完，警员就扣住被告的手腕往囚车方向带。Once the verdict was read, the officers moved to incarcerate the man in the city jail.
sceneCN: 这里指「依法把人收押进监狱」这一动作，对应第 1 个义项：由有权机关将判刑之人送进监所；句意为判决宣读后，警员随即将被告押往市监狱关押。画面要点：镇礼堂里的临时法庭、囚车、扣住手腕的动作。

pos.zh: 监禁；关押（及物动词，宾语为被关押的人或动物）

derivatives.zh: 加名词后缀（源自拉丁语，表动作或状态）→ 由「把人关进去」这一动作转为「被关押的状态或关押行为本身」
加过去分词词尾（转作形容词）→ 由「已被关进去」转为「处于被关押状态的」
词干 carcer（拉丁「牢笼」）加形容词后缀→ 由「牢笼」转为「与监狱制度有关的」
incarceration 与 rate 复合 → 由「监禁」转为「在押人口比例的统计指标」

senses.title: Sentenced to the cell: the court sends a person in
senses.titleCN: 判刑之后把人送进牢房
senses.definition: to place a person who has been sentenced into a prison so that they can no longer move freely
senses.definitionCN: 把已被判刑的人送进监狱，使其不能再自由行动
senses.example: The court ordered the state to incarcerate the offender for six years.
senses.exampleCN: 法院命令州政府将该罪犯监禁六年。
senses.why: Latin in- 'into' plus carcer 'prison' plus a verb ending gives the plain physical act: a body is moved from outside the walls to inside them.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语中表示「进入」的成分、意为「牢笼」的词干，再加动词词尾，给的就是这个直白的身体动作：把一个人从墙外移到墙内。

senses.title: Custody before trial: held while the case waits
senses.titleCN: 案件未结时的先行羁押
senses.definition: to keep an accused person locked up while legal proceedings are still pending
senses.definitionCN: 在法律程序尚未结束时把被指控者关押起来
senses.example: The suspect was incarcerated pending a bail hearing.
senses.exampleCN: 嫌疑人在保释听证之前一直被关押。
senses.why: The same enclosure can close before any verdict, when the law holds the body to ensure that it will appear in court.
senses.whyCN: 同一道围合可以在判决之前就关上：法律扣住这个身体，是为了确保他到时候会出现在法庭上。

senses.title: Any closed room: shut in a ward or a camp
senses.titleCN: 关进病房、营房等任何封闭之处
senses.definition: to confine a person within a room, ward, cell or camp that they are not free to leave
senses.definitionCN: 把某人限制在房间、病房、牢房或营地之内，使其不能自由离开
senses.example: Patients with the fever were incarcerated in an isolation ward.
senses.exampleCN: 发烧的病人被隔离在单独的病房里。
senses.why: The prison wall is one species of a larger kind: any boundary a person cannot cross performs the same work, so the verb follows the body wherever it is enclosed.
senses.whyCN: 监狱的墙只是更大一类东西中的一种：任何一个人越不过的界线都在做同一件事，所以这个动词跟着被围住的身体走，不管围住它的是什么。

senses.title: Barred cages: animals put behind wire
senses.definition: to keep an animal inside a cage, pen or other enclosure
senses.definitionCN: 把动物关在笼子、圈栏或其他围合之中
senses.example: The shelter incarcerated the stray dogs in narrow cages.
senses.exampleCN: 收容所把流浪狗关进窄小的笼子里。
senses.why: Animals are put behind bars too, and the verb attaches to the enclosing act itself, whether or not a law or a sentence is involved.
senses.whyCN: 动物也会被关在栏杆之后，这个动词附着在「围起来」这个动作本身上，并不需要有法律或判决参与。

senses.title: No iron bars: trapped by circumstance
senses.titleCN: 被处境困住的比喻用法
senses.definition: to fix a person in a situation, role or habit from which escape seems impossible
senses.definitionCN: 把某人固定在一种似乎无法逃脱的处境、角色或习惯之中
senses.example: Debt had incarcerated him in a job he hated.
senses.exampleCN: 债务把他困在一份他厌恶的工作里。
senses.why: Once the bars are no longer physical, the verb describes any arrangement that removes a person's room to move, and the prison becomes a figure of speech.
senses.whyCN: 当栏杆不再是实物，这个动词就用来描述任何削减一个人活动余地的安排，监狱也随之变成一种修辞。

senses.title: Clinical trapping: a hernia held fast
senses.definition: of a hernia or organ, to become held fast in a narrow opening so that it cannot return
senses.definitionCN: 疝或器官被卡在狭窄开口中、无法回纳
senses.example: The scan showed a loop of bowel incarcerated in the hernia.
senses.exampleCN: 扫描显示一段肠管嵌顿在疝口里。
senses.why: The prison image survives in clinical language for tissue caught in a gap, held where it does not belong and unable to slip back.
senses.whyCN: 监狱意象在临床语言里延续下来，指组织被卡在一个缝隙里，待在不该待的地方，也滑不回去。

senses.title: Policy at scale: thousands locked away
senses.titleCN: 成规模地关押一整群人
senses.definition: to put large numbers of people from a group into prison as a matter of state policy
senses.definitionCN: 作为国家政策把某一群体中的大批人关进监狱
senses.example: The regime incarcerated thousands of dissidents.
senses.exampleCN: 该政权关押了数以千计的异议者。
senses.why: The single act repeated across a state becomes a policy, and the verb takes on the weight of the system standing behind each locked door.
senses.whyCN: 同一个动作在一个国家里被重复无数次就变成政策，这个动词也因此带上了每扇锁着的门背后那套体制的分量。

senses.title: The formal order: legal commitment to jail
senses.titleCN: 法律程序上的正式收押
senses.definition: in legal usage, to commit a person to jail by formal order
senses.definitionCN: 在法律用语中，依正式命令将某人收押入狱
senses.example: The magistrate incarcerated the defendant until the hearing.
senses.exampleCN: 治安法官将被告收押至听证之日。
senses.why: Law needs a name for the procedural step itself, separate from the sentence that may follow, so the verb also means the formal act of committing.
senses.whyCN: 法律需要给程序上的这一步一个名称，把它与之后可能作出的判决分开，因此这个动词也指正式的收押行为。

intro.en: Incarcerate comes from Latin incarcerare, itself in- 'into' plus carcer 'prison' plus the verb ending -are. English borrowed the verb, and its noun incarceration adds the Latin action ending. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: incarcerate 来自拉丁 incarcerare，后者由表示「进入」的成分、意为「牢笼」的词干与动词词尾构成；英语借入这个动词，其名词 incarceration 又加上表动作的拉丁后缀。年代均为约数。

items.en: Carcer named a prison, a walled pen and the starting stalls of the circus, all enclosures that hold something inside.
items.cn: carcer 指监狱、围起的圈栏，也指竞技场的出发栅，都是把东西关在里面的围合结构。

items.en: In- 'into' was added to the noun, producing a verb that meant to put a person inside the enclosure.
items.cn: 表示「进入」的成分加在这个名词前，造出一个意为「把人送进围合之中」的动词。

items.en: The past participle incarcerated meant having been put in prison, and it later supplied the English adjective.
items.cn: 过去分词意为「已被关进牢中」，后来为英语的形容词形式提供了来源。

items.en: The verb entered English in the sixteenth century, at first in legal writing for committing a person to prison.
items.cn: 这个动词在十六世纪进入英语，最初见于法律文书中，指将人收押入狱。

items.en: Modern usage extends the verb to figurative traps, to clinical trapping of tissue, to animals and to mass imprisonment as policy.
items.cn: 现代用法把这个动词扩展到比喻性的困境、医学上的组织嵌顿、动物关押，以及作为政策的大规模监禁。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin prison stem or merely resembles the verb in spelling; the second group offers plainer verbs for holding a person against their will.
note.cn: 第一组或与本词共享拉丁「牢笼」词干，或只是拼写相近；第二组是「违背意愿留住一个人」的更朴素动词。

entries.definition: The noun for the state or act of being imprisoned; it is the result or the deed behind the verb, not another family.
entries.definitionCN: 指被监禁的状态或行为的名称，是这个动词所做的事或其结果，并非另一词族。

entries.definition: Of or relating to prisons; it shares the Latin prison stem but describes the system rather than the act.
entries.definitionCN: 与监狱有关的；共享拉丁「监狱」词干，但描述的是制度而非动作。

entries.definition: The appearance of a god or an idea in bodily form; it resembles the verb but comes from Latin caro 'flesh', so it is merely look-alike, not a relative.
entries.definitionCN: 神或观念以肉身显现；与这个动词形近，但出自拉丁 caro「肉」，只是形近，并非同源。

entries.definition: To burn something to ashes; it shares the shape of the verb but comes from Latin cinis 'ash', so it is merely look-alike, not a relative.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物烧成灰；与此词形状相近，但出自拉丁 cinis「灰」，只是形近，并非同源。

entries.definition: To put a person in prison; it is the everyday verb for the same act and carries no Latin weight.
entries.definitionCN: 把某人关进监狱；这是同一个动作的日常说法，不带拉丁语的厚重感。

entries.definition: To put a person in a local jail, usually for a shorter or pre-trial stay; it names a smaller institution.
entries.definitionCN: 把某人关进地方看守所，通常是较短或候审期间的关押，指的是较小的机构。

entries.definition: To keep a person in official custody, often briefly and before any charge is settled; it stresses holding, not sentencing.
entries.definitionCN: 把某人置于官方羁押之下，往往时间较短、指控尚未定论；强调扣留而非判刑。

entries.definition: To keep a person or thing within limits; it works for rooms and bodies alike and need not imply a prison.
entries.definitionCN: 把人或物限制在一定范围之内；房间与身体都适用，且不必含监狱之意。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin prison stem, the real prefix, the real verb ending and real derived forms.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁「牢笼」词干、真实的前缀、真实的动词词尾，以及真实的派生形式。

normal.en: Carcer is the Latin prison, so incarcerate is 'to put someone into the carcer'.
normal.cn: carcer 就是拉丁语的监狱，incarcerate 即「把某人放进 carcer」。

normal.en: The prefix in- marks direction: the person goes into the enclosure.
normal.cn: 前缀标出方向：人是往围合里面去的。

normal.en: The noun incarceration and the adjective carceral share the same stem, so one word teaches three.
normal.cn: 名词 incarceration 与形容词 carceral 共用同一词干，记住一个就带出三个。

normal.en: Fixed phrases show the legal frame: be incarcerated for years, incarcerate a defendant, incarcerate without trial.
normal.cn: 固定搭配展现法律框架：被关押多年、收押被告、未经审判即关押。

normal.en: The verb ending -ate marks an action, so this word names the act while the noun names the state.
normal.cn: 动词词尾标出动作，因此这个词指动作，而名词指状态。

abstract.en: Picture handcuffs clicking shut and an iron door swinging behind them.
abstract.cn: 想象手铐咔哒一声扣上，随后一扇铁门在背后合拢。

abstract.en: Picture a bird lifted gently and placed inside a cage, the hand withdrawing.
abstract.cn: 想象一只鸟被轻轻捧起放进笼子，随后那只手抽了回去。

abstract.en: Picture a plant growing inside a glass bottle, its leaves pressed against the wall.
abstract.cn: 想象一株植物长在玻璃瓶里，叶子被顶在瓶壁上。

examples.en: The judge may incarcerate the offender for up to ten years.
examples.cn: 法官可以将该罪犯监禁最多十年。

examples.en: Thousands were incarcerated without a hearing.
examples.cn: 数以千计的人未经听证就被关押。

examples.en: Poverty can incarcerate a family in one neighbourhood for decades.
examples.cn: 贫困能把一个家庭困在同一个街区几十年。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阴卡塞进」——把人硬卡着塞进铁门里去，门闩一落就只剩牢房 → 监禁、关押

root: 拉丁语表「进入」的前缀 + carcer「牢笼、围栏」+ 动词词尾 → incarcerare「关进牢中」；英语 incarcerate 即「把人送进牢笼」，其名词 incarceration 再加拉丁语中表动作或状态的词尾。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one action: moving a body across a boundary and locking it there. The verb applies that action to sentenced prisoners, to suspects awaiting trial, to patients, to animals, to trapped tissue, to people fixed in circumstances, to whole groups and finally to the formal court order.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都跟随同一个动作：把一个人移过某道界线并锁在里面。这个动词依次把它用在已判刑者、候审嫌疑人、病人、动物、被卡住的组织、被困在处境中的人、整群的人，最后落在法院的正式收押令上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand on a wrist, a body pushed through an iron door, and a bolt falling into place.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手扣住手腕，把人推过铁门，门闩随之落下。

branches.en: THE LITERAL ACT: a sentenced body is moved inside the walls, and the door is shut.
branches.cn: 字面动作：被判刑的身体被移进墙内，门随即关上。

branches.en: BEFORE THE VERDICT: the same lock may close while the case waits or by a magistrate's formal order.
branches.cn: 判决之前：同一把锁可以在案件待审时落下，也可以依治安法官的正式命令落下。

branches.en: OTHER WALLS: a ward, a camp or a cell serves the same purpose once crossing it is forbidden.
branches.cn: 别的墙：病房、营地或牢房，只要越不过去，就在起同样的作用。

branches.en: NON-HUMAN AND CLINICAL: cages hold animals, and narrow openings hold tissue fast.
branches.cn: 非人与临床：笼子关住动物，狭窄的缝隙卡住组织。

branches.en: WITHOUT BARS AND AT SCALE: debt can be a cage, and a state can lock up thousands.
branches.cn: 无栏与成规模：债务可以是笼子，国家也可以关押成千上万人。

intro.en: The verb is assembled from a Latin prefix, a Latin noun stem and a Latin verb ending, and English added its own noun and adjective forms afterwards.
intro.cn: 这个动词由拉丁前缀、拉丁名词词干和拉丁动词词尾拼成，英语随后又加上自己的名词与形容词形式。

latinIntro.en: Latin carcer 'prison' produced incarcerare 'to imprison' and incarceratio 'imprisonment', and English built carceral from the same stem.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 carcer「监狱」衍生出 incarcerare「监禁」与 incarceratio「监禁」，英语又用同一词干造出 carceral。

items.example: The prefix directs the action inward.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把动作指向内部。

items.example: The stem supplies the image of the cage.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干提供了笼子的意象。

items.meaning: to make; to put into a state
items.example: The ending marks the word as a verb.
items.exampleCN: 这个结尾把该词标为动词。

items.meaning: to put a person into prison
items.example: The officers moved to incarcerate the man.
items.exampleCN: 警员随即将那名男子收押。

items.example: Incarceration lasted nearly a year.
items.exampleCN: 关押持续了将近一年。

items.example: The incarcerated writer lost his appeal.
items.exampleCN: 那名被关押的作家上诉失败。

items.example: Incarcerating offenders is only one part of sentencing.
items.exampleCN: 关押罪犯只是量刑的一部分。

items.example: The study describes a carceral society.
items.exampleCN: 这项研究描述了一个监狱化的社会。

items.meaning: the act of, or the state produced
items.meaningCN: 动作，或动作造成的状态
items.example: The suffix turns the verb into a noun of result.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把动词变成表结果的名词。

definition_zh: 使康复；使恢复功能；改造罪犯使之重返社会；恢复名誉、权利或职位；使建筑物、生态恢复良好状态
definition_en: to restore a person to health, ability or a normal place in society, or to bring something back into good condition
core_image: 康复室里，病人双手扶着平行杠重新学迈步，治疗师在旁护着腰
scene: 事故之后，那名木工半年上不了脚手架，康复中心替他排了一套从抬腿到负重的训练。The clinic designed a slow programme to rehabilitate the injured carpenter.
sceneCN: 这里指「通过训练使伤者重新恢复身体功能」，对应第 2 个义项：借助治疗与反复练习，把失去的动作能力一点点建回来；句意为康复中心为受伤的木工安排了一套循序渐进的训练。画面要点：平行杠、治疗师、重新迈出的第一步。

pos.zh: 使康复；改造；恢复（及物动词，宾语可为人、机构、建筑或生态）

derivatives.zh: 加名词后缀（源自拉丁语，表动作或结果）→ 由「使恢复能力」转为「康复、复权的整个过程」
加形容词后缀（表倾向或功能）→ 由「使恢复」转为「有助于康复的」
加过去分词词尾（转作形容词）→ 由「已使恢复」转为「已康复或已恢复资格的」
由拉丁词干（源自 habilis「能干的」）加动词词尾（源自拉丁语，表「使……」）→ 由「能干」转为「使具备能力、使合用」
habilitate 加名词后缀（表动作或结果）→ 由「使有能力」转为「取得资格的过程」
源自拉丁 habilis「易于掌握的、能干的」加名词后缀（表性质）→ 由「能干」转为「能力」这一性质

senses.title: Back to health: a sick body made well
senses.titleCN: 让病后的身体回到健康
senses.definition: to bring a person back to health after illness or injury through care and treatment
senses.definitionCN: 通过照料与治疗，使人在患病或受伤之后恢复健康
senses.example: The team worked for months to rehabilitate patients after the fire.
senses.exampleCN: 团队工作了数月，帮助火灾后的病人康复。
senses.why: The prefix re- means 'again, back', and the Latin base means 'to make able', so the core is not punishment but the return of a capacity that had been lost.
senses.whyCN: 前缀表示「再、回」，拉丁词干意为「使有能力」，因此这个词的核心不是惩罚，而是让一项失去的能力回来。

senses.title: Retraining a joint or limb: step by step
senses.titleCN: 一点一点练回关节与肢体
senses.definition: to train a specific movement or faculty until it works again
senses.definitionCN: 针对某一动作或机能反复训练，直到它重新正常工作
senses.example: She practised daily to rehabilitate her injured shoulder.
senses.exampleCN: 她每天练习，让受伤的肩膀恢复功能。
senses.why: The capacity is concrete: a shoulder, a knee, a step. The verb then names the slow drill that brings the movement back rather than the abstract idea of health.
senses.whyCN: 这里的能力很具体：一个肩膀、一只膝盖、一步路。动词因此指把这动作练回来的缓慢训练，而不是抽象的健康概念。

senses.title: Reform for society: not merely punish
senses.titleCN: 为重返社会而改造，而非只加惩罚
senses.definition: to prepare a convicted person for ordinary life through education, work and treatment rather than mere punishment
senses.definitionCN: 以教育、劳动与治疗帮助已定罪者过普通生活，而不是只施加惩罚
senses.example: The prison runs classes to rehabilitate young offenders.
senses.exampleCN: 这所监狱开设课程，帮助少年犯改过自新。
senses.why: A person who has lost their place in society is treated like a person who has lost a function: the task is to restore the ability to live among others, not to add pain.
senses.whyCN: 失去社会位置的人，被当作失去一项功能的人来处理：任务是恢复他与别人共同生活的能力，而不是增加痛苦。

senses.title: Rights and name restored: the legal sense
senses.titleCN: 恢复权利与名誉的法律义
senses.definition: to give a person back a former legal standing, office or good name
senses.definitionCN: 把某人原先的法律地位、职位或名誉归还给他
senses.example: The decree rehabilitated the officers who had been dismissed.
senses.exampleCN: 这项法令为那些被免职的军官恢复了名誉。
senses.why: This is the oldest use: re- means back, and the person is returned to a position that had been taken away, so the word speaks of standing rather than of the body.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的用法：前缀意为「回」，人被送回一个曾被剥夺的位置，因此这个词讲的是地位，而不是身体。

senses.title: Bricks made usable: buildings brought back
senses.definition: to repair and upgrade a building, district or facility so that it is usable again
senses.definitionCN: 修缮并提升建筑、街区或设施，使其重新可以使用
senses.example: The city plans to rehabilitate the old dock warehouses.
senses.exampleCN: 市政府计划修缮旧码头的仓库。
senses.why: The object shifts from a body to bricks, but the shape of the act is the same: something fallen into disrepair is made fit for use again.
senses.whyCN: 对象从身体换成了砖块，但动作的形状没变：一样陷入失修的东西被重新弄得合于使用。

senses.title: Land healed: an ecosystem restored
senses.titleCN: 让土地与生态恢复健康
senses.definition: to return damaged land, water or habitat to a healthy working state
senses.definitionCN: 使受损的土地、水体或栖息地回到健康的运转状态
senses.example: Volunteers rehabilitated the strip mine into a wetland.
senses.exampleCN: 志愿者把露天矿坑修复成了湿地。
senses.why: Land, too, can lose its functions; the verb treats soil and water as a system whose capacities must be brought back, just as a body's are.
senses.whyCN: 土地也会失去它的功能；这个动词把土壤与水当作一套必须把能力恢复过来的系统，正如对待身体一样。

senses.title: Back in the post: an official reinstated
senses.titleCN: 让官员回到原来的职位
senses.definition: to restore an official to a post, rank or privilege that had been removed
senses.definitionCN: 使官员回到曾被撤销的职位、军衔或特权
senses.example: The board voted to rehabilitate the suspended director.
senses.exampleCN: 董事会投票决定恢复被停职董事的职位。
senses.why: When the lost thing is a seat at the table, the verb moves from bodily capacity to institutional membership, yet the 'making able again' remains.
senses.whyCN: 当失去的东西是桌边的一个席位，这个词就从身体能力转向制度中的成员资格，但「重新使有能力」这一层仍然在。

senses.title: A good name regained: ideas and works
senses.titleCN: 让作品与观念重获好评
senses.definition: to make a neglected or discredited idea, word or artwork respected again
senses.definitionCN: 使被冷落或已被否定的观念、词语或作品重新受到尊重
senses.example: Later critics rehabilitated the painter's early work.
senses.exampleCN: 后来的评论家为这位画家早期的作品恢复了声誉。
senses.why: Reputation is another capacity that can be lost, and the verb extends to anything whose good name has been taken away, from a person to a painting.
senses.whyCN: 声誉也是一种会失去的能力，这个词于是扩展到任何被夺去好评的东西，从一个人到一幅画都可以。

intro.en: Rehabilitate is not a native English construction: it comes from Medieval Latin rehabilitare, itself re- 'again, back' plus habilitare 'to make able', a verb from habilis 'apt, easily handled'. The same family contains ability and habilitate. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: rehabilitate 不是英语本土构造，而来自中世纪拉丁 rehabilitare：由表示「再、回」的前缀加 habilitare「使有能力」构成，后者又出自 habilis「易于掌握的、能干的」；同一词族还有 ability 与 habilitate。年代均为约数。

items.en: Habilis meant apt, handy or easily handled, an adjective built on habere 'to hold'; the idea was fitness for use.
items.cn: habilis 意为易于掌握的、顺手的、能干的，是由 habere「持有」构成的形容词，核心意思是「合用」。

items.en: Habilitare turned the adjective into a verb meaning to make able or to fit something for a purpose.
items.cn: habilitare 把这个形容词变成动词，意为使有能力，或使某物适合某一用途。

items.en: Re- 'again, back' was added to habilitare, and the compound was used in law and church language for restoring a person to a former right or rank.
items.cn: 表示「再、回」的前缀加在 habilitare 上，这个复合词用于法律与教会语言，指把某人恢复到原有的权利或地位。

items.en: English took the word in the sixteenth century, first in legal and ecclesiastical use for restoring standing.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪吸收了这个词，最初用于法律与教会语境，指恢复地位。

items.en: The medical and social senses developed later: restoring a patient's body, then preparing an offender for ordinary life.
items.cn: 医学与社会义后来才发展出来：先指恢复病人的身体，再指为罪犯重返普通生活作准备。

items.en: Contemporary usage extends the verb to buildings, districts, ecosystems and the reputation of ideas or works.
items.cn: 当代用法把这个动词扩展到建筑、街区、生态系统，以及观念或作品的声誉。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin ability stem or merely resembles the word in spelling; the second group offers near alternatives for bringing something back to a good state.
note.cn: 第一组或与本词共享拉丁「能力」词干，或只是拼写相近；第二组是「把某物带回良好状态」的近义替代。

entries.definition: To make someone able or fit; it is the base verb without the 'again' prefix, so it lacks the idea of restoring something already lost.
entries.definitionCN: 使某人有能力或合于用途；这是去掉「再」这一前缀的底层动词，因此不含「把已失去之物恢复过来」的意思。

entries.definition: To make someone weak; it is built on the same Latin ability adjective but through a prefix of removal, so it undoes capacity instead of restoring it.
entries.definitionCN: 使某人衰弱；它由同一个拉丁「能力」形容词经表「去除」的前缀构成，因此是拆掉能力而非恢复能力。

entries.definition: To sum up the main points again; it shares the re- prefix and the -ate ending but comes from Latin caput 'head', so it is merely look-alike, not a relative.
entries.definitionCN: 再次概括要点；它与本词共享「再」这一前缀和动词词尾，但出自拉丁 caput「头」，只是形近，并非同源。

entries.definition: The informal short form of rehabilitation, used chiefly for treatment programmes and centres.
entries.definitionCN: rehabilitation 的口语缩略形式，主要用于治疗项目与康复中心。

entries.definition: To bring something back to a former condition; it is broader and does not specify ability, health or standing.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物带回原先的状态；范围更宽，不特别指明能力、健康或地位。

entries.definition: To put a person back into a post or right; it covers only the institutional sense of the word.
entries.definitionCN: 把某人放回职位或权利之中；只覆盖本词的制度义。

entries.definition: To bring a person back into a group or society; it names the social goal rather than the training that achieves it.
entries.definitionCN: 把某人带回群体或社会之中；它指社会目标，而不是达成目标的训练。

entries.definition: To improve a person or institution by removing faults; for offenders it stresses moral change, while this word stresses restored capacity.
entries.definitionCN: 通过去除毛病来改善人或制度；用于罪犯时强调品德转变，而本词强调能力的恢复。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin ability stem, the real 'again' prefix and real derived words such as ability and habilitate.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁「能力」词干、真实的「再」前缀，以及 ability、habilitate 等真实派生词。

normal.en: Habilis means apt or able, and the English word ability comes from the same Latin adjective.
normal.cn: habilis 意为能干的、合用的，英语 ability 正出自同一个拉丁形容词。

normal.en: The prefix re- means again or back, so the word says the ability is brought back.
normal.cn: 前缀意为「再、回」，所以这个词说的是把能力带回来。

normal.en: Habilitate is the base verb 'to make able'; rehabilitate adds the return to a former state.
normal.cn: habilitate 是底层动词「使有能力」，rehabilitate 则再加「回到原先状态」这一层。

normal.en: Fixed phrases show the range: rehabilitate offenders, rehabilitate a building, drug rehabilitation.
normal.cn: 固定搭配展现范围：改造罪犯、修缮建筑、戒毒康复。

normal.en: The noun rehabilitation and the adjective rehabilitative both keep the idea of making fit again.
normal.cn: 名词 rehabilitation 与形容词 rehabilitative 都保留「重新弄得合用」这一意思。

abstract.en: Picture a patient gripping parallel bars and lifting one foot again.
abstract.cn: 想象病人握住平行杠，再一次把一只脚抬起来。

abstract.en: Picture a released prisoner handed a work badge at a factory gate.
abstract.cn: 想象一名获释的服刑人员在工厂门口接过工牌。

abstract.en: Picture a ruined brick warehouse with fresh scaffolding around it.
abstract.cn: 想象一座破败的砖砌仓库四周搭起了新的脚手架。

examples.en: Therapy helped rehabilitate her knee after the operation.
examples.cn: 治疗帮助她的膝盖在手术后恢复功能。

examples.en: Programmes that rehabilitate offenders cost less than long sentences.
examples.cn: 改造罪犯的项目比长期监禁花费更少。

examples.en: The trust hopes to rehabilitate the discredited theory with new evidence.
examples.cn: 该基金会希望用新证据为这个已被否定的理论恢复声誉。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞哈比立忒」——瑞气回来，比着平行杠把腿立起来，人又能站直了 → 康复、复权

root: 拉丁语表「回、再」的前缀 + habilitare「使有能力」（← habilis「易于掌握的、能干的」← habere「持有」）→ 中世纪拉丁 rehabilitare「使恢复能力与资格」；同族词有 ability、habilitate、rehabilitation。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses keep the same movement: something that once had a capacity lost it, and the verb brings that capacity back. The capacity may be health, a movement, a place in society, a legal right, a building's usefulness, a landscape's fertility, a post or a good name.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项守着同一个动作：某样东西本来具有一项能力，后来失去了，这个动词把它带回来。这项能力可以是健康、一个动作、社会位置、法律权利、建筑的可用性、土地的生机、一个职位，或一份好评。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: hands on parallel bars, one foot lifted again after a long pause.
core.cn: 核心意象：双手扶住平行杠，停歇很久之后那只脚又一次抬起来。

branches.en: THE BODY: health returns first as a general condition, then as a single joint or step trained back into use.
branches.cn: 身体：健康先以整体状态回来，随后又以某个关节或某一步被练回可用。

branches.en: THE PLACE AMONG OTHERS: an offender is fitted for ordinary life, and an official is put back into a lost post.
branches.cn: 人群中的位置：让罪犯重新适合普通生活，也让官员回到失去的职位。

branches.en: THE LEGAL NAME: rights and reputation are handed back by formal decision.
branches.cn: 法律上的名分：权利与名誉经正式决定被归还。

branches.en: THE MADE WORLD: bricks and land are repaired until they can work again.
branches.cn: 人造与自然之物：砖石与土地被修整到能重新运转。

branches.en: THE GOOD NAME OF THINGS: even a discredited idea or artwork can be given its standing back.
branches.cn: 事物的好评：连一个被否定的观念或作品，也能重新得到它应有的地位。

intro.en: Rehabilitate is assembled from Latin pieces: a prefix of return, an adjective stem meaning able, and a verb ending, with English noun and adjective suffixes added later.
intro.cn: rehabilitate 由拉丁成分拼成：一个表示「回、再」的前缀、一个意为「能干」的形容词词干，以及一个动词词尾；英语的名词与形容词后缀是后来才加上去的。

latinIntro.en: Latin habilis 'apt' came from habere 'to hold', and it also produced habilitare, rehabilitare and the English word ability.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 habilis「合用的、能干的」出自 habere「持有」，它还衍生出 habilitare、rehabilitare 以及英语的 ability。

items.meaning: again; back to a former state
items.example: The prefix marks the return of something that was lost.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标出「失去之物重新回来」。

items.example: The stem describes a person or thing that can be handled well.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干描述一个人或物能被好好使用。

items.structure: stem of Latin habilitare (to make able)
items.example: The stem carries the act of fitting someone for a task.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干承载「使人适合某项任务」的动作。

items.meaning: to make; to cause to be
items.meaningCN: 使成为；使处于某种状态
items.example: The ending marks the word as a verb.
items.exampleCN: 这个结尾把该词标为动词。

items.example: The clinic aims to rehabilitate each patient.
items.exampleCN: 康复中心的目标是让每位病人恢复功能。

items.example: Rehabilitation takes many months after a severe injury.
items.exampleCN: 重伤之后康复需要许多个月。

items.example: The ward offers rehabilitative care.
items.exampleCN: 该病区提供康复性照护。

items.example: The rehabilitated building reopened as a school.
items.exampleCN: 修缮后的建筑作为学校重新开放。

items.meaning: the process of making someone able
items.example: Habilitation precedes independent work.
items.exampleCN: 先具备能力，才能独立工作。

items.example: The injury did not damage her ability to walk.
items.exampleCN: 这次受伤没有损害她行走的能力。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 合用的；易于掌握的；能干的

latinEntries.meaning: to restore to a former right or capacity
latinEntries.meaningCN: 恢复原有的权利或能力

definition_zh: 公正；公平；正义；司法（制度）；法官；（应得的）赏罚；正当的理由
definition_en: the quality of giving every party its due by one and the same measure, and the system or the person that applies it
core_image: 一架黄铜天平立在法台正中，两端托盘各放一份证物，梁臂停在水平线上，谁都不许偷偷加砝码
scene: 法庭的木质天平摆在书记官手边，两端托盘里各放一份证物，梁臂停在正中，一丝不偏。The magistrate insisted that the ruling rest on justice rather than on the rank of the parties.
sceneCN: 这里指「用同一把尺子对待每一方」的公正，对应第 1 个义项：衡量标准不因身份高低而改变；句意为治安法官坚持裁决要依据公正，而不是依据双方的地位。画面要点：法台上的黄铜天平、两只托盘、水平的梁臂。

pos.zh: 公正；公平；正义（不可数，指性质）
司法；司法制度（不可数，指一整套机关与程序）
法官（可数，作头衔时首字母大写）
