collocations.zh: 对……作出相称的评价或呈现；充分展现

forms.label: 不可数名词（性质与制度）
复数（指法官或具体事例）

derivatives.zh: 去掉表性质的名词词尾而取形容词形 → 由「公正这一性质」转为「具备该性质的、正直的」
just 加副词后缀（古英语中表方式）→ 由「公正的」转为「以公正的方式」
拉丁 iustus 加表「使成」的动词词尾（由 facere「做」而来）→ 由「公正」转为「使显得正当、为……辩护」
justify 加名词后缀（源自拉丁语，表动作或结果）→ 由「使正当」转为「正当的理由或说明」
出自拉丁 iudicialis，源自 iudex「宣示法权者」，与 ius 同族 → 由「法权」转为「审判的、法庭的」
出自拉丁 iurare「宣誓」，与 ius 同族 → 由「法权」转为「宣誓后参与裁断的一群人」

senses.title: Even-handed treatment: the same measure for all
senses.definition: the practice of applying one and the same rule to every party, whatever their rank or advantage
senses.definitionCN: 对每一方都适用同一套规则的做法，不论其地位高低或占不占优势
senses.example: The tenants asked for justice in the way the landlord raised the rents.
senses.exampleCN: 房客们要求房东在涨租这件事上做到公平。
senses.why: The core image is a level beam: the pans may hold different things, but the arm rests level only when one measure governs both sides.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是一根水平的秤梁：两只托盘装的东西可以不同，但只有当同一把尺子管住两边时，梁臂才停得平。

senses.title: Rightness read as a moral principle
senses.definition: the principle that each person ought to receive what is morally owed to them
senses.definitionCN: 每个人都应当得到其在道义上应得之物的原则
senses.example: They saw the struggle as a demand for justice, not for revenge.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把这场抗争看作对正义的诉求，而不是为了报复。
senses.why: Once the level beam is read as a law of the world rather than a tool in one courtroom, even-handedness becomes a principle against which wrongs are measured.
senses.whyCN: 当水平的秤梁被读成世间的法则、而不只是某间法庭里的工具，一视同仁就升为一条原则，用来衡量一切不义。

senses.title: The courts and the legal machinery
senses.definition: the system of courts, laws and procedures through which lawful claims are heard and settled
senses.definitionCN: 受理并裁断合法诉求的法院、法律与程序所构成的体系
senses.example: The reform promised faster access to justice for poor defendants.
senses.exampleCN: 这项改革承诺让贫困被告更快地获得司法救济。
senses.why: A principle needs an instrument: the same balance is hung in a permanent building, given clerks, rules and dockets, and the quality turns into an institution.
senses.whyCN: 原则需要一件器具：同一架天平被挂进固定的建筑，配上书记员、规则与案卷，这种性质就变成了制度。

senses.title: The judge who keeps the beam level
senses.definition: a judge, especially of a high court, referred to by this title
senses.definitionCN: 法官，尤指高等法院的法官，可用这一头衔来称呼
senses.example: The justice questioned whether the search had been lawful.
senses.exampleCN: 这位法官质疑那次搜查是否合法。
senses.why: The person who steadies the beam comes to be named by the beam: the quality is handed over to its keeper.
senses.whyCN: 稳住秤梁的人，最后被秤梁本身来命名：性质被转交给了它的看守者。

senses.title: The outcome each side has earned
senses.definition: the reward or punishment that a person's conduct deserves
senses.definitionCN: 一个人的行为所应得的奖赏或惩罚
senses.example: After four years the family finally saw justice done in the sentencing.
senses.exampleCN: 四年之后，这家人终于在判决中看到公正得到伸张。
senses.why: The beam tips once the pans are filled; a scale does not merely compare, it pays out, and the settled position is the deserved outcome.
senses.whyCN: 托盘装满之后，秤梁就倾斜；天平不只是比较，它还结算，停稳后的位置就是应得的结果。

senses.title: Weight of a claim or complaint
senses.definition: the quality of being well founded, so that a claim deserves to be heard
senses.definitionCN: 有充分依据、因而值得被受理的性质
senses.example: She argued the justice of her complaint with figures the board could not ignore.
senses.exampleCN: 她用董事会无法忽视的数据论证自己的申诉是站得住脚的。
senses.why: If a claim is laid on the pan and the arm does not fly up, the claim has weight; the justice of a claim is exactly that weight on the moral scale.
senses.whyCN: 把一项主张放上托盘，若梁臂不翘起，这主张就有分量；一项主张的正当性，正是它在道德天平上的重量。

senses.title: Treating something by its true measure
senses.titleCN: 按事物本来分量对待它
senses.definition: to represent or handle something in a way equal to its real worth
senses.definitionCN: 以与某物真实价值相称的方式来呈现或处理它
senses.example: A single photograph hardly does justice to the width of the valley.
senses.exampleCN: 一张照片几乎无法展现这道山谷的辽阔。
senses.why: The scale can be held up to a thing rather than to a person: to measure it truly is to give it neither less nor more than its due.
senses.whyCN: 天平也可以对着物件而不是对着人来举：真实地量它，就是不多不少地给出它应得的分量。

senses.title: Doing oneself justice
senses.titleCN: 发挥出自己应有的水平
senses.definition: to act or perform up to one's real ability
senses.definitionCN: 以自己真正的能力去行动或表现
senses.example: On her last attempt she finally did herself justice.
senses.exampleCN: 在最后一次尝试中，她终于发挥出了应有的水平。
senses.why: The beam turns inward: the weigher and the weight are now the same person, and fairness means not underrating oneself.
senses.whyCN: 秤梁转向内侧：称量与砝码成了同一个人，此时的公正就是不高估、也不低估自己。

intro.en: Justice descends from Latin iustitia, the abstract noun of iustus 'just', which rests on ius 'right, law'. It reached English through Old French, and the same root ius also produced judge, judicial and jury by a second route.
intro.cn: justice 出自拉丁 iustitia，是 iustus「公正的」的抽象名词，而 iustus 又立在 ius「法权、法律」之上；它经古法语进入英语。同一词根还经另一条路生出 judge、judicial 与 jury。

items.en: Ius, genitive iuris, meant 'right, law, legal power'; it is the single root behind the whole family of legal words.
items.cn: ius 的属格是 iuris，意为「法权、法律、合法权力」，是整个法律词族唯一的根。

items.en: Iustus 'upright, lawful, just' was the adjective of ius, naming a person or act that stayed within the law.
items.cn: iustus 意为「正直的、合乎法权的、公正的」，是 ius 的形容词，指守在法律之内的人或行为。

items.en: Iustitia 'justice, righteousness' added the abstract suffix to iustus and named the quality itself rather than the person who had it.
items.cn: iustitia 意为「公正、正义」，给 iustus 加上表性质的后缀，指这种性质本身，而不是具备它的人。

items.en: Iudex joined ius with dicere 'to say', literally 'one who declares the law', while iurare 'to swear' produced the oath-bound jury; both belong to the same root.
items.cn: iudex 把 ius 与 dicere「说」合在一起，字面是「宣示法权的人」；iurare「宣誓」则生出以誓约约束的陪审团；两者都属同一词根。

items.en: Old French carried iustitia forward as justise, and medieval English borrowed it in that shape; the exact first date of the borrowing is uncertain.
items.cn: 古法语把 iustitia 传成 justise，中世纪的英语沿用了这个形态借入；借入的确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: English used justice by about 1300 for the moral and legal quality, and only later extended it to the officer who administers it.
items.cn: 英语大约在 1300 年用 justice 指道德与法律上的性质，后来才扩展到执行这种性质的官员身上。

note.en: The first group is the Latin ius family in other shapes; the second group offers near alternatives, and one of them comes from a completely different root.
note.cn: 第一组是拉丁 ius 词族的其他形态；第二组是近义替代，其中有一个词的源流与本词完全不同。

entries.definition: Upright or fair; it is the bare adjective of ius and carries the quality without the abstract noun ending.
entries.definitionCN: 正直的、公正的；它是 ius 一脉的形容词，带着这种性质而不带抽象名词词尾。

entries.definition: To show that something is right or reasonable; the family root is present but the action is proving, not weighing.
entries.definitionCN: 证明某事正当或合理；词族之根仍在，但动作是证明，而不是称量。

entries.definition: A body of sworn persons who decide a case; it comes from the oath, not from the abstract quality, yet shares the same root.
entries.definitionCN: 由宣誓者组成、裁断案件的团体；它出自「宣誓」而非抽象性质，但同属一个词根。

entries.definition: To harm a person or thing; it descends from Latin injuria 'wrong', built on in- plus ius, and has drifted from injustice to physical harm.
entries.definitionCN: 伤害人或物；出自拉丁 injuria「不义」，由否定前缀加 ius 构成，语义已从「不公」滑向「身体伤害」。

entries.tag: close in meaning, unrelated in origin
entries.definition: Even-handedness; it overlaps with justice but comes from Old English fæger 'beautiful', so the two are merely close in meaning and unrelated in origin.
entries.definitionCN: 不偏不倚；它与公正意思相近，却出自古英语 fæger「美好的」，两者只是意思相近，源流并不相干。

entries.definition: Fairness that looks past strict rules to the merits of a case, from Latin aequitas 'evenness', not from ius.
entries.definitionCN: 不拘泥于条文、看重案件实情的公平，出自拉丁 aequitas「平坦、均等」，并非出自 ius。

entries.definition: The state of favouring no side; it describes the posture of the weigher rather than the result of the weighing.
entries.definitionCN: 不偏向任何一方的状态；它描述称量者的姿态，而不是称量的结果。

entries.definition: Conformity to a moral or religious law; it stresses personal virtue where justice stresses what is owed between parties.
entries.definitionCN: 合乎道德或宗教律法；它强调个人德性，而公正强调各方之间应得的关系。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real root ius, the real derived words and the real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的词根 ius、真实的派生词与真实的固定搭配。

normal.en: Latin ius means 'right, law', and every member of this family grows from that one syllable.
normal.cn: 拉丁 ius 意为「法权、法律」，这个词族的每个成员都从这一个音节长出来。

normal.en: Iudex joins ius with dicere 'to say', so a judge is literally the one who declares the law.
normal.cn: iudex 把 ius 与 dicere「说」合起来，所以法官字面上就是宣示法权的人。

normal.en: Iurare means 'to swear', which is why a jury is a body of people bound by an oath before they weigh anything.
normal.cn: iurare 意为「宣誓」，所以陪审团是一群在称量之前先被誓约约束的人。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the main senses: do justice to, bring to justice, the justice system.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出主要义项：对……作出相称的呈现、将……绳之以法、司法制度。

normal.en: The title travels too: a member of a supreme court is addressed as a justice, not as a judge.
normal.cn: 头衔也会移动：最高法院的成员被称作法官头衔的这一形式，而不是普通法官那个词。

abstract.en: Picture a brass balance on a bench, the arm dead level, both pans holding different things that still weigh the same.
abstract.cn: 想象法台上的一架黄铜天平，梁臂纹丝不动，两只托盘装着不同的东西，却恰好等重。

abstract.en: Picture two bowls filled from one and the same measuring cup, so neither side can claim a larger scoop.
abstract.cn: 想象两只碗都用同一只量杯舀满，谁也无法声称自己那一勺更大。

abstract.en: Picture a courtroom where the same chair, the same table and the same rule are given to each side in turn.
abstract.cn: 想象一间法庭，同样的椅子、同样的桌子和同样的规则，轮流给到每一方。

examples.en: The ruling was praised as an act of justice rather than of charity.
examples.cn: 这项裁决被称赞为公正之举，而不是施舍。

examples.en: Local people still wait for justice three decades after the fire.
examples.cn: 大火过去三十年，当地居民仍在等待正义得到伸张。

examples.en: No translation can do justice to the terseness of the original.
examples.cn: 任何译文都无法充分呈现原文的简练。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「贾斯蒂斯」——听成「加事提司」：遇事先「加」一杆秤，事事「提」到秤上，斯斯文文称一称，两边一样重才算数 → 公正、正义、司法

root: 拉丁 ius「法权、权利」→ iustus「合乎法权的、正直的」→ iustitia「公正」→ 古法语 justise → 英语 justice；同族有 just、judge、judicial、jury、injure（出自 injuria「不义」）。

sensesIntro.en: All eight senses grow from one act: a beam held level while two different loads are compared. The level reading becomes fair treatment, then a moral principle, then a courtroom with clerks and rules, then the officer who keeps it level, then the deserved outcome. Finally the scale is turned on a claim, on an object and on oneself.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都从一个动作长出来：秤梁在两份不同的重量之间保持水平。这个水平读数依次成为公平对待、道德原则、配有书记员与规则的法庭、掌秤的官员，以及应得的结果；最后天平被转向一项主张、一件物品，乃至自己。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a brass balance whose beam rests level because one measure governs both pans.
core.cn: 核心意象：一架黄铜天平，因为同一把尺子管住两只托盘，梁臂才停在水平线上。

branches.en: EVEN MEASURE: the same rule laid on every party, whatever their rank.
branches.cn: 同一把尺：同一套规则落到每一方身上，不论其地位高低。

branches.en: MORAL PRINCIPLE: the level reading read as a law of the world, not a tool of one court.
branches.cn: 道德原则：把水平读数读成世间的法则，而不只是一间法庭的工具。

branches.en: INSTITUTIONS AND KEEPERS: the balance housed in courts, and the officer named after it.
branches.cn: 制度与掌秤者：天平被安进法院，掌秤的官员则以它为头衔。

branches.en: SETTLEMENT: the pans filled, the beam tipped, the outcome paid out as due.
branches.cn: 结算：托盘装满、梁臂倾斜，结果按应得之份付清。

branches.en: THE SCALE TURNED OUTWARD AND INWARD: a claim weighed, an object measured truly, and a person judging her own worth.
branches.cn: 天平的外转与内转：称一项主张、真实地量一件物品，以及一个人衡量自己的分量。

intro.en: Justice is built from a Latin root, an abstract suffix and a later French reshaping; the same root appears in the judge and jury line.
intro.cn: justice 由一个拉丁词根、一个抽象名词后缀和后期的法语改写构成；同一词根还见于法官与陪审团那一条线。

latinIntro.en: Latin ius 'right, law' yields iustus, iustitia, iudex, iudicium and iurare, and from these English drew justice, just, judicial, judge and jury.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 ius「法权、法律」衍生出 iustus、iustitia、iudex、iudicium 与 iurare，英语由此取得 justice、just、judicial、judge 与 jury。

items.example: Ius is the seed of the whole legal family.
items.exampleCN: 法权一词是整个法律词族的种子。

items.meaning: the state or quality of being
items.meaningCN: 表状态或性质的名词后缀
items.example: Iustitia names the quality of being iustus.
items.exampleCN: iustitia 指「合乎法权」这一性质。

items.example: The Latin noun passed through French into English.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁名词经法语进入了英语。

items.meaningCN: 正直的；合乎法权的；公正的
items.example: Iustus describes the person who stays within the law.
items.exampleCN: iustus 描述那个守在法律之内的人。

items.example: Iudex is the source of the English judge.
items.exampleCN: iudex 是英语 judge 的来源。

items.example: Iudicium names the act and result of judging.
items.exampleCN: iudicium 指裁断这一动作及其结果。

items.example: Jurors were sworn before they weighed the case.
items.exampleCN: 陪审员在裁断案件之前先要宣誓。

items.meaning: the quality of giving each its due
items.meaningCN: 给每一方应得之份的性质
items.example: The magistrate rested the ruling on justice.
items.exampleCN: 治安法官让裁决立在公正之上。

items.example: The decision was just and plainly explained.
items.exampleCN: 这个决定是公正的，也解释得明白。

items.example: Judicial review came under public scrutiny.
items.exampleCN: 司法审查受到了公众的审视。

items.meaningCN: 宣誓后参与裁断的团体
items.example: The jury returned after two hours.
items.exampleCN: 陪审团两小时后回来了。

latinEntries.meaning: judge, one who declares the law

definition_zh: 不公正；不公平；不义之举；冤屈；制度性的不公
definition_en: the absence of even-handedness, and any act or arrangement that gives one party less than its due
core_image: 村口的木秤被人偷偷在一端灌了铅，秤砣还没挪动，低下去的那一头就已经判定了输赢
scene: 集市上有人发现那杆秤的一头被灌了铅，买粮的农妇还没开口，围观的人已经替她不平。The crowd protested against the injustice of a scale that had been weighted before anyone weighed.
sceneCN: 这里指「称量被暗中做了手脚」的不公，对应第 1 个义项：本该用同一把尺子，却有人事先偏了心；句意为众人抗议一杆事先被加重过的秤所造成的不公。画面要点：被灌铅的木秤、围拢的集市人群。

pos.zh: 不公正；不公平（不可数，指性质）
不义之举；冤屈（可数，指一桩具体的事）

forms.label: 不可数名词（不公的性质）

derivatives.zh: 去掉名词后缀，换形容词词尾（源自拉丁语 iustus）→ 由「不公之事」转为「不公正的」
unjust 加副词后缀（古英语中表方式）→ 由「不公正的」转为「以不公的方式」
加复数后缀 → 由「一桩不义之举」转为「多桩不义之举」
去掉否定前缀（拉丁语中表否定）→ 由「不公」反转为「公正」

senses.title: Absence of even-handedness
senses.definition: the failure to apply one and the same rule to all parties concerned
senses.definitionCN: 未能对相关各方适用同一套规则
senses.example: The parents complained of injustice when only one child was punished.
senses.exampleCN: 只有一个孩子受到惩罚，父母便抱怨这不公平。
senses.why: The core image is a beam secretly loaded at one end: before any weighing begins the measure already favours a side, and that prior tilt is the first sense.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是一根被人在一端偷偷加重的秤梁：还没开始称，尺子就已经偏向一边；这个事先的倾斜就是第一个义项。

senses.title: A single unjust deed
senses.definition: one act that takes from someone what is owed to them
senses.definitionCN: 夺走某人应得之物的某一个行为
senses.example: The seizure of the family's land was an injustice no court would defend.
senses.exampleCN: 没收这家人土地是一桩没有哪家法院愿意为之辩护的不义之举。
senses.why: A tilted beam produces a reading; written into an act, that reading becomes a deed with a victim, and the abstract failure hardens into something countable.
senses.whyCN: 倾斜的秤梁给出一个读数；把它写成一个行为，这个读数就成了带有受害者的举动，抽象的性质凝结为可数的一件事。

senses.title: Wrongful handling by courts or officials
senses.titleCN: 法院或官员的错误处置
senses.definition: the mishandling of a case, especially a conviction or ruling that the person does not deserve
senses.definitionCN: 对案件的不当处置，尤指当事人不应得的定罪或裁决
senses.example: The inquiry found injustice in the way the confession had been obtained.
senses.exampleCN: 调查认定，取得那份口供的方式存在不公。
senses.why: Because the balance is most visible in a courtroom, its crooked version is most often charged against courts: the institution meant to hold it level is accused of holding it wrong.
senses.whyCN: 天平在法庭里最显眼，所以它歪掉的样子最常被算在法院头上：本该把秤端平的机关，被指为把秤端歪了。

senses.title: Unfairness built into the rules
senses.titleCN: 写进规则里的结构性不公
senses.definition: unfairness built into the rules of a society, market or institution, so that some groups are always short-changed
senses.definitionCN: 社会、市场或机构规则中固有的不公，使某些群体总是吃亏
senses.example: Campaigners described the tax as a quiet injustice written into the code.
senses.exampleCN: 活动人士把这项税称为悄悄写进法规的一处不公。
senses.why: One loaded pan can be a mistake; the same load placed in every scale of a country becomes a structure, and the word moves from an event to the order of things.
senses.whyCN: 一只托盘被加重可以是失误；把同样的加重放进一国的每一杆秤，就成了结构，这个词也从一件事移到事物的秩序上。

senses.title: A wrong a person has suffered
senses.definition: the grievance or injury that a person carries after being treated unfairly
senses.definitionCN: 一个人受到不公对待之后背负的委屈或伤害
senses.example: She never spoke of the injustice she had suffered at the factory.
senses.exampleCN: 她从不谈起自己在厂里受过的冤屈。
senses.why: Every tilted reading leaves a weight in the lighter pan; that residue, felt by the person, is the wrong carried rather than the act that caused it.
senses.whyCN: 每一次倾斜的称量都在较轻的那只托盘里留下重量；这份被当事人感到的残余，是背在身上的冤屈，而不是造成它的那个行为。

senses.title: An unfair verdict on a person
senses.definition: an unjust judgement of someone's character, work or worth
senses.definitionCN: 对某人的品性、工作或价值所作的不公正评判
senses.example: To call him lazy would do him an injustice.
senses.exampleCN: 说他懒，那对他就太不公平了。
senses.why: The scale can be turned on a reputation instead of a purse: weighing a person by false evidence is the same crooked operation in miniature.
senses.whyCN: 天平可以对着名声而不是对着钱袋：用不实的证据去称一个人，是同一套歪掉的把戏，只是缩小了规模。

senses.title: An unreasonable burden laid on one side
senses.titleCN: 单方面压下的不合理负担
senses.definition: a demand or condition that places more on one party than fairness allows
senses.definitionCN: 把超出公平限度之多的东西压到某一方头上的要求或条件
senses.example: The new levy placed an injustice on small shops that could least afford it.
senses.exampleCN: 新征的费用把一重不合理的负担压在最无力承担的小店铺身上。
senses.why: If the load is put on only one pan before weighing starts, the demand is already decided; the word then names the pre-loaded burden rather than the deed that follows.
senses.whyCN: 如果在称量开始前就把重量只压在一只托盘上，要求其实已经定了；此时这个词指那份额外压上的负担，而不是随后的行为。

senses.title: The unfairness of chance
senses.definition: the unjust character of fate, fortune or natural events, which distribute good and ill without regard to merit
senses.definitionCN: 命运、运气或自然事件的不义性质：它们不分功过地分发好坏
senses.example: They spoke of the injustice of a storm that spared the warehouse and ruined the homes.
senses.exampleCN: 他们说起那场风暴的不公：它放过了仓库，却毁掉了住宅。
senses.why: The beam is now held by no visible hand; when no one can be blamed, the word still names the tilt, and injustice becomes the shape of chance itself.
senses.whyCN: 此时秤梁没有看得见的手在握；当无人可以归咎时，这个词仍指那道倾斜，不公于是成了运气本身的形状。

intro.en: Injustice is the negative of justice: Latin in- 'not' was added to iustitia, and Latin already had injustitia and injustus. Old French carried the form on, and English borrowed it with the negative prefix intact.
intro.cn: injustice 是 justice 的否定形式：拉丁否定前缀加在 iustitia 之上，而拉丁本身已有 injustitia 与 injustus。古法语把这个形式传下去，英语带着完整否定前缀借入。

items.en: Latin in- marked negation, and its shape could change before certain consonants; on a noun of quality it produced the opposite quality.
items.cn: 拉丁语中表否定的前缀，在部分辅音前形态会有变化；加在表性质的名词上，就造出相反的性质。

items.en: Iustitia 'justice' was the abstract noun of iustus 'just', itself built on ius 'right, law'.
items.cn: iustitia「公正」是 iustus「公正的」的抽象名词，而 iustus 又立在 ius「法权、法律」之上。

items.en: Latin formed iniustitia 'injustice' directly, and the adjective iniustus 'unjust' already existed beside it.
items.cn: 拉丁直接造出了 iniustitia「不公」，与之并存的形容词 iniustus「不公正的」也已经存在。

items.en: Old French used injustice for both the quality and a wrong done; the exact century of the borrowing into English is uncertain.
items.cn: 古法语用 injustice 兼指这种性质与一桩不义之事；借入英语的确切世纪不确定。

items.en: English records the word early but the precise first date is uncertain; it named the quality first and a countable act later.
items.cn: 英语早期文献已见该词，但确切首见年代不确定；它先指性质，后指可数的一桩事。

note.en: The first group keeps the ius root in other shapes; the second group gives near alternatives, one of which comes from a different root and must not be confused with this family.
note.cn: 第一组以别的形态保留 ius 词根；第二组是近义替代，其中一个出自另一条词根，不能与这一族混为一谈。

entries.definition: Not fair or lawful; it is the negative of just and states the quality where injustice states the thing.
entries.definitionCN: 不公的、不合法的；它是否定形式的「公正的」，说的是性质，而不公说的是事情本身。

entries.definition: To harm a person physically; it comes from Latin injuria 'wrong' but has narrowed from injustice to bodily damage.
entries.definitionCN: 在身体上伤害人；出自拉丁 injuria「不义」，但语义已从「不公」收窄为「身体损伤」。

entries.definition: Harmful or wrongful; the same family as injure and justice, now used chiefly of damage.
entries.definitionCN: 有害的、造成侵害的；与 injure、justice 同族，现在主要用于损害之义。

entries.definition: Wicked or grossly unfair; it shares the negative prefix but comes from Latin iniquus 'unequal', so it only looks related and is not the same root.
entries.definitionCN: 邪恶的、极不公的；它只共享否定前缀，出自拉丁 iniquus「不均等」，所以只是形近，并非同源。

entries.definition: The plain everyday name for the same failure; it comes from Old English fæger and is unrelated to the Latin root of injustice.
entries.definitionCN: 同一种缺失最平实的说法；它出自古英语 fæger，与 injustice 的拉丁词根没有源流关系。

entries.definition: An act or state that violates what is right; it does not require a rule or a comparison of parties.
entries.definitionCN: 违反正当之事的举动或状态；它不要求有规则，也不要求比较双方。

entries.definition: Lack of evenness in treatment, from Latin aequus 'even'; the root is different from ius, though the effect described is close.
entries.definitionCN: 待遇上的不均等，出自拉丁 aequus「平坦、均等」；词根与 ius 不同，尽管所描述的效果相近。

entries.definition: Unfairness held in place by power, so that the weaker side cannot appeal; it adds force to the idea of injustice.
entries.definitionCN: 以权力维持的不公，使较弱一方无从申诉；它在「不公」之上加了强制这一层。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the negative prefix, the real family words and the real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的否定前缀、真实的同族词与真实的固定搭配。

normal.en: In- is the plain Latin 'not', so injustice is justice with that switch thrown.
normal.cn: 这个否定前缀就是拉丁语里平实的「不」，所以 injustice 是把 justice 的那个开关扳到否定。

normal.en: Unjust and unjustly carry the same switch into the adjective and the adverb.
normal.cn: unjust 与 unjustly 把同一个否定开关带进了形容词和副词。

normal.en: The noun turns countable when it names one deed: an injustice, two injustices.
normal.cn: 当它指一桩具体的事，这个名词就可数：一桩不义之举、两桩不义之举。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: do someone an injustice, redress an injustice, social injustice.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：冤枉某人、纠正一桩不公、社会不公。

normal.en: The root line is shared with justice: ius 'right', iustus 'just', iustitia 'justice'.
normal.cn: 词根线与 justice 共享：ius「法权」、iustus「公正的」、iustitia「公正」。

abstract.en: Picture one pan of a balance with a lump of lead hidden under it, the beam already down before the goods arrive.
abstract.cn: 想象天平的一只托盘底下藏着一块铅，货物还没放上去，秤梁已经先沉了下去。

abstract.en: Picture a ruler with the first inch filed away, so that every honest measurement comes out short.
abstract.cn: 想象一把尺子的第一寸被锉掉了，于是每一次老实的测量都偏短。

abstract.en: Picture a race where one lane's starting line is chalked several steps behind the others.
abstract.cn: 想象一场赛跑，其中一条跑道的起跑线被画在别人后面好几步的地方。

examples.en: The report catalogued a long history of injustice against the fishing villages.
examples.cn: 报告记录了这些渔村长期遭受不公的历史。

examples.en: He considered it an injustice that the oldest workers were the first to be dismissed.
examples.cn: 他认为最先被辞退的是最年长的工人，这实在不公。

examples.en: No apology can undo the injustice of those lost years.
examples.cn: 任何道歉都无法抹去那些失去的年岁所造成的不公。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因贾斯蒂斯」——把开头记成「因为」：因为有人偷偷往秤里加了分量，斯文的天平就歪了 → 不公、不义、冤枉

root: 表否定的拉丁前缀 + justice（拉丁 iustitia，出自 ius「法权」）→ 不公；拉丁已有 iniustitia，经古法语 injustice 进入英语，与 justice 同一词根而意义相反。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all start from one crooked reading: a beam loaded before the weighing. That tilt becomes unfair treatment, then a countable deed, then courts that handle a case wrongly, then rules that load every scale the same way. From there it moves to the wound a person carries, a false verdict on a reputation, a burden laid on one side, and finally a tilt with no hand behind it.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都从同一个歪掉的读数开始：秤在称量之前就被加重。这道倾斜成为不公平的对待，继而成为一桩可数的事、把案子办错的法院、以同样方式给每一杆秤加重的规则；由此再移到当事人背负的伤口、对名声的错判、单方压下的负担，最后是一道找不到推手可归的倾斜。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a beam already loaded at one end, so the result is settled before the weighing.
core.cn: 核心意象：秤梁的一端早已被加重，结果在称量之前就定了。

branches.en: THE TILT ITSELF: one rule fails to reach all parties equally.
branches.cn: 倾斜本身：同一套规则没能同等落到每一方身上。

branches.en: THE DEED: the tilt written into one act that takes what was owed.
branches.cn: 一桩事：把倾斜写进一个行为，夺走本该属于他人的东西。

branches.en: COURTS AND WOUNDS: the crooked reading charged against a court, and the weight it leaves in the victim's pan.
branches.cn: 法院与伤口：把歪掉的读数算在法院头上，以及它留在受害者托盘里的那份重量。

branches.en: STRUCTURE: the same hidden load placed in every scale of a society.
branches.cn: 结构：把同样的暗载放进一个社会的每一杆秤。

branches.en: JUDGEMENT, BURDEN AND FATE: a person weighed falsely, a load pushed onto one side, and a tilt with no hand behind it.
branches.cn: 评判、负担与命运：被不实称量的人、被推到一方头上的重量，以及找不到推手的倾斜。

intro.en: Injustice is a negated Latin abstract noun; the prefix and the noun each keep their own meaning, and the pair travelled together through French.
intro.cn: injustice 是一个被否定的拉丁抽象名词；前缀与名词各自保留自己的意思，二者一起经法语传来。

latinIntro.en: Latin in- 'not' joins iustitia 'justice' to give injustitia; the same negative also produced injustus 'unjust', the adjective that English keeps as unjust.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语表「不」的否定前缀与 iustitia「公正」合起来得到 injustitia；同一个否定成分还造出 injustus「不公正的」，英语把它保留为 unjust。

items.example: In- turns a quality into its absence.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把一种性质变成它的缺失。

items.example: Iustitia is the noun that in- negates.
items.exampleCN: iustitia 正是那个被否定的名词。

items.example: Latin injustitia is the direct model of the English word.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁 injustitia 是英语这个词的直接范本。

items.example: Injustus stands beside injustitia in Latin.
items.exampleCN: 在拉丁语里，injustus 与 injustitia 并立。

items.meaning: the quality of giving each its due
items.meaningCN: 给每一方应得之份的性质
items.example: Without the negative prefix the word means justice.
items.exampleCN: 去掉否定前缀，这个词就是「公正」。

items.example: The crowd protested against the injustice of the scale.
items.exampleCN: 众人抗议那杆秤带来的不公。

items.example: The rules were unjust to the smallest traders.
items.exampleCN: 这些规则对最小的商户并不公平。

items.example: The book lists the injustices of that decade.
items.exampleCN: 这本书列举了那个年代的种种不义之举。

items.example: He was unjustly blamed for the failure.
items.exampleCN: 那次失败他被不公平地归咎了。

definition_zh: 公平；公正；公道；白皙；秀美；（抄本的）清晰工整
definition_en: the quality of being even-handed and rule-bound, and, in older use, of being pleasing to look at or free from blemish
core_image: 跑道上用白粉弹出一条笔直的起跑线，两条赛道宽窄一样，边沿干净齐整，看着就悦目
scene: 田径场的起跑线用白粉弹得笔直，两条跑道宽窄一样，边沿没有一处毛糙。The referee walked the track to confirm the fairness of the lanes before the final.
sceneCN: 这里指「起跑条件对双方一样」的公平，对应第 1 个义项：规则同等适用于每一方，不许谁先占便宜；句意为裁判沿跑道查看各条赛道是否公平。画面要点：白粉起跑线、等宽的跑道、齐整的边沿。

pos.zh: 公平；公正；公道（不可数，指性质）
白皙；秀美（不可数，指外貌，属较旧的用法）
清晰工整（不可数，指抄本或字迹）

forms.label: 不可数名词（公平的性质）

derivatives.zh: 去掉名词后缀（古英语中表性质）→ 由「公平这一性质」转为「公平的、悦目的」
fair 加副词后缀（古英语中表方式）→ 由「公平的」转为「以公平的方式；相当地」
古英语中表否定的前缀加 fair → 由「公平的」转为「不公平的」
否定前缀加 fair 再加名词后缀 → 由「公平」转为「不公平的性质」
fair 与 minded 复合（表心性）→ 由「公平」转为「心地公正、不偏私的」

senses.title: Even-handedness between parties
senses.definition: the quality of applying the same rule to everyone concerned
senses.definitionCN: 对相关每一个人都适用同一套规则的性质
senses.example: The board promised fairness in the way the grants were awarded.
senses.exampleCN: 董事会承诺在发放资助时做到公平。
senses.why: The core image is a chalked line laid across a track: whatever the runners' strength, the line and the lane width are the same for each, and that sameness is the first sense.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是横在跑道上的一条白粉线：不论选手强弱，起跑线与跑道宽度对每个人都一样，这份「一样」就是第一个义项。

senses.title: Justness of a decision or rule
senses.titleCN: 决定或规则的公正合理
senses.definition: the quality of a ruling or rule that gives each side what is reasonably due
senses.definitionCN: 某项裁决或规则给每一方合理应得之份的性质
senses.example: Tenants questioned the fairness of a rent rise announced without warning.
senses.exampleCN: 房客们质疑这次毫无预告就宣布的涨租是否公道。
senses.why: A starting line settles only where the race begins; when the same even measure is applied to a verdict, it becomes the justness of the decision itself.
senses.whyCN: 起跑线只决定比赛从何处开始；当同一把均等的尺子被用到裁决上，它就变成了决定本身的公正。

senses.title: Fair play under the rules
senses.definition: honest observance of the rules, especially in sport or competition
senses.definitionCN: 尤其指体育或竞赛中诚实遵守规则
senses.example: The coach praised the visiting team for its fairness under pressure.
senses.exampleCN: 教练称赞客队在压力之下仍然守规矩。
senses.why: From sameness of conditions comes a second demand: that no one secretly break the rule, so fairness grows from a measured line into a code of conduct.
senses.whyCN: 条件相同又引出第二项要求：谁都不许暗中破例；于是公平从一条量好的线长成一套行为准则。

senses.title: Fairness of procedure
senses.definition: the quality of a hearing or process that gives each party a real chance to be heard
senses.definitionCN: 听证或程序给每一方真正陈述机会的性质
senses.example: Lawyers challenged the fairness of a tribunal held behind closed doors.
senses.exampleCN: 律师们质疑一场闭门进行的审理是否公正。
senses.why: The line must be visible to be trusted: procedure is fairness made public, step by step, so that no advantage is taken behind a door.
senses.whyCN: 线要看得见才可信：程序就是把公平公开地一步步做出来，使谁也不能在门后占到便宜。

senses.title: Lightness of skin or hair
senses.definition: the quality of having pale skin or fair hair
senses.definitionCN: 皮肤白皙或头发颜色浅的性质
senses.example: Her fairness meant that the sun burned her before anyone else in the group.
senses.exampleCN: 她肤色浅，太阳总是先晒到她，比别人都早。
senses.why: Old English fæger first meant 'pleasing to look at'; a pale, clean brightness was one kind of pleasingness, so the word came to name light colouring.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 fæger 最初意为「看上去悦目」；一种干净而浅淡的明亮正是悦目的一类，于是这个词也用来指浅色的外貌。

senses.title: Beauty, loveliness
senses.definition: the quality of being beautiful or attractive, an older and literary sense
senses.definitionCN: 美丽动人的性质，属较旧且偏文学的义项
senses.example: Poets of the period praised the fairness of the summer fields.
senses.exampleCN: 那个时代的诗人赞美夏日田野的秀美。
senses.why: This is the oldest layer: fæger was simply 'beautiful, pleasant', and the noun first named beauty long before it named justice.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的一层：fæger 本就是「美好的、悦人的」，这个名词先指美，很久以后才指公正。

senses.title: Clearness of a written copy
senses.definition: the neatness and legibility of a written or printed copy
senses.definitionCN: 书写或印刷抄本的整洁与易读
senses.example: The clerk checked the fairness of the final copy before it was sealed.
senses.exampleCN: 书吏在封存之前检查了最终抄本是否清晰工整。
senses.why: Something free from spots and blots was called fair; transferred to writing, the same freedom from blemish became the clean, readable page.
senses.whyCN: 没有污点与墨渍的东西被称作「洁净悦目」；转到书写上，同一份「无瑕」就成了干净易读的页面。

senses.title: Reasonableness of a price or amount
senses.definition: the quality of an amount that is neither excessive nor stingy
senses.definitionCN: 数额既不过高也不刻薄的性质
senses.example: Customers argued about the fairness of the new delivery charge.
senses.exampleCN: 顾客们议论这项新收的配送费是否公道。
senses.why: The 'fitting' sense of fæger survives in measure: an amount is fair when it fits the thing it pays for, neither over nor under.
senses.whyCN: fæger 里「合宜」的那层意思在度量中留存下来：一个数额与它所偿付的东西相称，不多不少，就是公道。

intro.en: Fairness is Germanic, not Latin: Old English fæger 'beautiful, pleasant' plus the noun suffix -nes(s). It is not related to justice, which descends from Latin ius, even though the two words overlap in meaning today.
intro.cn: fairness 属日耳曼语一脉，与拉丁语无关：古英语 fæger「美好的、悦人的」加上古英语名词后缀构成。它与出自拉丁 ius 的 justice 并无源流关系，尽管今天两词意思重叠。

items.en: Fæger meant 'beautiful, pleasant, attractive' and could describe a person, a day or a field; it is the direct ancestor of modern fair.
items.cn: fæger 意为「美好的、悦人的、动人的」，可以形容人、天气或田野；它是现代 fair 的直接祖先。

items.en: The reconstructed form *fagraz 'suitable, fitting' stands behind fæger; Gothic fagrs 'fitting' and Old Norse fagr 'fair' point to the same source.
items.cn: 重构形式 *fagraz「合宜的、合适的」是 fæger 的前身；哥特语 fagrs「合适的」与古诺斯语 fagr「美好的」指向同一来源。

items.en: The suffix -nes(s) turned adjectives into nouns of quality, and fægernes 'beauty, fairness' is recorded in Old English.
items.cn: 古英语名词后缀把形容词变成表性质的名词，古英语中已记录有 fægernes「美、悦目」。

items.en: Middle English fairnes(se) joined fair with -nesse and still meant beauty as well as a pleasing appearance.
items.cn: 中古英语 fairnes(se) 把 fair 与古英语名词后缀合起来，仍兼指美与悦目的外貌。

items.en: The sense of impartiality is later and its exact first date is uncertain; in modern usage even-handedness dominates, while beauty and light colour remain secondary.
items.cn: 「不偏不倚」这一义出现较晚，确切首见年代不确定；现代用法中以公平为主，美与浅色退为次要义。

note.en: The first group shares spelling or sound with fair but not always the root; the second group gives near alternatives, and justice belongs to a Latin family that fairness never joined.
note.cn: 第一组与 fair 在拼写或读音上相近，但未必同根；第二组是近义替代，其中 justice 属于一个 fairness 从未加入的拉丁词族。

entries.definition: Even-handed, or pleasing and pale; it is the adjective from which fairness is formed.
entries.definitionCN: 公平的，或悦目而浅色的；它是构成 fairness 的那个形容词。

entries.definition: In a fair manner, or to a moderate degree; it adds the manner suffix to the same adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 以公平的方式，或达到相当的程度；它给同一个形容词加上表方式的后缀。

entries.definition: A small supernatural being; it resembles fair in spelling but comes through Old French from Latin fata 'fate', so it only looks similar and is not the same root.
entries.definitionCN: 一种小型的超自然生灵；拼写近似 fair，却经古法语出自拉丁 fata「命运」，所以只是形近，并非同源。

entries.definition: The money paid for a journey, or to get on; it sounds like fair but comes from Old English faran 'to travel', so it only looks similar and is not the same root.
entries.definitionCN: 旅费，或进展得如何；读音近似 fair，却出自古英语 faran「行走」，所以只是形近，并非同源。

entries.tag: close in meaning, unrelated in origin
entries.definition: The quality of giving each its due; it overlaps with fairness but descends from Latin ius, so the two are close in meaning and unrelated in origin.
entries.definitionCN: 给每一方应得之份的性质；它与公平意思相近，却出自拉丁 ius，所以两者意思相近而源流无关。

entries.definition: Fairness that weighs the merits rather than only the wording, from Latin aequitas 'evenness'.
entries.definitionCN: 看重实情而不只看字面的公平，出自拉丁 aequitas「均等」。

entries.definition: The state of favouring no party; it names the neutral stance rather than the whole quality of fair dealing.
entries.definitionCN: 不偏向任何一方的状态；它指中立的姿态，而不是公平对待的全部品质。

entries.definition: The quality of being just, from the ius family; it means much the same as fairness but belongs to the other root line.
entries.definitionCN: 公正的性质，出自 ius 词族；意思与 fairness 相近，却属于另一条词根线。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the Old English adjective, the real suffix and the real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的古英语形容词、真实的后缀与真实的固定搭配。

normal.en: Fair comes from Old English fæger 'beautiful', so the whole family is Germanic, not Latin.
normal.cn: fair 出自古英语 fæger「美好的」，所以整个词族属日耳曼语，而非拉丁语。

normal.en: The suffix -ness turns the adjective into the quality: fair, fairness.
normal.cn: 名词后缀把形容词变成性质名词：fair 变成 fairness。

normal.en: Germanic cousins confirm the line: Gothic fagrs 'fitting' and Old Norse fagr 'fair'.
normal.cn: 日耳曼语族的亲属可以印证这条线：哥特语 fagrs「合适的」与古诺斯语 fagr「美好的」。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: in all fairness, fairness and equity, a sense of fairness.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：公平地说、公平与公正、公平感。

normal.en: Fair also means pale, so fair hair and fair skin show why fairness can name light colouring.
normal.cn: fair 还表示浅色，所以浅色头发与白皙皮肤说明了 fairness 为何能指浅淡的外貌。

abstract.en: Picture a white chalk line snapped straight across a track, equally far from both ends.
abstract.cn: 想象一条白粉线在跑道上弹得笔直，离两端的距离一样远。

abstract.en: Picture a linen sheet bleaching on the grass, spotless and evenly white, pleasant to look at.
abstract.cn: 想象一块亚麻布在草地上晒白，没有一处污渍，白得均匀，看着悦目。

abstract.en: Picture two identical bowls filled to the very same mark by one measuring cup.
abstract.cn: 想象两只一模一样的碗，用同一只量杯舀到同一条刻度。

examples.en: In all fairness, the decision was reached before the new evidence arrived.
examples.cn: 公平地说，这个决定在新证据到达之前就已作出。

examples.en: The union demanded fairness in the allocation of overtime.
examples.cn: 工会要求在加班分配上做到公平。

examples.en: The old manuscript was admired for the fairness of its script.
examples.cn: 那份古老的手稿因字迹清晰工整而受人称赞。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「费厄奈斯」——把同样的力气「费」在每个人身上，厄难同当，奈心平摊，谁也不多占一分 → 公平、公道、不偏不倚

root: 古英语 fæger「美好的、悦人的」（重构的原始日耳曼语 *fagraz「合宜的」）→ 加古英语名词后缀成 fægernes／fairness；与拉丁 ius 一脉的 justice 毫无源流关系。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses start from one Germanic idea: what is pleasing is also what fits. From 'fitting' come the same line for every runner, the justness of a rule, fair play and fair procedure. From 'pleasing to look at' come pale colouring and beauty; from 'free from blemish' come the clean copy and, by way of fit measure, the reasonable price.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都从一个日耳曼语观念出发：悦目之物也是合宜之物。由「合宜」生出给每个跑者同一条起跑线、规则的公正、公平竞赛与公正程序；由「看上去悦目」生出浅淡的肤色与秀美；由「没有瑕疵」生出清晰工整的抄本，再经由「分量合宜」生出公道的价钱。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a chalk line snapped straight across a track, with lanes of equal width on either side.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条弹得笔直的白粉起跑线横过跑道，两侧赛道宽窄相等。

branches.en: THE SAME LINE: identical conditions laid down for every party before anything begins.
branches.cn: 同一条线：在一切开始之前，给每一方定下完全相同的条件。

branches.en: DECISIONS AND PROCEDURE: the even measure applied to a ruling, and made visible step by step.
branches.cn: 决定与程序：把均等的尺子用到裁决上，并一步步公开做出来。

branches.en: THE CODE OF PLAY: no one may quietly step over the line once the race starts.
branches.cn: 竞赛准则：比赛一开始，谁都不许悄悄越过那条线。

branches.en: PLEASING APPEARANCE: pale, clean brightness, and beauty as the oldest layer of the word.
branches.cn: 悦目的外貌：干净而浅淡的明亮，以及作为这个词最古老一层的秀美。

branches.en: FREEDOM FROM BLEMISH AND FROM EXCESS: a clean, legible copy, and an amount that fits what it pays for.
branches.cn: 无瑕亦无过：干净易读的抄本，以及与所偿付之物相称的数额。

intro.en: Fairness is an Old English adjective turned into a noun by a native suffix; its parts are Germanic, and no Latin element entered its making.
intro.cn: fairness 是一个古英语形容词被本族后缀变成的名词；它的各组成部分都属日耳曼语，构词中没有拉丁成分参与。

latinIntro.en: There are no Latin entries for this word: its ancestry is Old English and Proto-Germanic, and Latin offered no cognate; the apparent Latin look of the ending is misleading.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁同族词：它的来历是古英语与原始日耳曼语，拉丁语并无对应的同族形式；词尾看上去像拉丁语，其实会造成误导。

items.example: Fæger could describe a field or a face.
items.exampleCN: 这个词可以形容田野，也可以形容面容。

items.example: The asterisk marks a reconstructed, unwritten form.
items.exampleCN: 星号表示这是一个重构而未见书写的形式。

items.structure: Old English suffix -nes(s), noun of quality
items.example: The suffix turned adjectives into abstract nouns.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把形容词变成抽象名词。

items.example: Old English already had this noun of quality.
items.exampleCN: 古英语里已经有这个表性质的名词。

items.example: A fair rule looks the same to both sides.
items.exampleCN: 一条公平的规则在双方眼里是同一个样子。

items.example: The referee confirmed the fairness of the lanes.
items.exampleCN: 裁判确认了各条赛道的公平。

items.example: The shares were divided fairly.
items.exampleCN: 各份被公平地分开了。

items.example: The charge was unfair to small buyers.
items.exampleCN: 这项收费对小买家并不公平。

items.example: They complained about the unfairness of the test.
items.exampleCN: 他们抱怨这场测试不公平。

items.meaningCN: 愿意不带偏见地判断的
items.example: A fair-minded reader will see both sides.
items.exampleCN: 心地公正的读者会看到双方的理由。
